VwRLIt6jgdM.zh: 【TED-Ed】玻璃為什麼是透明的？ ——馬克‧米歐多尼克（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Take a look out your window, put on your glasses if you wear them.
cues.en: Take a look out your window, put on your glasses if you wear them.
cues.zh: 朝窗外看看， 如果你有眼鏡，把它戴上 你可能也需要一副望遠鏡

cues.text: You might want to grab a pair of binoculars, too, or a magnifying lens.
cues.en: You might want to grab a pair of binoculars, too, or a magnifying lens.
cues.zh: 你可能也需要一副望遠鏡 或是放大鏡 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？

cues.text: Now, what do you see?
cues.en: Now, what do you see?
cues.zh: 或是放大鏡 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？

cues.text: Well, whatever it is, it's not the multiple layers of glass
cues.en: Well, whatever it is, it's not the multiple layers of glass
cues.zh: 那麼，現在你看到了什麼？ 不論是什麼 你眼前出現的

cues.text: right in front of you.
cues.en: right in front of you.
cues.zh: 你眼前出現的 總不會是一層層的玻璃

cues.text: But have you ever wondered how something so solid can be so invisible?
cues.en: But have you ever wondered how something so solid can be so invisible?
cues.zh: 總不會是一層層的玻璃 你曾否想過 這麼堅固的東西 怎麼可能如此剔透？ 要了解其中原因

cues.text: To understand that, we have to understand what glass actually is,
cues.en: To understand that, we have to understand what glass actually is,
cues.zh: 要了解其中原因 我們得先了解玻璃究竟是什麼 以及它是從哪裡來的

cues.text: and where it comes from.
cues.en: and where it comes from.
cues.zh: 我們得先了解玻璃究竟是什麼 以及它是從哪裡來的

cues.text: It all begins in the Earth's crust, where the two most common elements are
cues.en: It all begins in the Earth's crust, where the two most common elements are
cues.zh: 這一切都得從地殼開始說起 組成地殼最主要的兩種成分是

cues.text: silicon and oxygen.
cues.en: silicon and oxygen.
cues.zh: 矽和氧

cues.text: These react together to form silicon dioxide, whose molecules arrange themselves
cues.en: These react together to form silicon dioxide, whose molecules arrange themselves
cues.zh: 矽和氧 這兩種成分經由 化學變化後形成二氧化矽 當中的分子排列 組成規則的晶體 也就是我們所知的石英

cues.text: into a regular crystalline form known as quartz.
cues.en: into a regular crystalline form known as quartz.
cues.zh: 組成規則的晶體 也就是我們所知的石英 石英在砂子裡很常見

cues.text: Quartz is commonly found in sand, where it often makes up most of the grains
cues.en: Quartz is commonly found in sand, where it often makes up most of the grains
cues.zh: 石英在砂子裡很常見 它是常見組成砂粒

cues.text: and is the main ingredient in most type of glass.
cues.en: and is the main ingredient in most type of glass.
cues.zh: 它是常見組成砂粒 以及大部分玻璃種類的主要成分 當然，你或許已經注意到

cues.text: Of course, you probably noticed that glass isn't made of multiple tiny bits of quartz,
cues.en: Of course, you probably noticed that glass isn't made of multiple tiny bits of quartz,
cues.zh: 當然，你或許已經注意到 玻璃並不是由許多 細小的石英顆粒組成的

cues.text: and for good reason.
cues.en: and for good reason.
cues.zh: 玻璃並不是由許多 細小的石英顆粒組成的 這背後有其道理在

cues.text: For one thing, the edges of the rigidly formed grains and smaller defects within the crystal structure
cues.en: For one thing, the edges of the rigidly formed grains and smaller defects within the crystal structure
cues.zh: 首先，當光線照射到砂粒粗糙的邊緣 以及晶體結構中的微小瑕疵時 會向四面八方反射分散

cues.text: reflect and disperse light that hits them.
cues.en: reflect and disperse light that hits them.
cues.zh: 會向四面八方反射分散

cues.text: But when the quartz is heated high enough the extra energy makes the molecules vibrate
cues.en: But when the quartz is heated high enough the extra energy makes the molecules vibrate
cues.zh: 但若石英加熱到一定溫度時 多餘的能量促使石英分子振動

cues.text: until they break the bonds holding them together and become a flowing liquid,
cues.en: until they break the bonds holding them together and become a flowing liquid,
cues.zh: 多餘的能量促使石英分子振動 直到打斷分子之間的鍵結 而變成流動的液體

cues.text: the same way that ice melts into water.
cues.en: the same way that ice melts into water.
cues.zh: 就如同冰溶化成為水一般 但不同於水的是，液態的二氧化矽

cues.text: Unlike water, though, liquid silicon dioxide does not reform into a crystal solid when it cools.
cues.en: Unlike water, though, liquid silicon dioxide does not reform into a crystal solid when it cools.
cues.zh: 就如同冰溶化成為水一般 但不同於水的是，液態的二氧化矽 冷卻後不會變回固態的晶體

cues.text: Instead, as the molecules lose energy, they are less and less able
cues.en: Instead, as the molecules lose energy, they are less and less able
cues.zh: 冷卻後不會變回固態的晶體 反之，當二氧化矽分子的能量減弱 他們越來越不可能

cues.text: to move into an ordered position, and the result is what is called an amorphous solid.
cues.en: to move into an ordered position, and the result is what is called an amorphous solid.
cues.zh: 他們越來越不可能 回復到規律整齊的排列 結果形成所謂的非晶態固體 具有液體般混亂結構的固體

cues.text: A solid material with the chaotic structure of a liquid,
cues.en: A solid material with the chaotic structure of a liquid,
cues.zh: 具有液體般混亂結構的固體 其中的分子可自由移動 填充任何的間隙

cues.text: which allows the molecules to freely fill in any gaps.
cues.en: which allows the molecules to freely fill in any gaps.
cues.zh: 具有液體般混亂結構的固體 其中的分子可自由移動 填充任何的間隙

cues.text: This makes the surface of glass uniform on a microscopic level,
cues.en: This makes the surface of glass uniform on a microscopic level,
cues.zh: 這使玻璃表面 即使由微觀的角度看來 也是平整的 因此光線照射上去

cues.text: allowing light to strike it without being scattered in different directions.
cues.en: allowing light to strike it without being scattered in different directions.
cues.zh: 因此光線照射上去 也不會四處散射 但這仍然不能解釋

cues.text: But this still doesn't explain why light is able to pass through glass
cues.en: But this still doesn't explain why light is able to pass through glass
cues.zh: 但這仍然不能解釋 為何光線能夠穿透玻璃

cues.text: rather than being absorbed as with most solids.
cues.en: rather than being absorbed as with most solids.
cues.zh: 為何光線能夠穿透玻璃 而不是像其他固體一樣被吸收

cues.text: For that, we need to go all the way down to the subatomic level.
cues.en: For that, we need to go all the way down to the subatomic level.
cues.zh: 為此，我們得進入 原子內的世界來瞭解 你可能知道 一個原子的組成包含一個原子核

cues.text: You may know that an atom consists of a nucleus with electrons orbiting around it,
cues.en: You may know that an atom consists of a nucleus with electrons orbiting around it,
cues.zh: 你可能知道 一個原子的組成包含一個原子核 以及若干圍繞在周圍的電子

cues.text: but you may be surprised to know that it's mostly empty space.
cues.en: but you may be surprised to know that it's mostly empty space.
cues.zh: 以及若干圍繞在周圍的電子 但你可能會很驚訝地發現 原子裡大部分是空蕩蕩的 事實上，如果將原子 比喻成一個體育場這麼大

cues.text: In fact, if an atom were the size of a sports stadium, the nucleus would be like a single pea in the center,
cues.en: In fact, if an atom were the size of a sports stadium, the nucleus would be like a single pea in the center,
cues.zh: 事實上，如果將原子 比喻成一個體育場這麼大 原子核就像是一顆在場中央的豌豆 而電子便是

cues.text: while the electrons would be like grains of sand in the outer seats.
cues.en: while the electrons would be like grains of sand in the outer seats.
cues.zh: 而電子便是 在場外圍座位的砂粒

cues.text: That should leave plenty of space for light to pass through without hitting any of these particles.
cues.en: That should leave plenty of space for light to pass through without hitting any of these particles.
cues.zh: 在場外圍座位的砂粒 因此 光線有大量的空間能夠穿透 而不會撞擊到這些粒子

cues.text: So the real question is not why is glass transparent, but why aren't all materials transparent?
cues.en: So the real question is not why is glass transparent, but why aren't all materials transparent?
cues.zh: 所以真正的問題並不是 為什麼玻璃是透明的 而是為什麼其他的材料不是透明的？ 這個問題的答案

cues.text: The answer has to do with the different energy levels that electrons in an atom can have.
cues.en: The answer has to do with the different energy levels that electrons in an atom can have.
cues.zh: 這個問題的答案 與原子內的電子 具有不同程度的能量有關 你可以把它想成是體育場裡

cues.text: Think of these as different rows of seats in the stadium stands.
cues.en: Think of these as different rows of seats in the stadium stands.
cues.zh: 與原子內的電子 具有不同程度的能量有關 你可以把它想成是體育場裡 一排排的座位

cues.text: An electron is initially assigned to sit in a certain row, but it could jump to a better row,
cues.en: An electron is initially assigned to sit in a certain row, but it could jump to a better row,
cues.zh: 一開始，一顆電子 被指定坐在某一排 但若是它有足夠的能量

cues.text: if it only had the energy.
cues.en: if it only had the energy.
cues.zh: 但若是它有足夠的能量 就可以跳到比較好的座位

cues.text: As luck would have it, absorbing one of those light photons passing through the atom can provide
cues.en: As luck would have it, absorbing one of those light photons passing through the atom can provide
cues.zh: 如果幸運的話 吸收穿過原子的光子 正好可以提供 這個電子所需的能量

cues.text: just the energy the electron needs.
cues.en: just the energy the electron needs.
cues.zh: 這個電子所需的能量 不過還有一個問題

cues.text: But there's a catch.
cues.en: But there's a catch.
cues.zh: 這個電子所需的能量 不過還有一個問題

cues.text: The energy from the photon has to be the right amount to get an electron to the next row.
cues.en: The energy from the photon has to be the right amount to get an electron to the next row.
cues.zh: 不過還有一個問題 這個光子提供的能量 必須正好等於 把電子送到下一排所需的能量

cues.text: Otherwise, it will just let the photon pass by, and it just so happens that in glass,
cues.en: Otherwise, it will just let the photon pass by, and it just so happens that in glass,
cues.zh: 不然，電子就只得任由光子透過 這就恰如發生在玻璃當中 由於排與排之間相隔非常遙遠

cues.text: the rows are so far apart that a photon of visible light
cues.en: the rows are so far apart that a photon of visible light
cues.zh: 這就恰如發生在玻璃當中 由於排與排之間相隔非常遙遠 可見光的光子

cues.text: can't provide enough energy for an electron to jump between them.
cues.en: can't provide enough energy for an electron to jump between them.
cues.zh: 無法提供電子足夠的能量 在排與排之間跳躍 另一方面，紫外線的光子

cues.text: Photons from ultraviolet light, on the other hand, give just the right amount of energy,
cues.en: Photons from ultraviolet light, on the other hand, give just the right amount of energy,
cues.zh: 在排與排之間跳躍 另一方面，紫外線的光子 便提供恰恰好的能量

cues.text: and are absorbed, which is why you can't get a suntan through glass.
cues.en: and are absorbed, which is why you can't get a suntan through glass.
cues.zh: 便提供恰恰好的能量 而被吸收 這就是為什麼隔著玻璃 皮膚不會被曬黑的原因

cues.text: This amazing property of being both solid and transparent has given glass many uses
cues.en: This amazing property of being both solid and transparent has given glass many uses
cues.zh: 玻璃這種兼具堅固而透明 令人驚歎的特質 賦予了玻璃多種用途

cues.text: throughout the centuries.
cues.en: throughout the centuries.
cues.zh: 令人驚歎的特質 賦予了玻璃多種用途 達數世紀之久

cues.text: From windows that let in light while keeping out the elements, to lenses that allow us to see both
cues.en: From windows that let in light while keeping out the elements, to lenses that allow us to see both
cues.zh: 達數世紀之久 從能透入光線 卻將其他元素阻隔在外的窗戶 到能讓我們看到

cues.text: the vast worlds beyond our planet, and the tiny ones right around us.
cues.en: the vast worlds beyond our planet, and the tiny ones right around us.
cues.zh: 地球以外的浩瀚世界 以及我們週遭的渺小事物

cues.text: It is hard to imagine modern civilization without glass.
cues.en: It is hard to imagine modern civilization without glass.
cues.zh: 實在很難想像 沒有玻璃的現代文明 對於玻璃這麼重要的一個物質

cues.text: And yet for such an important material we rarely think about glass and its impact.
cues.en: And yet for such an important material we rarely think about glass and its impact.
cues.zh: 對於玻璃這麼重要的一個物質 我們卻鮮少想到它及其影響 就是因為玻璃最重要的

cues.text: It is precisely because the most important and useful quality of glass is
cues.en: It is precisely because the most important and useful quality of glass is
cues.zh: 就是因為玻璃最重要的 也最有用的特質就是 平凡而且看不見

cues.text: being featureless and invisible that we often forget that it's even there.
cues.en: being featureless and invisible that we often forget that it's even there.
cues.zh: 平凡而且看不見 所以我們常常忘記它的存在

cues.en: On the day of the big concert, the band wakes up to find themselves tied up
cues.zh: 這讓他們的經理十分惱火。 就在一場大型音樂會的當天， 這個樂隊醒來發現他們被綁在

cues.text: in a windowless, soundproof practice room.
cues.en: in a windowless, soundproof practice room.
cues.zh: 這個樂隊醒來發現他們被綁在 一個沒有窗戶並且隔音的練習室。

cues.text: Their manager explains what's happening.
cues.en: Their manager explains what's happening.
cues.zh: 一個沒有窗戶並且隔音的練習室。 他們的經理解釋了這是怎麼回事。

cues.text: Outside, there are ten large boxes.
cues.en: Outside, there are ten large boxes.
cues.zh: 他們的經理解釋了這是怎麼回事。 在外面，一共有十個大盒子。

cues.text: Each contains one of your instruments, but don't be fooled by the pictures - they've been randomly placed.
cues.en: Each contains one of your instruments, but don't be fooled by the pictures - they've been randomly placed.
cues.zh: 在外面，一共有十個大盒子。 每一個裝著一件你們的樂器， 但別被上面的圖片迷惑了， 他們都是隨機放置的。

cues.text: I'm going to let you out one at a time.

cues.text: While you're outside, you can look inside any five boxes before security takes you back to the tour bus.

cues.text: If each one of you can find your own instrument, then you can play tonight.

cues.en: You have three minutes to think about it before we start.

cues.text: The band is in despair.
cues.en: The band is in despair.

cues.text: After all, each musician only has a 50% chance of finding their instrument

yRwoReHd7XU.title: What is the rarest color in nature? - Victoria Hwang
yRwoReHd7XU.speaker: TED-Ed
yRwoReHd7XU.zh: 【TED-Ed】自然界中最稀有的顏色是什麼？ - 黃維多利亞（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Every color you see in front of you can be found in nature.
cues.en: Every color you see in front of you can be found in nature.
cues.zh: 你眼前的所有顏色， 都能在大自然中找到。 有些植物、動物、礦物， 含有你能想像到的幾乎所有顏色。

cues.text: Some plant, animal, or mineral bears almost every hue imaginable.
cues.en: Some plant, animal, or mineral bears almost every hue imaginable.
cues.zh: 有些植物、動物、礦物， 含有你能想像到的幾乎所有顏色。

cues.text: But which of these colors are you least likely to see in the natural world?
cues.en: But which of these colors are you least likely to see in the natural world?
cues.zh: 但在這些顏色之中， 哪一種顏色最難在自然中發現？

cues.text: There are two factors that drive the rarity of color in nature:
cues.en: There are two factors that drive the rarity of color in nature:
cues.zh: 自然顏色的稀有度， 主要由兩個因素決定：

cues.text: physics and evolution.
cues.en: physics and evolution.
cues.zh: 物理和演化。

cues.text: Let’s start with physics.
cues.en: Let’s start with physics.
cues.zh: 讓我們先來看看物理學。

cues.text: Colors are generated when wavelengths of light interact with objects,
cues.en: Colors are generated when wavelengths of light interact with objects,
cues.zh: 顏色是光的波長 和物體表面互動的結果。

cues.text: and most of the colors you’ve seen outside a screen were produced in one of two ways.
cues.en: and most of the colors you’ve seen outside a screen were produced in one of two ways.
cues.zh: 顏色是光的波長 和物體表面互動的結果。 你在螢幕外看見的大多數顏色， 由兩種方式產生。 就基於吸收而產生的顏色來說，

cues.text: In absorption-based colors, certain wavelengths are absorbed by an object, while others are not.
cues.en: In absorption-based colors, certain wavelengths are absorbed by an object, while others are not.
cues.zh: 就基於吸收而產生的顏色來說， 物體會吸收特定波長的光波， 而反射其他波長的光波。

cues.text: The result is a matte final color generated by these leftover light waves.
cues.en: The result is a matte final color generated by these leftover light waves.
cues.zh: 這些被反射的光波彼此混合， 產生最終顯示的顏色。

cues.text: Most naturally occurring colors fall into this category, including those of many fruits and flowers.
cues.en: Most naturally occurring colors fall into this category, including those of many fruits and flowers.
cues.zh: 大多數的自然顏色都是這樣產生， 包括許多水果和花卉的顏色。

cues.text: Plants are full of compounds called pigments that absorb light waves as part of photosynthesis,
cues.en: Plants are full of compounds called pigments that absorb light waves as part of photosynthesis,
cues.zh: 植物飽含名為「光合色素」的化合物， 用來吸收光線，作為光合作用的一環。 光合作用能將陽光轉化為能量。

cues.text: the process by which they convert sunlight into energy.
cues.en: the process by which they convert sunlight into energy.
cues.zh: 光合作用能將陽光轉化為能量。

cues.text: While different plants have evolved different pigments that result in different colors,
cues.en: While different plants have evolved different pigments that result in different colors,
cues.zh: 由於不同植物演化出不同的色素， 所以它們呈現的顏色也不同，

cues.text: higher energy wavelengths are more easily absorbed than lower energy ones.
cues.en: higher energy wavelengths are more easily absorbed than lower energy ones.
cues.zh: 較高能量的波長， 比較低能量的光更容易被吸收。

cues.text: And blue light has some of the highest energy wavelengths in the visible spectrum.
cues.en: And blue light has some of the highest energy wavelengths in the visible spectrum.
cues.zh: 而在可見光中， 藍光是能量最高的光波之一。

cues.text: Numerous pigments have evolved to absorb blue light, including chlorophyll, which absorbs blue and red wavelengths
cues.en: Numerous pigments have evolved to absorb blue light, including chlorophyll, which absorbs blue and red wavelengths
cues.zh: 許多光合色素演化出吸收藍光的功能， 例如能吸收紅光和藍光的葉綠素， 製造出大自然的標誌性綠色。

cues.text: to produce nature’s trademark green.
cues.en: to produce nature’s trademark green.
cues.zh: 製造出大自然的標誌性綠色。

cues.text: However, green light is still fairly energetic, and the most common class of pigments evolved to absorb these wavelengths
cues.en: However, green light is still fairly energetic, and the most common class of pigments evolved to absorb these wavelengths
cues.zh: 但是，綠光的能量也不低， 因此最常見的光合色素也都演化出 吸收綠光的功能。

cues.text: as well.
cues.en: as well.
cues.zh: 吸收綠光的功能。

cues.text: There are over 1,100 types of carotenoids, pigments which absorb high energy blue and green light,
cues.en: There are over 1,100 types of carotenoids, pigments which absorb high energy blue and green light,
cues.zh: 有超過 1100 種類胡蘿蔔素， 這是一種能吸收高能量的藍光與綠光， 同時反射低能量的 紅光與黃光的光合色素。

cues.text: while leaving behind the lower energy red and yellow light.
cues.en: while leaving behind the lower energy red and yellow light.
cues.zh: 同時反射低能量的 紅光與黃光的光合色素。

cues.text: While carotenoids are present in most green plants, they only become visible each fall when chlorophyll gets broken down
cues.en: While carotenoids are present in most green plants, they only become visible each fall when chlorophyll gets broken down
cues.zh: 雖然幾乎每種植物都含有類胡蘿蔔素， 但要到每年秋天，植物為了 儲備過冬能量而分解葉綠素時，

cues.text: to save energy for the winter.
cues.en: to save energy for the winter.
cues.zh: 但要到每年秋天，植物為了 儲備過冬能量而分解葉綠素時， 我們才能看見它們的顏色。

cues.text: But whether they’re working alone or side by side, these pigments absorb blue light in virtually all plants.
cues.en: But whether they’re working alone or side by side, these pigments absorb blue light in virtually all plants.
cues.zh: 但無論這些光合色素 是分工合作，或是單打獨鬥， 幾乎所有植物都會吸收藍光。

cues.text: Even fruits and flowers that appear blue actually have pigments that are red or purple,
cues.en: Even fruits and flowers that appear blue actually have pigments that are red or purple,
cues.zh: 就算是看似藍色的水果或花朵， 其實也含有紅色或紫色的色素， 並只在特定化學條件下才會變成藍色。

cues.text: and only truly turn blue under specific chemical conditions.
cues.en: and only truly turn blue under specific chemical conditions.
cues.zh: 並只在特定化學條件下才會變成藍色。

cues.text: So, is blue the rarest color in nature?
cues.en: So, is blue the rarest color in nature?
cues.zh: 所以藍色是自然中最稀有的顏色嗎？

cues.text: Not quite.
cues.en: Not quite.
cues.zh: 還不能下定論。

cues.text: Absorption is just one of the two main ways light generates color.
cues.en: Absorption is just one of the two main ways light generates color.
cues.zh: 吸收只是光產生顏色的其中一種方法。

cues.text: In the second method, some wavelengths are scattered and amplified—
cues.en: In the second method, some wavelengths are scattered and amplified—
cues.zh: 第二種方法中， 某些光波被散射、放大， 凌駕於其他光波之上， 決定了物體最終的顏色。

cues.text: overpowering the others to determine an object's final color.
cues.en: overpowering the others to determine an object's final color.
cues.zh: 凌駕於其他光波之上， 決定了物體最終的顏色。

cues.text: These structural colors occur because some objects around us are made of microscopic particles
cues.en: These structural colors occur because some objects around us are made of microscopic particles
cues.zh: 這些結構色之所以產生， 是因為我們周遭的 某些東西由微粒組成， 能產生奈米結構，和可見光相互作用。

cues.text: which can form nanostructures that interfere with visible light.
cues.en: which can form nanostructures that interfere with visible light.
cues.zh: 是因為我們周遭的 某些東西由微粒組成， 能產生奈米結構，和可見光相互作用。

cues.text: For example, this feather has no blue pigments in it.
cues.en: For example, this feather has no blue pigments in it.
cues.zh: 例如，這根羽毛並不含藍色的色素。 但光照射在羽毛上時， 羽毛奈米結構中的電子

cues.text: But when light strikes it, the electrons within its nanostructure
cues.en: But when light strikes it, the electrons within its nanostructure
cues.zh: 但光照射在羽毛上時， 羽毛奈米結構中的電子 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。

cues.text: vibrate at the same frequency as the wave.
cues.en: vibrate at the same frequency as the wave.
cues.zh: 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波，

cues.text: This makes the particles send out a new wave with the same frequency,
cues.en: This makes the particles send out a new wave with the same frequency,
cues.zh: 會用和光波相同的頻率震動。 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波，

cues.text: starting a chain reaction that amplifies and scatters blue light.
cues.en: starting a chain reaction that amplifies and scatters blue light.
cues.zh: 因此，粒子也會發射相同頻率的新波， 開始一段能放大、 折射藍光的連鎖反應。

cues.text: Nanostructures of various shapes and sizes scatter different wavelengths,
cues.en: Nanostructures of various shapes and sizes scatter different wavelengths,
cues.zh: 不同形狀和尺寸的奈米結構， 會折射出不同波長， 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波，

cues.text: but they typically scatter high-energy wavelengths most easily—
cues.en: but they typically scatter high-energy wavelengths most easily—
cues.zh: 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波， 讓藍光成了最常見的「構造色」。

cues.text: making blue the most common structural color.
cues.en: making blue the most common structural color.
cues.zh: 但它們通常最容易折射高能量的光波， 讓藍光成了最常見的「構造色」。

cues.text: Meanwhile, low-energy wavelengths like red are only weakly scattered.
cues.en: Meanwhile, low-energy wavelengths like red are only weakly scattered.
cues.zh: 而紅色這種低能量的光波， 折射力道通常很弱。

cues.text: Even when something evolves specific nanostructures that strongly scatter red light
cues.en: Even when something evolves specific nanostructures that strongly scatter red light
cues.zh: 就算有東西演化出特別的奈米結構， 能折射出強烈的紅光， 這些結構仍會和其他波長的光共振，

cues.text: they still resonate with other wavelengths, only appearing red at some angles of illumination and observation.
cues.en: they still resonate with other wavelengths, only appearing red at some angles of illumination and observation.
cues.zh: 這些結構仍會和其他波長的光共振， 只能以某些角度照明、觀察， 才能看見紅色。

cues.text: This gives us two contenders for nature’s rarest color:
cues.en: This gives us two contenders for nature’s rarest color:
cues.zh: 這讓我們看見自然界 最稀有顏色的兩個競爭者：

cues.text: absorption-based matte blues and structural iridescent reds.
cues.en: absorption-based matte blues and structural iridescent reds.
cues.zh: 因吸收混合出的藍色， 以及結構色中的紅色。

cues.text: Between these two, structural reds are much rarer.
cues.en: Between these two, structural reds are much rarer.
cues.zh: 以這兩者來說，結構色的紅色更稀有。

cues.text: Only a handful of animals and rocks scatter red light
cues.en: Only a handful of animals and rocks scatter red light
cues.zh: 只有少數動物和石頭能折射出紅光，

cues.text: and none of them scatter red light exclusively.
cues.en: and none of them scatter red light exclusively.
cues.zh: 但沒有一種物體能只折射出紅光。

cues.text: But since red and blue are rare in one way and common in another,
cues.en: But since red and blue are rare in one way and common in another,
cues.zh: 在兩種形成顏色的方式中，紅色 和藍色各是一種稀缺另一種普遍，

cues.text: we actually end up seeing both colors quite often.
cues.en: we actually end up seeing both colors quite often.
cues.zh: 在兩種形成顏色的方式中，紅色 和藍色各是一種稀缺另一種普遍， 因此我們仍能時常看見紅色與藍色。

cues.text: So what color is least likely to be generated in structural and absorption-based forms?
cues.en: So what color is least likely to be generated in structural and absorption-based forms?
cues.zh: 所以，究竟是哪種顏色最難製造， 不管是以結構色還是吸收色而言？

cues.text: The answer is violet.
cues.en: The answer is violet.
cues.zh: 答案是藍紫色。

cues.text: Not to be confused with purple, which is just a combination of red and blue light,
cues.en: Not to be confused with purple, which is just a combination of red and blue light,
cues.zh: 可別把它誤認成 紅光和藍光混合出的紫色。

cues.text: violet occupies a small portion of the visible light spectrum.
cues.en: violet occupies a small portion of the visible light spectrum.
cues.zh: 可別把它誤認成 紅光和藍光混合出的紫色。 藍紫光也是可見光譜裡的小小一員。

cues.text: There are only a few nanostructures precise enough to exclusively scatter violet light.
cues.en: There are only a few nanostructures precise enough to exclusively scatter violet light.
cues.zh: 只有少數夠精確的奈米結構， 才能特別散射出藍紫光。 藍紫光的能量比藍光更強，

cues.text: And violet wavelengths are even more energetic than blue ones, making them likely to be absorbed by pigment.
cues.en: And violet wavelengths are even more energetic than blue ones, making them likely to be absorbed by pigment.
cues.zh: 藍紫光的能量比藍光更強， 因此更容易被光合色素吸收。

cues.text: So if you ever stumble onto the iridescent violet wings
cues.en: So if you ever stumble onto the iridescent violet wings
cues.zh: 所以如果你碰巧看到 紫帝王蝶的藍紫色雙翅，

cues.text: of a purple emperor butterfly, take a second to appreciate one of nature’s rarest spectacles.
cues.en: of a purple emperor butterfly, take a second to appreciate one of nature’s rarest spectacles.
cues.zh: 紫帝王蝶的藍紫色雙翅， 就花點時間，欣賞 大自然中最獨特的奇觀吧。

WiX2amY7G-I.title: 5. Gothic Cathedrals
WiX2amY7G-I.speaker: Engineering Models
WiX2amY7G-I.zh: 【Engineering Models】5. 哥德式大教堂（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Gothic Cathedrals represent one of the high points in Western architecture.
cues.en: Gothic Cathedrals represent one of the high points in Western architecture.
cues.zh: 哥德式大教堂代表了西方建築的高峰之一。

cues.text: Their builders wanted to construct places of worship with upwards looking spaces and light filled interiors –
cues.en: Their builders wanted to construct places of worship with upwards looking spaces and light filled interiors –
cues.zh: 他們的建造者希望建造具有向上看的空間和光線充足的內部空間的禮拜場所 -

cues.text: features that spoke of the God they worshiped.
cues.en: features that spoke of the God they worshiped.
cues.zh: 這些特徵講述了他們所崇拜的上帝。

cues.text: To realize these grand goals, generations of builders, from the 12 to 16th centuries,
cues.en: To realize these grand goals, generations of builders, from the 12 to 16th centuries,
cues.zh: 為了實現這些宏偉目標，從12世紀到16世紀的一代代建設者，

cues.text: were forced to make dramatic advances in both architecture and engineering.
cues.en: were forced to make dramatic advances in both architecture and engineering.
cues.zh: 被迫在建築和工程方面取得巨大進展。

cues.text: Their efforts gave rise to many innovations, including large buildings with complex vaulted ceilings,
cues.en: Their efforts gave rise to many innovations, including large buildings with complex vaulted ceilings,
cues.zh: 他們的努力催生了許多創新，包括具有複雜拱形天花板的大型建築，

cues.text: high stained-glass windows, pointed arches that reduce lateral loading,
cues.en: high stained-glass windows, pointed arches that reduce lateral loading,
cues.zh: 高高的彩色玻璃窗，減少橫向載重的尖拱，

cues.text: and flying buttresses that can support tall thin walls
cues.en: and flying buttresses that can support tall thin walls
cues.zh: 以及可以支撐又高又薄的牆壁的飛扶壁

cues.text: while letting the sun shine in.
cues.en: while letting the sun shine in.
cues.zh: 同時讓陽光照進來。

cues.text: For thousands of years leading up to this time, most buildings were constructed
cues.en: For thousands of years leading up to this time, most buildings were constructed
cues.zh: 在此之前的數千年裡，大多數建築物都是建造的

cues.text: using posts and beams.
cues.en: using posts and beams.
cues.zh: 使用柱子和橫樑。

cues.text: The vertical loads carried by the beams resulted in simple, vertical loads
cues.en: The vertical loads carried by the beams resulted in simple, vertical loads
cues.zh: 梁承受的垂直荷載導致簡單的垂直荷載

cues.text: in the posts or walls to which they were attached.
cues.en: in the posts or walls to which they were attached.
cues.zh: 在它們所附著的柱子或牆壁上。

cues.text: Beams, however, could not stretch across the much wider spaces required for the new cathedrals.
cues.en: Beams, however, could not stretch across the much wider spaces required for the new cathedrals.
cues.zh: 然而，橫梁無法延伸到新大教堂所需的更廣闊的空間。

cues.text: Arches, like this model or this simplified model,
cues.en: Arches, like this model or this simplified model,
cues.zh: 拱門，就像這個模型或這個簡化的模型，

cues.text: could span these large distances.
cues.en: could span these large distances.
cues.zh: 可以跨越這麼大的距離。

cues.text: However, they generated large, horizontal forces at their ends,
cues.en: However, they generated large, horizontal forces at their ends,
cues.zh: 然而，它們在末端產生了巨大的水平力，

cues.text: and they could collapse if those forces were not adequately resisted.
cues.en: and they could collapse if those forces were not adequately resisted.
cues.zh: 如果這些力量沒有得到充分抵抗，它們可能會崩潰。

cues.text: Short, thick walls might be able to resist these forces,
cues.en: Short, thick walls might be able to resist these forces,
cues.zh: 短而厚的牆壁也許能夠抵抗這些力量，

cues.text: but the cathedral designers wanted tall, thin ones.
cues.en: but the cathedral designers wanted tall, thin ones.
cues.zh: 但大教堂設計師想要又高又瘦的。

cues.text: And they wanted to put large glass windows in those walls so the sun could illuminate the inside of their cathedrals.
cues.en: And they wanted to put large glass windows in those walls so the sun could illuminate the inside of their cathedrals.
cues.zh: 他們想在這些牆上安裝大玻璃窗，這樣陽光就可以照亮大教堂的內部。

cues.text: The horizontal loads generated by arch ceilings would have easily pushed over the kinds of walls they wanted to build.
cues.en: The horizontal loads generated by arch ceilings would have easily pushed over the kinds of walls they wanted to build.
cues.zh: 拱形天花板產生的水平荷載很容易推過他們想要建造的牆壁。

cues.text: One possible solution to this problem was to pile stone on the outside of the building
cues.en: One possible solution to this problem was to pile stone on the outside of the building
cues.zh: 解決這個問題的一個可能的解決方案是在建築物的外部堆砌石頭

cues.text: so as to support the wall.
cues.en: so as to support the wall.
cues.zh: 從而支撐牆壁。

cues.text: Over time, the engineers developed structures called buttresses,
cues.en: Over time, the engineers developed structures called buttresses,
cues.zh: 隨著時間的推移，工程師們發展了一種叫做扶壁的結構，

cues.text: and these elegant structures can be found in many early Gothic cathedrals.
cues.en: and these elegant structures can be found in many early Gothic cathedrals.
cues.zh: 這些優雅的結構在許多早期哥德式大教堂中都能找到。

cues.text: Unfortunately, they tend to block the sunlight, as this model demonstrates.
cues.en: Unfortunately, they tend to block the sunlight, as this model demonstrates.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，正如該模型所示，它們往往會阻擋陽光。

cues.text: In time, designers figured out how to build thin lateral supports called flying buttresses.
cues.en: In time, designers figured out how to build thin lateral supports called flying buttresses.
cues.zh: 隨著時間的推移，設計師們找到如何建造稱為飛扶壁的薄型橫向支撐。

cues.text: The earlier buttress designs were essentially broken into separate tall pieces
cues.en: The earlier buttress designs were essentially broken into separate tall pieces
cues.zh: 早期的扶壁設計基本上被分成單獨的高塊

cues.text: and moved a short distance from the side of the building.
cues.en: and moved a short distance from the side of the building.
cues.zh: 並從建築物的側面移動了一小段距離。

cues.text: The resulting tall sections were called piers, and they were connected to each other
cues.en: The resulting tall sections were called piers, and they were connected to each other
cues.zh: 由此產生的高部分稱為橋墩，它們相互連線

cues.text: and to the side of the cathedral using sloped, arch-like members called flyers.
cues.en: and to the side of the cathedral using sloped, arch-like members called flyers.
cues.zh: 大教堂的側面使用傾斜的拱形構件，稱為傳單。

cues.text: As this model demonstrates, flying buttresses kept the tall, thin walls from collapsing,
cues.en: As this model demonstrates, flying buttresses kept the tall, thin walls from collapsing,
cues.zh: 正如這個模型所展示的，飛扶壁可以防止又高又薄的牆壁倒塌，

cues.text: and they allowed the sun to shine in.
cues.en: and they allowed the sun to shine in.
cues.zh: 他們讓陽光照進來。

cues.text: This drawing shows how the forces from the vaulted ceilings were transferred to the flyers
cues.en: This drawing shows how the forces from the vaulted ceilings were transferred to the flyers
cues.zh: 這張圖顯示了拱形天花板的力如何傳遞到傳單上

cues.text: and then down through the piers to the ground.
cues.en: and then down through the piers to the ground.
cues.zh: 然後穿過橋墩到達地面。

cues.text: Spires and other heavy architectural features were sometimes placed on the tops of the piers
cues.en: Spires and other heavy architectural features were sometimes placed on the tops of the piers
cues.zh: 尖塔和其他重型建築特徵有時被放置在橋墩的頂部

cues.text: so that the lateral components of the arch forces could be more efficiently transferred to the ground.

ofk-aw5G-FQ.title: How comic books can help you learn - Gene Luen Yang
ofk-aw5G-FQ.speaker: TED-Ed
ofk-aw5G-FQ.zh: 【TED-Ed】漫畫書如何幫助你學習 - Gene Luen Yang（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: When I was in the fifth grade, I bought an issue of DC Comics Presents number 57
cues.en: When I was in the fifth grade, I bought an issue of DC Comics Presents number 57
cues.zh: 五年級的時候，我從我家附近 書店的旋轉書架上買了一本

cues.text: off of a spinner rack at my local bookstore.
cues.en: off of a spinner rack at my local bookstore.
cues.zh: 第五十七集的《DC 漫畫特刊》。

cues.text: And that comic book changed my life.
cues.en: And that comic book changed my life.
cues.zh: 那本漫畫改變了我的人生。

cues.text: I immediately fell in love with the medium of comics.
cues.en: I immediately fell in love with the medium of comics.
cues.zh: 我馬上就愛上了漫畫這種媒介。

cues.text: But I never brought them to school.
cues.en: But I never brought them to school.
cues.zh: 但我從來不會帶漫畫 去學校，因為我直覺知道

cues.text: Instinctively, I knew that comic books didn’t belong in the classroom.
cues.en: Instinctively, I knew that comic books didn’t belong in the classroom.
cues.zh: 但我從來不會帶漫畫 去學校，因為我直覺知道 漫畫不該出現在教室裡。

cues.text: Eventually, I became a published cartoonist, writing and drawing comic books for a living.
cues.en: Eventually, I became a published cartoonist, writing and drawing comic books for a living.
cues.zh: 最終，我成了有出版作品的漫畫家， 靠撰寫和繪製漫畫來維生。

cues.text: I also became a high school teacher.
cues.en: I also became a high school teacher.
cues.zh: 我也成了高中老師。

cues.text: This is where I taught: Bishop O’Dowd High School in Oakland, California.
cues.en: This is where I taught: Bishop O’Dowd High School in Oakland, California.
cues.zh: 我教書的地方是加州 奧克蘭的奧多德主教高中。

cues.text: I remember telling my students on the first day of every class that I was also a cartoonist.
cues.en: I remember telling my students on the first day of every class that I was also a cartoonist.
cues.zh: 我記得在每門課的第一堂課 我都會告訴我的學生我身兼漫畫家。

cues.text: I was hoping comics would make them think that I was cool.
cues.en: I was hoping comics would make them think that I was cool.
cues.zh: 我希望漫畫會讓他們覺得我很酷。

cues.text: I was wrong.
cues.en: I was wrong.
cues.zh: 我錯了。

cues.text: They thought I was kind of a dork.
cues.en: They thought I was kind of a dork.
cues.zh: 他們反而覺得我是個阿呆。

cues.text: They would use comic books as a way of distracting me.
cues.en: They would use comic books as a way of distracting me.
cues.zh: 他們會用漫畫來讓我分心。

cues.text: They would raise their hands and ask me questions like, “Mr. Yang, who do you think would win in a fight: Superman or the Hulk?”
cues.en: They would raise their hands and ask me questions like, “Mr. Yang, who do you think would win in a fight: Superman or the Hulk?”
cues.zh: 他們會舉手，問我像這樣的問題： 「楊老師，你認為如果超人 和浩克對打，誰會贏？」

cues.text: It seemed like my instincts in fifth grade were correct— comic books didn’t belong in the classroom—
cues.en: It seemed like my instincts in fifth grade were correct— comic books didn’t belong in the classroom—
cues.zh: 我在五年級時的直覺似乎是對的—— 漫畫不該出現在教室裡——

cues.text: but again I was wrong.
cues.en: but again I was wrong.
cues.zh: 但我又錯了。

cues.text: One semester I was asked to sub for this Algebra 2 class.
cues.en: One semester I was asked to sub for this Algebra 2 class.
cues.zh: 有一個學期，我去代 「代數二」這門課。

cues.text: But there was a problem.
cues.en: But there was a problem.
cues.zh: 但有個問題：每幾週， 我就有一、兩堂課非請假不可。

cues.text: Every couple of weeks, I had to miss 1 or 2 periods.
cues.en: Every couple of weeks, I had to miss 1 or 2 periods.
cues.zh: 但有個問題：每幾週， 我就有一、兩堂課非請假不可。

cues.text: In an effort to provide some sort of consistency for my students,
cues.en: In an effort to provide some sort of consistency for my students,
cues.zh: 為了提供我的學生 某種程度的一致性，

cues.text: I began videotaping myself giving lectures.
cues.en: I began videotaping myself giving lectures.
cues.zh: 我開始把自己教課的過程錄影下來。

cues.text: I tried to make these videos as engaging as possible.
cues.en: I tried to make these videos as engaging as possible.
cues.zh: 我盡量把這些影片做到能吸引人。

cues.text: These video lectures were a disaster.
cues.en: These video lectures were a disaster.
cues.zh: 這些課程影片簡直是災難， 有學生來找我，說像這樣的話：

cues.text: I had students coming up to me and saying things like, “Mr. Yang, we thought you were boring in person,
cues.en: I had students coming up to me and saying things like, “Mr. Yang, we thought you were boring in person,
cues.zh: 這些課程影片簡直是災難， 有學生來找我，說像這樣的話： 「楊老師，我們以為 你本人已經夠無趣了，但，

cues.text: but on video you are just unbearable.” So as a desperate second attempt, I began drawing these lectures as comics.
cues.en: but on video you are just unbearable.” So as a desperate second attempt, I began drawing these lectures as comics.
cues.zh: 影片中的你簡直讓人無法忍受。」 我做了絕望的第二次嘗試， 開始把這些課程畫成漫畫。

cues.text: Much to my surprise, these comics lectures were a hit.
cues.en: Much to my surprise, these comics lectures were a hit.
cues.zh: 出乎意料，這些課程漫畫大受歡迎。

cues.text: My students would ask me to make these for them, even when I could be there in person.
cues.en: My students would ask me to make these for them, even when I could be there in person.
cues.zh: 即使我可以親自教學，我的學生 還是希望我幫他們把課程畫成漫畫，

cues.text: it was like they liked cartoon me more than actual me.
cues.en: it was like they liked cartoon me more than actual me.
cues.zh: 好像他們比較喜歡漫畫版的我， 而不是真正的我。

cues.text: I began to understand the educational potential of comics.
cues.en: I began to understand the educational potential of comics.
cues.zh: 我開始瞭解漫畫的教育潛力。

cues.text: Comics lectures taught visually.
cues.en: Comics lectures taught visually.
cues.zh: 課程漫畫是用視覺的方式來教學。

cues.text: Our students grow up in a visual culture— so they’re used to taking in information that way.
cues.en: Our students grow up in a visual culture— so they’re used to taking in information that way.
cues.zh: 我們的學生是在視覺文化中長大， 所以他們很習慣 用視覺的方式吸收資訊。

cues.text: In a comic, past, present, and future all sit side by side on the same page.
cues.en: In a comic, past, present, and future all sit side by side on the same page.
cues.zh: 在漫畫中，過去，現在， 和未來都並存在同一頁上。

cues.text: This means that the rate of information flow is firmly in the hands of the reader.
cues.en: This means that the rate of information flow is firmly in the hands of the reader.
cues.zh: 意思就是，資訊流動的速度 完全由讀者掌控。

cues.text: When my students didn’t understand something in my comics lecture,
cues.en: When my students didn’t understand something in my comics lecture,
cues.zh: 當我的學生不瞭解 課程漫畫中的某部分時，

cues.text: they could just reread that passage as quickly or as slowly as they needed.
cues.en: they could just reread that passage as quickly or as slowly as they needed.
cues.zh: 當我的學生不瞭解 課程漫畫中的某部分時， 他們可以重讀那一段，閱讀速度 要快要慢完全根據自己的需求。

cues.text: Comic books first became a mass medium in the 1940s, with millions of copies selling every month.
cues.en: Comic books first became a mass medium in the 1940s, with millions of copies selling every month.
cues.zh: 在 1940 年代，漫畫 首次成為大眾媒介， 那時，每個月可以賣出數百萬冊。

cues.text: A lot of innovative teachers began bringing comics into their classrooms
cues.en: A lot of innovative teachers began bringing comics into their classrooms
cues.zh: 許多創新的老師開始 將漫畫帶進他們的教室，

cues.text: to experiment.
cues.en: to experiment.
cues.zh: 進行實驗。

cues.text: But then along comes this guy.
cues.en: But then along comes this guy.
cues.zh: 但後來這個傢伙出現了。

cues.text: This is child psychologist Dr. Fredrick Wortham, and in 1954, he wrote a book called “Seduction of the innocent,”
cues.en: This is child psychologist Dr. Fredrick Wortham, and in 1954, he wrote a book called “Seduction of the innocent,”
cues.zh: 他是兒童心理學家 佛雷德里克‧沃瑟姆博士， 在 1954 年，他寫了 《誘惑無辜者》這本書， 在書中，他主張漫畫 會造成青少年犯罪。

cues.text: where he argues that comic books cause juvenile delinquency.
cues.en: where he argues that comic books cause juvenile delinquency.
cues.zh: 在書中，他主張漫畫 會造成青少年犯罪。

cues.text: He was wrong.
cues.en: He was wrong.
cues.zh: 他錯了。

cues.text: In the 1940s and 50s, almost every kid in America read comic books.
cues.en: In the 1940s and 50s, almost every kid in America read comic books.
cues.zh: 在 1940 和 1950 年代，在美國 幾乎所有的孩子都會看漫畫。

cues.text: Dr. Wortham does a pretty dubious job of proving his case, but his book does inspire the Senate of the United States
cues.en: Dr. Wortham does a pretty dubious job of proving his case, but his book does inspire the Senate of the United States
cues.zh: 沃瑟姆博士並沒有為他的論點 提出可靠的證據， 但他的書確實導致美國參議院 舉行一系列聽證會， 以瞭解實際上漫畫是否會造成

cues.text: to hold a series of hearings to see if, in fact, comic books caused juvenile delinquency.
cues.en: to hold a series of hearings to see if, in fact, comic books caused juvenile delinquency.
cues.zh: 舉行一系列聽證會， 以瞭解實際上漫畫是否會造成 青少年犯罪。

cues.text: These hearings lasted for almost two months.
cues.en: These hearings lasted for almost two months.
cues.zh: 這些聽證會持續了近兩個月的時間，

cues.text: They ended inconclusively, but not before doing tremendous damage to the reputation of comic books
cues.en: They ended inconclusively, but not before doing tremendous damage to the reputation of comic books
cues.zh: 最後也沒得出結論， 但早就已經嚴重損毀了 美國大眾眼中漫畫的名聲。

cues.text: in the eyes of the American public.
cues.en: in the eyes of the American public.
cues.zh: 美國大眾眼中漫畫的名聲。

cues.text: It wasn’t until the 1970s that a few brave souls started making their way back in
cues.en: It wasn’t until the 1970s that a few brave souls started making their way back in
cues.zh: 一直到 1970 年代，才有幾個 勇敢的人重新涉足這個領域，

cues.text: and it really wasn’t until pretty recently— maybe the last decade or so—
cues.en: and it really wasn’t until pretty recently— maybe the last decade or so—
cues.zh: 且要到非常近期—— 也許是過去十年左右——

cues.text: that comics have seen more widespread acceptance among American educators.
cues.en: that comics have seen more widespread acceptance among American educators.
cues.zh: 美國的教育界才比較廣泛接受漫畫。

cues.text: And this is even happening at Bishop O’Dowd, where I used to teach.
cues.en: And this is even happening at Bishop O’Dowd, where I used to teach.
cues.zh: 甚至連我以前任職的 奧多德主教高中都開始接受了。

cues.text: Mr. Smith, one of my former colleagues, uses Scott McCloud’s “Understanding Comics” in his literature and film class.
cues.en: Mr. Smith, one of my former colleagues, uses Scott McCloud’s “Understanding Comics” in his literature and film class.
cues.zh: 甚至連我以前任職的 奧多德主教高中都開始接受了。 我的前同事史密斯老師把史考特‧ 麥克勞德的《漫畫原來要這樣看》 用在他的「文學與電影」課。

cues.text: Mr. Burns assigns a comics essay to his students every year
cues.en: Mr. Burns assigns a comics essay to his students every year
cues.zh: 伯恩斯老師每年都會要求 他的學生繳交一篇漫畫論文，

cues.text: by asking his students to process a prose novel using images.
cues.en: by asking his students to process a prose novel using images.
cues.zh: 做法是要求學生用影象來呈現 一部散文小說的內容。

cues.text: And Miss Murac uses my own “American Born Chinese” with her English one students.
cues.en: And Miss Murac uses my own “American Born Chinese” with her English one students.
cues.zh: 穆拉克老師則是用我寫的 《生在美國的中國人》 來教「英文一」的學生。

cues.text: Over in the library, Miss Counts has built a pretty impressive graphic novel collection
cues.en: Over in the library, Miss Counts has built a pretty impressive graphic novel collection
cues.zh: 在圖書館，伯特小姐為奧多德 主教高中建立了精采的漫畫館藏。

cues.text: for Bishop O’Dowd.
cues.en: for Bishop O’Dowd.
cues.zh: 在圖書館，伯特小姐為奧多德 主教高中建立了精采的漫畫館藏。

cues.text: A school library journal article stated that the mere presence of graphic novels
cues.en: A school library journal article stated that the mere presence of graphic novels
cues.zh: 有一篇學校圖書館期刊文章 指出光是在圖書館內納入漫畫館藏

cues.text: in a library increased usage by about 80%, and increased the circulation of non-comics material by about 30%.
cues.en: in a library increased usage by about 80%, and increased the circulation of non-comics material by about 30%.
cues.zh: 指出光是在圖書館內納入漫畫館藏 就能讓圖書館的使用量增加約八成， 並讓非漫畫館藏的流通量 增加了約三成。

cues.text: American cartoonists are now producing more explicitly educational content
cues.en: American cartoonists are now producing more explicitly educational content
cues.zh: 美國漫畫家現在 為幼稚園到十二年級市場 創作的明確教育內容 比以往都還要多。

cues.text: for the K-12 market than ever before.
cues.en: for the K-12 market than ever before.
cues.zh: 創作的明確教育內容 比以往都還要多。

cues.text: More comics and graphic novels are starting to tackle math and science topics.
cues.en: More comics and graphic novels are starting to tackle math and science topics.
cues.zh: 有越來越多漫畫開始 處理數學和科學主題。

cues.text: STEM comics and graphic novels really are like this uncharted territory
cues.en: STEM comics and graphic novels really are like this uncharted territory
cues.zh: 科學、科技、工程、數學漫畫就像是 等待著被探索的未知領土。

cues.text: ready to be explored.
cues.en: ready to be explored.
cues.zh: 等待著被探索的未知領土。

cues.text: America is finally waking up to the fact that comic books
cues.en: America is finally waking up to the fact that comic books
cues.zh: 美國終於認清了這個事實： 漫畫確實應該成為 教育工作者的工具之一。

cues.text: really do belong in every educator’s toolkit.
cues.en: really do belong in every educator’s toolkit.
cues.zh: 漫畫確實應該成為 教育工作者的工具之一。

cues.text: The educational potential is there just waiting to be tapped
cues.en: The educational potential is there just waiting to be tapped
cues.zh: 教育潛力就在那裡， 等著像你這樣有創意的人去善用。

cues.text: by creative people like you.
cues.en: by creative people like you.
cues.zh: 等著像你這樣有創意的人去善用。

sfAyXjRFUJk.title: How The Global Computer Chip Shortage Happened
sfAyXjRFUJk.speaker: CNBC
sfAyXjRFUJk.zh: 【CNBC】全球電腦晶片短缺是如何發生的（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: It's not an overstatement to say that semiconductors power the modern world.
cues.en: It's not an overstatement to say that semiconductors power the modern world.
cues.zh: 說半導體為現代世界提供動力並不誇張。

cues.text: They're not only a key component of nearly every electronic device we buy and use, they
cues.en: They're not only a key component of nearly every electronic device we buy and use, they
cues.zh: 它們不僅是我們購買和使用的幾乎所有電子裝置的關鍵元件，

cues.text: also power the factories that make the electronic devices we buy and use.
cues.en: also power the factories that make the electronic devices we buy and use.
cues.zh: 也為生產我們購買和使用的電子裝置的工廠提供電力。

cues.text: They power our laptops, our cell phones, our cars, our washing machines, our refrigerators,
cues.en: They power our laptops, our cell phones, our cars, our washing machines, our refrigerators,
cues.zh: 它們為我們的筆記型電腦、手機、汽車、洗衣機、冰箱、

cues.text: yeah, even our refrigerators.
cues.en: yeah, even our refrigerators.
cues.zh: 是的，甚至我們的冰箱。

cues.text: And this is just the stuff in our home.
cues.en: And this is just the stuff in our home.
cues.zh: 這只是我們家裡的東西。

cues.zh: 這種節約用水、節約用水的運動，現在成為貧窮人口必須承擔的負擔。

cues.text: Living on a fixed income, I cannot afford any of this.
cues.en: Living on a fixed income, I cannot afford any of this.
cues.zh: 靠固定收入過活，我負擔不起這些。

cues.text: It might be that we don't end up treating all water equally.
cues.en: It might be that we don't end up treating all water equally.
cues.zh: 也許我們最終並沒有平等地對待所有的水。

cues.text: We know that there is a certain percentage of water,
cues.en: We know that there is a certain percentage of water,
cues.zh: 我們知道水有一定的比例，

cues.text: it's around 60 liters per day per person, that is associated with human rights issues,
cues.en: it's around 60 liters per day per person, that is associated with human rights issues,
cues.zh: 每人每天約 60 公升，與人權問題有關，

cues.text: but above that, people should pay for water.
cues.en: but above that, people should pay for water.
cues.zh: 但除此之外，人們還應該為水付費。

cues.text: In 2017, Philadelphia started experimenting with tying water prices to income.
cues.en: In 2017, Philadelphia started experimenting with tying water prices to income.
cues.zh: 2017年，費城開始嘗試將水價與收入掛鉤。

cues.text: We need to price it in such a way that we protect basic human needs.
cues.en: We need to price it in such a way that we protect basic human needs.
cues.zh: 我們需要以保護人類基本需求的方式定價。

cues.text: The fact that we all need water makes this crisis exceptionally hard.
cues.en: The fact that we all need water makes this crisis exceptionally hard.
cues.zh: 我們都需要水這一事實使得這場危機異常艱難。

cues.text: But it can also inspire people to act in exceptional ways to solve it.
cues.en: But it can also inspire people to act in exceptional ways to solve it.
cues.zh: 但它也可以激勵人們以特殊的方式採取行動來解決這個問題。

cues.text: Cape Town's Day Zero was first scheduled for March 18.
cues.en: Cape Town's Day Zero was first scheduled for March 18.
cues.zh: 開普敦的「零日」原定於 3 月 18 日舉行。

cues.text: But then people started conserving.
cues.en: But then people started conserving.
cues.zh: 但後來人們開始節約。

cues.text: The water restrictions are clearly having some effect.
cues.en: The water restrictions are clearly having some effect.
cues.zh: 限水措施顯然產生了一些效果。

cues.text: Day Zero has been pushed back by a month.
cues.en: Day Zero has been pushed back by a month.
cues.zh: 「零日」已延後一個月。

cues.text: Cape Town announced it pushed back Day Zero until July 9th.
cues.en: Cape Town announced it pushed back Day Zero until July 9th.
cues.zh: 開普敦宣佈將「零日」推遲到 7 月 9 日。

cues.text: Authorities expect Day Zero, as it's been dubbed, to take place at the end of August instead of July.
cues.en: Authorities expect Day Zero, as it's been dubbed, to take place at the end of August instead of July.
cues.zh: 當局預計「零日」（即所謂的「零日」）將於八月底而不是七月發生。

cues.text: Now, that's since been pushed back to next year, thanks to extraordinary efforts of residents and authorities.
cues.en: Now, that's since been pushed back to next year, thanks to extraordinary efforts of residents and authorities.
cues.zh: 現在，由於居民和當局的非凡努力，這一目標已被推遲到明年。

cues.text: By early 2018, the city's water consumption was less than half what it had been just four years earlier,
cues.en: By early 2018, the city's water consumption was less than half what it had been just four years earlier,
cues.zh: 到 2018 年初，該市的用水量還不到四年前的一半，

cues.text: and the Day Zero countdown clock was paused indefinitely.
cues.en: and the Day Zero countdown clock was paused indefinitely.
cues.zh: 零日倒數被無限期暫停。

cues.text: Not enough action was taken until they started talking about Day Zero.
cues.en: Not enough action was taken until they started talking about Day Zero.
cues.zh: 在他們開始談論「零日」之前，並沒有採取足夠的行動。

cues.text: That really got people's attention.
cues.en: That really got people's attention.
cues.zh: 這確實引起了人們的注意。

cues.text: And it was remarkable, between the time that the city started to talk about Day Zero
cues.en: And it was remarkable, between the time that the city started to talk about Day Zero
cues.zh: 值得注意的是，在這座城市開始談論「零日」期間

cues.text: and, a month later, how much people cut back their water use.
cues.en: and, a month later, how much people cut back their water use.
cues.zh: 一個月後，有多少人減少了用水量。

cues.text: And it goes to show what we can do.
cues.en: And it goes to show what we can do.
cues.zh: 這表明我們可以做什麼。

cues.text: But Cape Town also got lucky.
cues.en: But Cape Town also got lucky.
cues.zh: 但開普敦也很幸運。

cues.text: It rained.
cues.en: It rained.
cues.zh: 下雨了。

cues.text: The trick is recognizing how valuable water is before there isn't enough of it,
cues.en: The trick is recognizing how valuable water is before there isn't enough of it,
cues.zh: 訣竅是在水不足之前認識到水的價值，

cues.text: and remembering that our fates are tied to what rushes out of our taps.
cues.en: and remembering that our fates are tied to what rushes out of our taps.
cues.zh: 並記住我們的命運與從水龍頭流出的水息息相關。

cues.text: Mexico City was founded within a lake.
cues.en: Mexico City was founded within a lake.
cues.zh: 墨西哥城建在一個湖中。

cues.text: But today our relation with water is very distant.
cues.en: But today our relation with water is very distant.
cues.zh: 但今天我們與水的關係卻非常遙遠。

cues.text: It's very important to recover our historical consciousness with water.
cues.en: It's very important to recover our historical consciousness with water.
cues.zh: 用水來恢復我們的歷史意識是非常重要的。

cues.text: There are many actions individuals can take in order to save water,
cues.en: There are many actions individuals can take in order to save water,
cues.zh: 個人可以採取許多行動來節約用水，

cues.text: but also to be aware that water has a value.
cues.en: but also to be aware that water has a value.
cues.zh: 但也要意識到水是有價值的。

xgFInCmXrPw.title: Milan and Lake Como
xgFInCmXrPw.speaker: Rick Steves' Europe
xgFInCmXrPw.zh: 【Rick Steves' Europe】米蘭和科莫湖（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Hi, I'm Rick Steves, back with more of the best of Europe.
cues.en: Hi, I'm Rick Steves, back with more of the best of Europe.
cues.zh: 大家好，我是裡克·史蒂夫斯，我帶著更多歐洲最好的作品回來了。

cues.text: This time, we're in north Italy, enjoying the lofty and inspiring heights of Milano.
cues.en: This time, we're in north Italy, enjoying the lofty and inspiring heights of Milano.
cues.zh: 這一次，我們來到了義大利北部，欣賞米蘭的崇高和鼓舞人心的高度。

cues.text: Thanks for joining us.
cues.en: Thanks for joining us.
cues.zh: 感謝您加入我們。

cues.text: Many tourists come to Italy because of its past.
cues.en: Many tourists come to Italy because of its past.
cues.zh: 許多遊客來到義大利是因為它的過去。

cues.text: But Milano is today's Italy, and no Italian trip is complete without visiting this city.
cues.en: But Milano is today's Italy, and no Italian trip is complete without visiting this city.
cues.zh: 但米蘭就是今天的義大利，如果不參觀這座城市，義大利之旅就不完整。

cues.text: While overlooked by many, Milano has plenty to see and is a joy to visit.
cues.en: While overlooked by many, Milano has plenty to see and is a joy to visit.
cues.zh: 雖然米蘭被許多人忽視，但它有很多值得一看的地方，而且遊覽起來很愉快。

cues.text: In Milano, we'll soar on the rooftop of one of Europe's grandest Gothic cathedrals,
cues.en: In Milano, we'll soar on the rooftop of one of Europe's grandest Gothic cathedrals,
cues.zh: 在米蘭，我們將翱翔在歐洲最宏偉的哥德式大教堂之一的屋頂上，

cues.text: window-shop in Milan's fashionable neighborhoods, visit the world's most famous Opera house,
cues.en: window-shop in Milan's fashionable neighborhoods, visit the world's most famous Opera house,
cues.zh: 在米蘭的時尚街區逛逛櫥窗，參觀世界上最著名的歌劇院，

cues.text: and admire a Leonardo masterpiece before relaxing in the 19th-century charm of Lake Como.
cues.en: and admire a Leonardo masterpiece before relaxing in the 19th-century charm of Lake Como.
cues.zh: 欣賞達芬奇的傑作，然後在科莫湖的 19 世紀魅力中放鬆身心。

cues.text: Italy hosts millions of visitors every year, but many miss the highlights of the north.
cues.en: Italy hosts millions of visitors every year, but many miss the highlights of the north.
cues.zh: 義大利每年接待數百萬遊客，但許多人錯過了北部的亮點。

cues.text: In this program, we tour Milano and side trip into the Lake District,
cues.en: In this program, we tour Milano and side trip into the Lake District,
cues.zh: 在這個節目中，我們遊覽米蘭並順便遊覽湖區，

cues.text: exploring my favorite -- Lake Como -- specifically, the towns of Varenna and Bellagio.
cues.en: exploring my favorite -- Lake Como -- specifically, the towns of Varenna and Bellagio.
cues.zh: 探索我最喜歡的——科莫湖——特別是瓦倫納和貝拉吉奧鎮。

cues.text: They say, for every church in Rome, there's a bank in Milan.
cues.en: They say, for every church in Rome, there's a bank in Milan.
cues.zh: 他們說，羅馬有一座教堂，米蘭就有一家銀​​行。

cues.text: Italy's second city, and the capital of the region of Lombardy, Milano is a hardworking, fashion-conscious,
cues.en: Italy's second city, and the capital of the region of Lombardy, Milano is a hardworking, fashion-conscious,
cues.zh: 米蘭是義大利的第二大城市，也是倫巴第大區的首府，是個勤奮、時尚、

cues.text: time-is-money city of nearly a million and a half.
cues.en: time-is-money city of nearly a million and a half.
cues.zh: 時間就是金錢的城市，擁有近百萬人口。

cues.text: And the city is a fascinating melting pot of people and history.
cues.en: And the city is a fascinating melting pot of people and history.
cues.zh: 這座城市是一個令人著迷的人文和歷史的熔爐。

cues.text: Italy recently surpassed Britain in per capita income, and that didn't happen because of its cute Riviera ports
cues.en: Italy recently surpassed Britain in per capita income, and that didn't happen because of its cute Riviera ports
cues.zh: 義大利最近在人均收入方面超過了英國，但這並沒有發生，因為它可愛的裡維埃拉港口

cues.text: and Tuscan hilltowns.
cues.en: and Tuscan hilltowns.
cues.zh: 和托斯卡納山城。

cues.text: The economic success of modern Italy is driven by this city of publicists and pasta power lunches.
cues.en: The economic success of modern Italy is driven by this city of publicists and pasta power lunches.
cues.zh: 現代義大利的經濟成功是由這座城市的公關人員和麵食午餐推動的。

cues.text: Milan is Italy's industrial, banking, publishing, and convention capital.
cues.en: Milan is Italy's industrial, banking, publishing, and convention capital.
cues.zh: 米蘭是義大利的工業、銀行、出版和會議之都。

cues.text: As if making up for its blocky architecture, its people are works of art.
cues.en: As if making up for its blocky architecture, its people are works of art.
cues.zh: 彷彿彌補了其塊狀建築的不足，這裡的人們都是藝術品。

cues.text: Milan is an international fashion center with a refined taste.
cues.en: Milan is an international fashion center with a refined taste.
cues.zh: 米蘭是國際時尚中心，品味高雅。

cues.text: Window displays are gorgeous.
cues.en: Window displays are gorgeous.
cues.zh: 櫥窗展示很華麗。

cues.text: Yet, thankfully, Milan is no more expensive for tourists than other Italian cities.
cues.en: Yet, thankfully, Milan is no more expensive for tourists than other Italian cities.
cues.zh: 然而，值得慶幸的是，米蘭對遊客來說並不比其他義大利城市貴。

cues.text: The importance of Milano is nothing new.
cues.en: The importance of Milano is nothing new.
cues.zh: 米蘭的重要性並不新鮮。

cues.text: Three hundred years before Christ, the Romans called this place Mediolanum,
cues.en: Three hundred years before Christ, the Romans called this place Mediolanum,
cues.zh: 在基督誕生前三百年，羅馬人稱這個地方為Mediolanum，

cues.text: or "the central place." By the 4th century AD, it was the capital of the western half of the Roman Empire.
cues.en: or "the central place." By the 4th century AD, it was the capital of the western half of the Roman Empire.
cues.zh: 或“中心地點”。到公元4世紀，它已成為羅馬帝國西半部的首都。

cues.text: It was from here that Emperor Constantine issued the Edict of Milan,
cues.en: It was from here that Emperor Constantine issued the Edict of Milan,
cues.zh: 康斯坦丁皇帝正是從這裡頒布了米蘭法令，

cues.text: which legalized Christianity in the year 313.
cues.en: which legalized Christianity in the year 313.
cues.zh: 313年使基督教合法化。

cues.text: After struggling through the early Middle Ages, Milan rose to prominence
cues.en: After struggling through the early Middle Ages, Milan rose to prominence
cues.zh: 在經歷了中世紀早期的掙扎後，米蘭崛起

cues.text: under the powerful Visconti and Sforza families.
cues.en: under the powerful Visconti and Sforza families.
cues.zh: 在強大的維斯康提和斯福爾扎家族的統治下。

cues.text: By the time of the Renaissance, the city was called "the new Athens"
cues.en: By the time of the Renaissance, the city was called "the new Athens"
cues.zh: 到文藝復興時期，這座城市被稱為“新雅典”

cues.text: and was enough of a cultural center for Leonardo da Vinci to call home.
cues.en: and was enough of a cultural center for Leonardo da Vinci to call home.
cues.zh: 足以成為達文西稱之為家的文化中心。

cues.text: And then came four centuries of foreign domination -- Spain, Austria, France, and more Austria.
cues.en: And then came four centuries of foreign domination -- Spain, Austria, France, and more Austria.
cues.zh: 然後是四個世紀的外國統治——西班牙、奧地利、法國，還有更多的奧地利。

cues.text: In the 19th century, Milano became a center of revolution
cues.en: In the 19th century, Milano became a center of revolution
cues.zh: 19世紀，米蘭成為革命中心

cues.text: against Austrian rule, and then it helped spearhead the movement for Italian independence and unification.
cues.en: against Austrian rule, and then it helped spearhead the movement for Italian independence and unification.
cues.zh: 反對奧地利統治，然後幫助領導了義大利獨立和統一運動。

cues.text: In the 20th century, Mussolini left a heavy fascist touch on Milan's architecture.
cues.en: In the 20th century, Mussolini left a heavy fascist touch on Milan's architecture.
cues.zh: 20世紀，墨索里尼為米蘭的建築留下了濃厚的法西斯色彩。

cues.text: Il Duce himself made grandiose speeches from these balconies.
cues.en: Il Duce himself made grandiose speeches from these balconies.
cues.zh: 領袖本人就在這些陽臺上發表了宏偉的演講。

cues.text: And Milan's immense train station thunders fascism.
cues.en: And Milan's immense train station thunders fascism.
cues.zh: 米蘭巨大的火車站震懾著法西斯主義。

cues.text: Every time I pass through, I imagine the rush the fascists must have felt on the day in 1931
cues.en: Every time I pass through, I imagine the rush the fascists must have felt on the day in 1931
cues.zh: 每次我經過這裡，我都會想像法西斯主義者在 1931 年的那一天一定感受到的衝擊

cues.text: when the grand renovations of this station were unveiled.
cues.en: when the grand renovations of this station were unveiled.
cues.zh: 當這個車站的宏偉改造揭幕時。

cues.text: It's designed to make you feel small, too small to question Mussolini
cues.en: It's designed to make you feel small, too small to question Mussolini
cues.zh: 它的目的是讓你感覺自己很渺小，渺小到無法質疑墨索里尼

cues.text: and his government's right wing agenda.
cues.en: and his government's right wing agenda.
cues.zh: 以及他的政府的右翼議程。

cues.text: Mussolini's excesses led to the bombing of Milan in World War II.
cues.en: Mussolini's excesses led to the bombing of Milan in World War II.
cues.zh: 墨索里尼的暴行導致了第二次世界大戰中米蘭的轟炸。

cues.text: But Milan rose again.
cues.en: But Milan rose again.
cues.zh: 但米蘭再次崛起。

cues.text: The 1959 Pirelli Tower was a trendsetter.
cues.en: The 1959 Pirelli Tower was a trendsetter.
cues.zh: 1959 年的倍耐力大樓 (Pirelli Tower) 引領了潮流。

cues.text: Today, Milan is dynamic and a commercial powerhouse.
cues.en: Today, Milan is dynamic and a commercial powerhouse.
cues.zh: 如今，米蘭充滿活力，是個商業強國。

cues.text: The city's centerpiece is its magnificent Duomo, or cathedral -- the fourth-largest in Europe.
cues.en: The city's centerpiece is its magnificent Duomo, or cathedral -- the fourth-largest in Europe.
cues.zh: 這座城市的中心是宏偉的大教堂－歐洲第四大教堂。

cues.text: Back in the 14th century, when Europe was fragmented into countless little independent states,
cues.en: Back in the 14th century, when Europe was fragmented into countless little independent states,
cues.zh: 早在14世紀，當歐洲分裂成無數獨立的小國時，

cues.text: the dukes of Milan wanted to impress their German and French counterparts.
cues.en: the dukes of Milan wanted to impress their German and French counterparts.
cues.zh: 米蘭公爵想要給德國和法國同行留下深刻的印象。

cues.text: To earn their respect, they built this huge and richly ornamented cathedral.
cues.en: To earn their respect, they built this huge and richly ornamented cathedral.
cues.zh: 為了贏得他們的尊重，他們建造了這座巨大且裝飾華麗的大教堂。

cues.text: Even though the Renaissance style, with its domes and rounded arches, was in vogue elsewhere in Italy,
cues.en: Even though the Renaissance style, with its domes and rounded arches, was in vogue elsewhere in Italy,
cues.zh: 儘管帶有圓頂和圓形拱門的文藝復興風格在義大利其他地方很流行，

cues.text: conservative Milano stuck with the Gothic style.
cues.en: conservative Milano stuck with the Gothic style.
cues.zh: 保守的米蘭堅持哥德式風格。

cues.text: The dukes, thinking Northerners could relate better to Gothic, loaded it with pointed spires and arches.
cues.en: The dukes, thinking Northerners could relate better to Gothic, loaded it with pointed spires and arches.
cues.zh: 公爵們認為北方人更容易接受哥德式建築，因此在哥德式建築上安裝了尖頂和拱門。

cues.text: And everything's made of marble.
cues.en: And everything's made of marble.
cues.zh: 一切都是大理石製成的。

cues.text: The statues on the tips of the many spires seem so relaxed,
cues.en: The statues on the tips of the many spires seem so relaxed,
cues.zh: 眾多尖塔尖上的雕像顯得如此輕鬆，

cues.text: like they're just hanging out, waiting for their big day.
cues.en: like they're just hanging out, waiting for their big day.
cues.zh: 就像他們只是閒逛，等待他們的大日子。

cues.text: The fanciful gargoyles, functioning as drain spouts, are especially imaginative.
cues.en: The fanciful gargoyles, functioning as drain spouts, are especially imaginative.
cues.zh: 奇特的石像鬼，充當排水管，特別有想像。

cues.text: The church is a good example of the flamboyant, or "flamelike," overdone final stage of Gothic.
cues.en: The church is a good example of the flamboyant, or "flamelike," overdone final stage of Gothic.
cues.zh: 這座教堂是哥德式風格最後階段華麗或「火焰般」過度的一個很好的例子。

cues.text: Step inside, and you're struck by the immensity of the place.
cues.en: Step inside, and you're struck by the immensity of the place.
cues.zh: 走進去，你就會被這個地方的廣闊震撼。

cues.text: The soaring ceiling is supported by sequoia-sized pillars.
cues.en: The soaring ceiling is supported by sequoia-sized pillars.
cues.zh: 高聳的天花板由紅杉大小的柱子支撐。

cues.text: Started in 1386 and not finished until 1810,
cues.en: Started in 1386 and not finished until 1810,
cues.zh: 1386年開始，直到1810年才完成，

cues.text: this construction project originated the phrase Italians use to say "never-ending":
cues.en: this construction project originated the phrase Italians use to say "never-ending":
cues.zh: 這個建設專案起源於義大利人所說的「永無止境」：

cues.text: "like building a cathedral." Much of the brilliantly colored stained glass
cues.en: "like building a cathedral." Much of the brilliantly colored stained glass
cues.zh: 「就像建造一座大教堂。」大部分色彩鮮豔的彩色玻璃

cues.text: dates from about 1500.
cues.en: dates from about 1500.
cues.zh: 其歷史可追溯至約 1500 年。

cues.text: So does the fine inlaid marble floor.
cues.en: So does the fine inlaid marble floor.
cues.zh: 精美鑲嵌的大理石地板也是。

cues.text: After 500 years of wear, you can tell that the black marble is harder than the rest.
cues.en: After 500 years of wear, you can tell that the black marble is harder than the rest.
cues.zh: 經過 500 年的磨損，您可以看出黑色大理石比其他大理石更硬。

cues.text: A grotesque 16th-century statue of St. Bartolomeo, a martyr skinned alive by the Romans,
cues.en: A grotesque 16th-century statue of St. Bartolomeo, a martyr skinned alive by the Romans,
cues.zh: 一座 16 世紀的聖巴爾託洛梅奧 (St. Bartolomeo) 雕像，他是一位被羅馬人活剝皮的烈士，

cues.text: wears his skin like a robe.
cues.en: wears his skin like a robe.
cues.zh: 他的皮膚就像一件長袍。

cues.text: You can actually see his limp feet and dangling face.
cues.en: You can actually see his limp feet and dangling face.
cues.zh: 你實際上可以看到他無力的雙腳和晃來晃去的臉。

cues.text: It was sculpted by a student of Leonardo, who obviously picked up
cues.en: It was sculpted by a student of Leonardo, who obviously picked up
cues.zh: 它是由列奧納多的一名學生雕刻的，他顯然學到了

cues.text: his master's passion for the human anatomy.
cues.en: his master's passion for the human anatomy.
cues.zh: 他的老師對人體解剖學的熱情。

cues.text: Cap your visit with a trip to the rooftop.
cues.en: Cap your visit with a trip to the rooftop.
cues.zh: 以屋頂之旅結束您的訪問。

cues.text: Walking through its forest of pinnacles and statues, you enjoy great views of the church's statuary,
cues.en: Walking through its forest of pinnacles and statues, you enjoy great views of the church's statuary,
cues.zh: 漫步在尖塔和雕像的森林中，您可以欣賞到教堂雕像的美景，

cues.text: as well as of the city.
cues.en: as well as of the city.
cues.zh: 以及城市的。

cues.text: And, crowning the cathedral, a golden Virgin Mary overlooks everything.
cues.en: And, crowning the cathedral, a golden Virgin Mary overlooks everything.
cues.zh: 在大教堂的頂上，一尊金色的聖母瑪利亞俯視著一切。

cues.text: "La Madonnina," as she's affectionately called, is an icon of Milano.
cues.en: "La Madonnina," as she's affectionately called, is an icon of Milano.
cues.zh: 她被親切地稱為“La Madonnina”，是米蘭的象徵。

cues.text: Milan's main square is a classic European scene
cues.en: Milan's main square is a classic European scene
cues.zh: 米蘭的主廣場是經典的歐洲場景

cues.text: and a popular local gathering point.
cues.en: and a popular local gathering point.
cues.zh: 和一個受歡迎的當地聚集點。

cues.text: The statue features Victor Emmanuel II, first king of Italy.
cues.en: The statue features Victor Emmanuel II, first king of Italy.
cues.zh: 這座雕像的主角是義大利第一位國王維克託·伊曼紐二世。

cues.text: He's looking at the grand gallery named for him.
cues.en: He's looking at the grand gallery named for him.
cues.zh: 他正在看著以他命名的大畫廊。

cues.text: The words above the triumphal arch entrance read: "To Victor Emmanuel II, from the people of Milano."
cues.en: The words above the triumphal arch entrance read: "To Victor Emmanuel II, from the people of Milano."
cues.zh: 凱旋門入口上方寫著：“米蘭人民致維克託·伊曼紐爾二世。”

cues.text: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele is the pride of the city.
cues.en: The Galleria Vittorio Emanuele is the pride of the city.
cues.zh: 維托里奧埃馬努埃萊長廊是這座城市的驕傲。

cues.text: Built during the heady days of Italian unification, around 1870, it was the first building in town
cues.en: Built during the heady days of Italian unification, around 1870, it was the first building in town
cues.zh: 它建於 1870 年左右義大利統一的鼎盛時期，是鎮上的第一座建築

cues.text: to have electric lighting.
cues.en: to have electric lighting.
cues.zh: 有電照明。

cues.text: Its art celebrates the establishment of Italy as an independent country.
cues.en: Its art celebrates the establishment of Italy as an independent country.
cues.zh: 它的藝術慶祝義大利作為一個獨立國家的建立。

cues.text: Around the central dome, mosaics symbolize the four major continents.
cues.en: Around the central dome, mosaics symbolize the four major continents.
cues.zh: 中央穹頂周圍的馬賽克圖案象徵著四大洲。

cues.text: The mosaic floor is also patriotic.
cues.en: The mosaic floor is also patriotic.
cues.zh: 馬賽克地板也很愛國。

cues.text: The She-wolf with Romulus and Remus honors Rome, the national capital.
cues.en: The She-wolf with Romulus and Remus honors Rome, the national capital.
cues.zh: 母狼與羅慕路斯和雷穆斯向國家首都羅馬致敬。

cues.text: A favorite is the torino, or "little bull." While it represents the city of Torino,
cues.en: A favorite is the torino, or "little bull." While it represents the city of Torino,
cues.zh: 最喜歡的是都靈，或「小公牛」。雖然它代表了都靈市，

cues.text: for locals, it's a source of good luck.
cues.en: for locals, it's a source of good luck.
cues.zh: 對當地人來說，這是好運的泉源。

cues.text: They can't resist stepping on his little testicles.
cues.en: They can't resist stepping on his little testicles.
cues.zh: 他們忍不住踩著他的小睪丸。

cues.text: Locals claim it works better if you give it a spin.
cues.en: Locals claim it works better if you give it a spin.
cues.zh: 當地人聲稱，如果你嘗試一下，效果會更好。

cues.text: Milan's immense Sforza Castle tells the story of the city in brick.
cues.en: Milan's immense Sforza Castle tells the story of the city in brick.
cues.zh: 米蘭巨大的斯福爾扎城堡用磚塊講述了這座城市的故事。

cues.text: It guarded the gate to the city wall and defended the ruling family
cues.en: It guarded the gate to the city wall and defended the ruling family
cues.zh: 它守護著城牆的大門，保衛著統治家族

cues.text: from threats both foreign and domestic.
cues.en: from threats both foreign and domestic.
cues.zh: 免受國內外威脅。

cues.text: In the 1500s, the entire city was circled by state-of-the-art walls,
cues.en: In the 1500s, the entire city was circled by state-of-the-art walls,
cues.zh: 在1500年代，整個城市被最先進的城牆包圍，

cues.text: of which this castle was a key element.
cues.en: of which this castle was a key element.
cues.zh: 這座城堡是其中的關鍵元素。

cues.text: It's apparent from the enormity of this fortification that Milano was a strategic prize.
cues.en: It's apparent from the enormity of this fortification that Milano was a strategic prize.
cues.zh: 從這座防禦工事的巨大程度可以看出，米蘭是個戰略戰利品。

cues.text: While the town walls are long gone, this massive castle survives, leaving the city
cues.en: While the town walls are long gone, this massive castle survives, leaving the city
cues.zh: 雖然城牆早已不復存在，但這座巨大的城堡倖存下來，離開了城市

cues.text: with an inviting and well-used public space.
cues.en: with an inviting and well-used public space.
cues.zh: 擁有誘人且使用良好的公共空間。

cues.text: Locals and tourists alike enjoy strolling its expansive grounds.
cues.en: Locals and tourists alike enjoy strolling its expansive grounds.
cues.zh: 當地人和遊客都喜歡在廣闊的土地上漫步。

cues.text: A short tram ride takes you to a different kind of public place --
cues.en: A short tram ride takes you to a different kind of public place --
cues.zh: 搭乘短程電車即可帶您前往不同型別的公共場所—

cues.text: Milan's Monumental Cemetery.
cues.en: Milan's Monumental Cemetery.
cues.zh: 米蘭紀念公墓。

cues.text: While there are many evocative cemeteries in Europe, this one -- with its emotional portrayals
cues.en: While there are many evocative cemeteries in Europe, this one -- with its emotional portrayals
cues.zh: 雖然歐洲有許多令人回味的墓地，但這個墓地充滿了情感描寫

cues.text: of the departed and their heavenly escorts -- in the melodramatic art styles
cues.en: of the departed and their heavenly escorts -- in the melodramatic art styles
cues.zh: 逝者與他們的天堂護衛－以情節劇的藝術風格

cues.text: from the late 19th and early 20th centuries -- is in a class by itself.
cues.en: from the late 19th and early 20th centuries -- is in a class by itself.
cues.zh: 19世紀末20世紀初－自成一類。

cues.text: It's a vast garden art gallery of proud busts and grim reapers,
cues.en: It's a vast garden art gallery of proud busts and grim reapers,
cues.zh: 這是一座巨大的花園藝術畫廊，裡面有驕傲的半身像和死神，

cues.text: heartbroken angels and weeping widows.
cues.en: heartbroken angels and weeping widows.
cues.zh: 傷心欲絕的天使和哭泣的寡婦。

cues.text: Soldiers too young to die.
cues.en: Soldiers too young to die.
cues.zh: 士兵太年輕，不能死。

cues.text: Acres of grief, hope, and memories.
cues.en: Acres of grief, hope, and memories.
cues.zh: 充滿悲傷、希望和回憶。

cues.text: The grand, pedestrianized Via Dante leads from the Sforza Castle
cues.en: The grand, pedestrianized Via Dante leads from the Sforza Castle
cues.zh: 宏偉的但丁步行街從斯福爾扎城堡延伸出來

cues.text: toward the town center and the cathedral.
cues.en: toward the town center and the cathedral.
cues.zh: 朝向市中心和大教堂。

cues.text: It was carved out of a medieval tangle of streets to celebrate Italian unification.
cues.en: It was carved out of a medieval tangle of streets to celebrate Italian unification.
cues.zh: 它是在中世紀混亂的街道上雕刻而成的，以慶祝義大利的統一。

cues.text: Because of that, the facades lining it are relatively new -- dating from the late 1800s.
cues.en: Because of that, the facades lining it are relatively new -- dating from the late 1800s.
cues.zh: 正因為如此，它的外牆相對較新——可以追溯到 1800 年代末。

cues.text: Over the vigorous complaints of merchants, the street became traffic-free in 1995.
cues.en: Over the vigorous complaints of merchants, the street became traffic-free in 1995.
cues.zh: 在商家的強烈投訴下，這條街於1995年禁止車輛通行。

cues.text: Today, those merchants would have it no other way.
cues.en: Today, those merchants would have it no other way.
cues.zh: 如今，那些商人別無他法。

cues.text: Fashionistas love Milan's world-class shopping zone, a neighborhood called the Quadrilateral.
cues.en: Fashionistas love Milan's world-class shopping zone, a neighborhood called the Quadrilateral.
cues.zh: 時尚達人喜愛米蘭的世界級購物區，名為「四邊形」的街區。

cues.text: This elegant high-fashion district was the original Beverly Hills of Milan.
cues.en: This elegant high-fashion district was the original Beverly Hills of Milan.
cues.zh: 這個優雅的高階時裝區是最初的米蘭比佛利山莊。

cues.text: Overseeing the shopping action are the exclusive and elusive penthouse apartments
cues.en: Overseeing the shopping action are the exclusive and elusive penthouse apartments
cues.zh: 獨特而難以捉摸的頂層公寓監督著購物活動

cues.text: with their plush roof gardens.
cues.en: with their plush roof gardens.
cues.zh: 及其豪華的屋頂花園。

cues.text: Since the 1920s, this has been the place for designer labels.
cues.en: Since the 1920s, this has been the place for designer labels.
cues.zh: 自 1920 年代以來，這裡一直是設計師品牌的聚集地。

cues.text: In this scene, the people-watching is as entertaining as the window-shopping.
cues.en: In this scene, the people-watching is as entertaining as the window-shopping.
cues.zh: 在這個場景中，觀看行人就像逛街一樣有趣。

cues.text: For edible fashion, check out one of Milan's gourmet delis like Peck.
cues.en: For edible fashion, check out one of Milan's gourmet delis like Peck.
cues.zh: 若想品嚐時尚美食，不妨前往 Peck 等米蘭的美食熟食店之一。

cues.text: If ever you wanted to have a picnic meal and not save money, buy it here.
cues.en: If ever you wanted to have a picnic meal and not save money, buy it here.
cues.zh: 如果您想野餐但又不想省錢，請在這裡購買。

cues.text: Everything's impeccable, from the staff to the lavish displays.
cues.en: Everything's impeccable, from the staff to the lavish displays.
cues.zh: 從工作人員到奢華的展示，一切都無可挑剔。

cues.text: The busy kitchen is like a gourmet assembly line.
cues.en: The busy kitchen is like a gourmet assembly line.
cues.zh: 忙碌的廚房就像一條美食流水線。

cues.text: Posh markets like this serve fine food to both Milan's busy professionals
cues.en: Posh markets like this serve fine food to both Milan's busy professionals
cues.zh: 像這樣的豪華市場為米蘭忙碌的專業人士提供美味佳餚

cues.text: and its well-to-do.
cues.en: and its well-to-do.
cues.zh: 以及它的富裕。

cues.text: And if you're spending half your budget on a picnic, you might as well ride the elevator into the cellar
cues.en: And if you're spending half your budget on a picnic, you might as well ride the elevator into the cellar
cues.zh: 如果你把一半的預算花在野餐上，不妨搭電梯進入地窖

cues.text: for a bottle of wine to match.
cues.en: for a bottle of wine to match.
cues.zh: 來一瓶與之相配的葡萄酒。

cues.text: Catering to people with good taste and more money than time,
cues.en: Catering to people with good taste and more money than time,
cues.zh: 迎合有品味、金錢比時間多的人，

cues.text: places like this put an elegant twist on fast food.
cues.en: places like this put an elegant twist on fast food.
cues.zh: 像這樣的地方為快餐增添了優雅的氣息。

cues.text: 500 years ago, Leonardo da Vinci contributed to the city's reputation for design and aesthetics.
cues.en: 500 years ago, Leonardo da Vinci contributed to the city's reputation for design and aesthetics.
cues.zh: 500 年前，達文西 (Leonardo da Vinci) 為這座城市的設計和美學聲譽做出了貢獻。

cues.text: In fact, Leonardo's identified with Milan more than any other Italian city.
cues.en: In fact, Leonardo's identified with Milan more than any other Italian city.
cues.zh: 事實上，李奧納多對米蘭的認同感超過了其他義大利城市。

cues.text: This is where he spent some of his most productive years, enjoying the generous patronage of the Sforza family.
cues.en: This is where he spent some of his most productive years, enjoying the generous patronage of the Sforza family.
cues.zh: 他在這裡度過了他最富有成效的歲月，享受了斯福爾扎家族的慷慨贊助。

cues.text: Leonardo was the epitome of a Renaissance genius.
cues.en: Leonardo was the epitome of a Renaissance genius.
cues.zh: 列奧納多是文藝復興時期天才的縮影。

cues.text: That means he was well-rounded -- he was a painter and sculptor.
cues.en: That means he was well-rounded -- he was a painter and sculptor.
cues.zh: 這意味著他是一位多才多藝的人——他是一位畫家和雕塑家。

cues.text: He was also a musician, scientist, engineer, architect -- you name it.
cues.en: He was also a musician, scientist, engineer, architect -- you name it.
cues.zh: 他還是一位音樂家、科學家、工程師、建築師──凡是你能想到的。

cues.text: He did everything, and he did it well.
cues.en: He did everything, and he did it well.
cues.zh: 他什麼都做了，而且做得很好。

cues.text: This statue celebrates the many ways Leonardo contributed to the city of Milan
cues.en: This statue celebrates the many ways Leonardo contributed to the city of Milan
cues.zh: 這座雕像慶祝了萊昂納多對米蘭市做出的多種貢獻

cues.text: during the years he lived here.
cues.en: during the years he lived here.
cues.zh: 他住在這裡的那些年。

cues.text: The reliefs recall Leonardo's varied professional triumphs.
cues.en: The reliefs recall Leonardo's varied professional triumphs.
cues.zh: 這些浮雕讓人回想起李奧納多的各種職業成就。

cues.text: Leonardo, wearing his hydroengineer hat here, re-engineered Milan's canal system, complete with locks.
cues.en: Leonardo, wearing his hydroengineer hat here, re-engineered Milan's canal system, complete with locks.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多在這裡戴著水利工程師的帽子，重新設計了米蘭的運河系統，並安裝了船閘。

cues.text: Until the 1920s, Milan was one of Italy's major ports,
cues.en: Until the 1920s, Milan was one of Italy's major ports,
cues.zh: 直到 1920 年代，米蘭一直是義大利的主要港口之一，

cues.text: with canals connecting the city to the Po river and to the Mediterranean beyond.
cues.en: with canals connecting the city to the Po river and to the Mediterranean beyond.
cues.zh: 運河將城市與波河和遠處的地中海連線起來。

cues.text: And Leonardo designed the largest equestrian monument in the world,
cues.en: And Leonardo designed the largest equestrian monument in the world,
cues.zh: 萊昂納多設計了世界上最大的馬術紀念碑，

cues.text: again, for the Sforza family.
cues.en: again, for the Sforza family.
cues.zh: 再次，為斯福爾扎家族。

cues.text: Though the original was destroyed in 1499 by invading French troops who used it for target practice,
cues.en: Though the original was destroyed in 1499 by invading French troops who used it for target practice,
cues.zh: 儘管原件於 1499 年被入侵的法國軍隊摧毀，當時法國軍隊將其用於打靶練習，

cues.text: the giant horse was rebuilt in 1999 by the American artist Charles Dent,
cues.en: the giant horse was rebuilt in 1999 by the American artist Charles Dent,
cues.zh: 這匹巨馬由美國藝術家查爾斯·登特於1999年重建，

cues.text: from Leonardo's drawings.
cues.en: from Leonardo's drawings.
cues.zh: 出自列奧納多的畫作。
