3uTmcG7CgdI.title: How do animals regrow their limbs? And why can't humans do it? - Jessica Whited
3uTmcG7CgdI.speaker: TED-Ed
3uTmcG7CgdI.zh: 【TED-Ed】動物如何重新長出四肢？而人類為什麼做不到呢？ - 傑西卡懷特（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: For some animals, losing a limb is a decidedly permanent affair.
cues.en: For some animals, losing a limb is a decidedly permanent affair.
cues.zh: 對於某些動物來說，斷肢 是永久且無法改變的事。

cues.text: But for salamanders, particularly axolotls, amputation is just a temporary affliction.
cues.en: But for salamanders, particularly axolotls, amputation is just a temporary affliction.
cues.zh: 但對於蠑螈而言， 特別是墨西哥鈍口螈， 斷肢只是種暫時性的麻煩。

cues.text: Not only can they grow back entire limbs in as little as six weeks,
cues.en: Not only can they grow back entire limbs in as little as six weeks,
cues.zh: 牠們不僅可以在短短六週內 就把斷掉的部分完全長回來，

cues.text: they can also regenerate heart and even brain tissue.
cues.en: they can also regenerate heart and even brain tissue.
cues.zh: 牠們不僅可以在短短六週內 就把斷掉的部分完全長回來， 連心臟，甚至大腦組織都可以再生。

cues.text: So how does this astonishing adaptation work?
cues.en: So how does this astonishing adaptation work?
cues.zh: 這種驚人的適應機制是如何運作的？

cues.text: Regardless of regeneration, every limbed creature had to grow their arms and legs at some point.
cues.en: Regardless of regeneration, every limbed creature had to grow their arms and legs at some point.
cues.zh: 先不談再生， 每一種有四肢的生物 都會在某個時點長出手腳來。

cues.text: And whether that process starts in the womb or the world, it almost always begins with little bumps called limb buds.
cues.en: And whether that process starts in the womb or the world, it almost always begins with little bumps called limb buds.
cues.zh: 無論這個過程是從子宮裡 就開始還是出世後才開始， 幾乎都始於一種小突起，叫做肢芽。

cues.text: These buds are full of progenitor cells— a cornucopia of cell types that can differentiate into various tissues,
cues.en: These buds are full of progenitor cells— a cornucopia of cell types that can differentiate into various tissues,
cues.zh: 肢芽裡面滿是先驅細胞， 也就是可以分化成各種組織的 多種型別的細胞，

cues.text: including muscles, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons.
cues.en: including muscles, cartilage, ligaments, and tendons.
cues.zh: 包括肌肉、軟骨、韌帶，和肌腱。

cues.text: Some of these progenitors are stem cells, capable of developing into a range of specialized cells and tissues,
cues.en: Some of these progenitors are stem cells, capable of developing into a range of specialized cells and tissues,
cues.zh: 有一些先驅細胞是幹細胞， 能夠發展成多種 專門化的細胞和組織，

cues.text: while others are merely derived from stem cells.
cues.en: while others are merely derived from stem cells.
cues.zh: 其他的則只是由幹細胞衍生出來的。

cues.text: But in either case, the progenitors differentiate and multiply rapidly
cues.en: But in either case, the progenitors differentiate and multiply rapidly
cues.zh: 但不論是哪一種先驅細胞， 都會隨著肢芽的發展 而快速分化和增殖。

cues.text: as the limb bud develops.
cues.en: as the limb bud develops.
cues.zh: 而快速分化和增殖。

cues.text: Nerves grow into the limb from nearby cell bodies and a network of blood vessels form which fuel the process with oxygen.
cues.en: Nerves grow into the limb from nearby cell bodies and a network of blood vessels form which fuel the process with oxygen.
cues.zh: 神經會從附近的細胞體 生長到四肢裡面， 還會形成血管網路， 為這個過程提供氧氣。

cues.text: Eventually, that tiny bud grows into a full infant limb.
cues.en: Eventually, that tiny bud grows into a full infant limb.
cues.zh: 最終，小芽長大成為 完整的新生四肢。

cues.text: Most salamanders, including axolotls, develop their limbs in the same way.
cues.en: Most salamanders, including axolotls, develop their limbs in the same way.
cues.zh: 大部分的蠑螈，包括墨西哥鈍口螈， 用同樣的方式長出牠們的肢體。

cues.text: But unlike other animals, they can also start this process all over again
cues.en: But unlike other animals, they can also start this process all over again
cues.zh: 但和其他動物不同的是， 如果有需要，牠們可以 一而再再而三啟動這個過程。

cues.text: if they need to.
cues.en: if they need to.
cues.zh: 如果有需要，牠們可以 一而再再而三啟動這個過程。

cues.text: When salamanders lose a limb, surrounding skin cells quickly surge across the wound’s surface.
cues.en: When salamanders lose a limb, surrounding skin cells quickly surge across the wound’s surface.
cues.zh: 蠑螈失去一肢時， 周圍的皮膚細胞 會迅速覆蓋傷口表面。

cues.text: This new layer of skin is called the wound epidermis,
cues.en: This new layer of skin is called the wound epidermis,
cues.zh: 這層新的皮膚稱為傷口表皮，

cues.text: and once established, it signals cells in the underlying limb stump
cues.en: and once established, it signals cells in the underlying limb stump
cues.zh: 形成之後，它會傳送訊號 給皮膚下殘肢中的細胞，

cues.text: to undergo something called dedifferentiation.
cues.en: to undergo something called dedifferentiation.
cues.zh: 進行一個叫做「去分化」的過程。

cues.text: This process reverts nearby cells from fully developed limb tissues
cues.en: This process reverts nearby cells from fully developed limb tissues
cues.zh: 這個過程會將附近的細胞還原， 從發展完成的肢體組織 回復到較早期、尚未分化成 有專門功能的先驅細胞。

cues.text: back into earlier, less specialized progenitor cells.
cues.en: back into earlier, less specialized progenitor cells.
cues.zh: 這個過程會將附近的細胞還原， 從發展完成的肢體組織 回復到較早期、尚未分化成 有專門功能的先驅細胞。

cues.text: At the same time, the peripheral nervous system fires up stem cells
cues.en: At the same time, the peripheral nervous system fires up stem cells
cues.zh: 同時， 周邊神經系統會啟動 蠑螈全身的幹細胞。

cues.text: throughout the salamander’s body.
cues.en: throughout the salamander’s body.
cues.zh: 周邊神經系統會啟動 蠑螈全身的幹細胞。

cues.text: This would be impossible for most multicellular organisms, whose stem cells typically lose their regenerative capacity with age.
cues.en: This would be impossible for most multicellular organisms, whose stem cells typically lose their regenerative capacity with age.
cues.zh: 大部分的多細胞生物 都做不到這一點， 牠們的幹細胞通常會 隨著年齡失去再生能力。

cues.text: But when salamander stem cells near the injury get the right signal,
cues.en: But when salamander stem cells near the injury get the right signal,
cues.zh: 但當蠑螈傷口附近的幹細胞 接收到對的訊號時，

cues.text: they reactivate and start multiplying.
cues.en: they reactivate and start multiplying.
cues.zh: 它們會重新啟動並開始增殖。

cues.text: Researchers don’t know what ratio of stem cells and dedifferentiated progenitor cells regeneration requires.
cues.en: Researchers don’t know what ratio of stem cells and dedifferentiated progenitor cells regeneration requires.
cues.zh: 研究人員還不知道再生需要 多少比例的幹細胞 和去分化先驅細胞。

cues.text: But we do know these cells come together to form the most important part of the process: the blastema.
cues.en: But we do know these cells come together to form the most important part of the process: the blastema.
cues.zh: 但我們確實知道 這些細胞結合起來形成 這個過程中最重要的部分： 胚基。

cues.text: This structure is almost identical to a limb bud— the primary difference is that it’s made of recycled, repurposed cells,
cues.en: This structure is almost identical to a limb bud— the primary difference is that it’s made of recycled, repurposed cells,
cues.zh: 它的結構和肢芽幾乎一模一樣—— 主要的差別在於胚基 是回收後再利用的細胞所構成，

cues.text: and potentially reserved cells, rather than completely new ones.
cues.en: and potentially reserved cells, rather than completely new ones.
cues.zh: 以及可能被儲備下來的細胞， 而不是全新的細胞。

cues.text: Beyond that, blastemas and limb buds have the same mission:
cues.en: Beyond that, blastemas and limb buds have the same mission:
cues.zh: 除了這個差異，胚基 和肢芽都具有相同的任務：

cues.text: to make thousands of new cells and organize them into the muscle, bone, skin, and nerve tissue
cues.en: to make thousands of new cells and organize them into the muscle, bone, skin, and nerve tissue
cues.zh: 製造數千個新細胞，並將它們組織 成為有功能的四肢需要的肌肉、 骨頭、皮膚，及神經組織。

cues.text: required for a functional limb.
cues.en: required for a functional limb.
cues.zh: 成為有功能的四肢需要的肌肉、 骨頭、皮膚，及神經組織。

cues.text: As this process unfolds, nerves and blood vessels spanning the injury site
cues.en: As this process unfolds, nerves and blood vessels spanning the injury site
cues.zh: 隨著這個過程發展， 分佈在受傷部位的神經和血管

cues.text: transmit nutrition and oxygen.
cues.en: transmit nutrition and oxygen.
cues.zh: 會遞送營養和氧氣。

cues.text: Over several weeks, the stump will steadily grow a miniature limb with translucent skin.
cues.en: Over several weeks, the stump will steadily grow a miniature limb with translucent skin.
cues.zh: 在幾週內，殘肢會穩定地 長出小型肢體， 帶有透明的皮膚。

cues.text: And when the process is complete, not only will the limb match the rest of the salamander,
cues.en: And when the process is complete, not only will the limb match the rest of the salamander,
cues.zh: 此過程完成後， 重新長出來的腳 不僅能匹配蠑螈的其他部位，

cues.text: there won't even be a scar.
cues.en: there won't even be a scar.
cues.zh: 還不會留下疤痕。

cues.text: The relationship between scarring and regeneration is just one of this processes’ many mysteries.
cues.en: The relationship between scarring and regeneration is just one of this processes’ many mysteries.
cues.zh: 形成疤痕和再生之間的關係 只是這個過程的許多奧秘之一。

cues.text: Scientists are still tracking salamander cells on the molecular level
cues.en: Scientists are still tracking salamander cells on the molecular level
cues.zh: 科學家仍在從分子層面 追蹤蠑螈的細胞，

cues.text: to determine how they revert from a mature stage into a regenerative one.
cues.en: to determine how they revert from a mature stage into a regenerative one.
cues.zh: 以確定這些細胞如何 從成熟階段回復到再生階段。

cues.text: And research into transplanting blastema cells investigates how other animals might replicate this reconstructive wizardry.
cues.en: And research into transplanting blastema cells investigates how other animals might replicate this reconstructive wizardry.
cues.zh: 移植胚基細胞的研究所探究的是 其他動物要如何複製這種重建奇蹟。

cues.text: We also don’t understand how salamanders’ bodies know what part of the limb has been lost or how much needs to be regrown.
cues.en: We also don’t understand how salamanders’ bodies know what part of the limb has been lost or how much needs to be regrown.
cues.zh: 我們也不明白蠑螈的身體怎麼會知道 斷掉的是腳的哪個部分 或者需要重新生長多少。 ［左臂：施工中］

cues.text: One theory is that blastema cells have a form of positional memory,
cues.en: One theory is that blastema cells have a form of positional memory,
cues.zh: ［左臂：施工中］ 有種理論認為胚基細胞 具有某種形式的位置記憶，

cues.text: allowing them to determine how much to grow in relation to one another.
cues.en: allowing them to determine how much to grow in relation to one another.
cues.zh: 讓它們能夠根據彼此的比例， 確定該生長多少。

cues.text: And it’s equally important to understand how these limbs know when to stop growing
cues.en: And it’s equally important to understand how these limbs know when to stop growing
cues.zh: 同等重要的是：要了解 這些肢體怎麼知道何時該停止生長，

cues.text: to prevent overdevelopment, like in cancerous tumors.
cues.en: to prevent overdevelopment, like in cancerous tumors.
cues.zh: 以預防過度生長， 如癌症的腫瘤細胞那樣。

cues.text: But one of regenerations essential ingredients doesn’t belong solely
cues.en: But one of regenerations essential ingredients doesn’t belong solely
cues.zh: 但再生的要件—— 胚基——並非蠑螈獨有。

cues.text: to salamanders: the blastema.
cues.en: to salamanders: the blastema.
cues.zh: 胚基——並非蠑螈獨有。

cues.text: Deer antlers use a similar healing tissue to regenerate each year,
cues.en: Deer antlers use a similar healing tissue to regenerate each year,
cues.zh: 鹿角就會使用類似的 癒合組織每年再生，

cues.text: even though their skin scars like ours.
cues.en: even though their skin scars like ours.
cues.zh: 不過鹿的皮膚和我們的 一樣會留下疤痕。

cues.text: Spiny mice can also restore skin, hair, and some other appendages scar-free.
cues.en: Spiny mice can also restore skin, hair, and some other appendages scar-free.
cues.zh: 棘鼠也可以讓皮膚、毛髮，及其他 一些凸出於軀幹外的部位復元， 且不留下疤痕。

cues.text: And even humans can regenerate the tips of our fingers and toes
cues.en: And even humans can regenerate the tips of our fingers and toes
cues.zh: 就連人類的 指尖和趾尖也可以 用非常類似的方式再生，

cues.text: in a surprisingly similar manner.
cues.en: in a surprisingly similar manner.
cues.zh: 指尖和趾尖也可以 用非常類似的方式再生，

cues.text: We still don’t know whether this ability is tied to our shared ancestry with salamanders
cues.en: We still don’t know whether this ability is tied to our shared ancestry with salamanders
cues.zh: 我們還不知道這種能力是來自於 我們和蠑螈的共同祖先，

cues.text: or fueled by distinct biological mechanisms.
cues.en: or fueled by distinct biological mechanisms.
cues.zh: 或者是由不同的生物機制所驅動。

cues.text: But with time and research, who knows what evolutionary knowledge we might grow back.
cues.en: But with time and research, who knows what evolutionary knowledge we might grow back.
cues.zh: 但隨時間和研究， 誰又知道我們可能會 長回哪些進化知識。

Qog18tiNnqg.title: What creates a total solar eclipse? - Andy Cohen
Qog18tiNnqg.speaker: TED-Ed
Qog18tiNnqg.zh: 【TED-Ed】是什麼造成了日全食？ ——安迪·科恩（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: On August 21, 2017 the shadow of the Moon will pass from the west coast to the east coast of the U.S.
cues.en: On August 21, 2017 the shadow of the Moon will pass from the west coast to the east coast of the U.S.
cues.zh: 2017 年 8 月 21 日 月亮的陰影會橫掃美國 從西岸到東岸

cues.text: Our blue sky will turn black as night and fill with stars, and there will be a hole in the sky
cues.en: Our blue sky will turn black as night and fill with stars, and there will be a hole in the sky
cues.zh: 我們的藍天會變得像晚上一樣黑 還會有滿天星斗 同時天空中也會出現一個洞

cues.text: where the Sun used to be, surrounded by the fiery ring of the Sun's corona,
cues.en: where the Sun used to be, surrounded by the fiery ring of the Sun's corona,
cues.zh: 就是太陽之前的位置 會被日冕形成的火環所圍繞

cues.text: a total eclipse of the Sun.
cues.en: a total eclipse of the Sun.
cues.zh: 這就是日全食

cues.text: This will truly be a historic event.
cues.en: This will truly be a historic event.
cues.zh: 這就是日全食 這將會是一個歷史性事件 關於日食的紀錄

cues.text: Accounts of solar eclipses date way back on the written record.
cues.en: Accounts of solar eclipses date way back on the written record.
cues.zh: 關於日食的紀錄 可以追溯回古時史書

cues.text: The early Mesopotamians wrote that the Sun was put to shame during the solar eclipse of the 14th century B.C.E.
cues.en: The early Mesopotamians wrote that the Sun was put to shame during the solar eclipse of the 14th century B.C.E.
cues.zh: 可以追溯回古時史書 早期的美索不達米亞人寫道： 太陽蒙羞了 西元前第十四世紀的一場日食

cues.text: and it may have started the Sun worship of the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.
cues.en: and it may have started the Sun worship of the Egyptian pharaoh Akhenaten.
cues.zh: 西元前第十四世紀的一場日食 可能是導致 埃及法老阿肯那頓太陽膜拜的開端

cues.text: Ancient Chinese astrologers paid with their lives if they failed to predict the solar eclipse
cues.en: Ancient Chinese astrologers paid with their lives if they failed to predict the solar eclipse
cues.zh: 古代的中國占星術士如果漏報了日食 或無法預示皇帝的命兆 是要賠上性命的

cues.text: and portend the fate of their emperors whose symbol was the Sun.
cues.en: and portend the fate of their emperors whose symbol was the Sun.
cues.zh: 是要賠上性命的 因為太陽就是皇帝的象徵

cues.text: The earliest date of a specific event in human history, a battle between the armies of Lydia and Media,
cues.en: The earliest date of a specific event in human history, a battle between the armies of Lydia and Media,
cues.zh: 因為太陽就是皇帝的象徵 人類史上最早記載日期的特定事件 為利底亞與米底亞之間的戰爭 發生於西元前 535 年 5 月 28 日

cues.text: occurred on May 28, 535 B.C.E.
cues.en: occurred on May 28, 535 B.C.E.
cues.zh: 發生於西元前 535 年 5 月 28 日

cues.text: when a solar eclipse caused the soldiers to lay down their arms and declare a truce.
cues.en: when a solar eclipse caused the soldiers to lay down their arms and declare a truce.
cues.zh: 發生於西元前 535 年 5 月 28 日 當時發生的日食造成 士兵棄械並宣告停戰

cues.text: So how does it happen?
cues.en: So how does it happen?
cues.zh: 那日食是怎麼形成的？

cues.text: During a total solar eclipse, the Moon moves between the Earth and the Sun.
cues.en: During a total solar eclipse, the Moon moves between the Earth and the Sun.
cues.zh: 當日全食發生時 月球執行到地球與太陽之間

cues.text: When this happens, the disc of the Moon appears to perfectly cover the disc of the Sun
cues.en: When this happens, the disc of the Moon appears to perfectly cover the disc of the Sun
cues.zh: 而且月球的盤面 看起來完全擋住太陽

cues.text: even though the Sun is much larger than the Moon.
cues.en: even though the Sun is much larger than the Moon.
cues.zh: 看起來完全擋住太陽 即使太陽比月球大很多

cues.text: But how is this possible?
cues.en: But how is this possible?
cues.zh: 但這怎麼可能？

cues.text: The Sun is 400 times bigger than the Moon, but by sheer coincidence, the Moon is 390 times closer to Earth.
cues.en: The Sun is 400 times bigger than the Moon, but by sheer coincidence, the Moon is 390 times closer to Earth.
cues.zh: 太陽比月球大了 400 倍 但是就有這麼巧 月球到地球的距離 比日地距離近 390 倍

cues.text: Size and distance cancel each other out so that the Moon and Sun appear to be almost the exactly same size.
cues.en: Size and distance cancel each other out so that the Moon and Sun appear to be almost the exactly same size.
cues.zh: 尺寸及距離的效應互相抵銷 因此月球與太陽看起來 大小幾乎相同

cues.text: Every time the Moon orbits the Earth, once every 27.3 days,
cues.en: Every time the Moon orbits the Earth, once every 27.3 days,
cues.zh: 大小幾乎相同 每次月球繞地球公轉 一圈 27.3 天

cues.text: it has to pass between the Earth and the Sun, a stage called the new moon phase.
cues.en: it has to pass between the Earth and the Sun, a stage called the new moon phase.
cues.zh: 它總會穿過地球與太陽之間一次 這時期稱做新月

cues.text: And every time it passes, the New Moon has a chance to block out the Sun.
cues.en: And every time it passes, the New Moon has a chance to block out the Sun.
cues.zh: 每次它穿過 新月就有機會擋住太陽

cues.text: Most of the time, the Moon passes a little above or a little below the Sun,
cues.en: Most of the time, the Moon passes a little above or a little below the Sun,
cues.zh: 大部分的時間 月球穿過的位置 可能比太陽高一點或低一點

cues.text: but if they align perfectly, the shadow of the Moon will make a narrow path across Earth
cues.en: but if they align perfectly, the shadow of the Moon will make a narrow path across Earth
cues.zh: 但如果它們完全對齊 月球的陰影 就會在地球上掃出一條狹長的食帶

cues.text: and those in the shadows will see a total solar eclipse.
cues.en: and those in the shadows will see a total solar eclipse.
cues.zh: 只有在食帶中的人才能看到日全食

cues.text: Just like on night side of the Earth, the sky during a total eclipse is black
cues.en: Just like on night side of the Earth, the sky during a total eclipse is black
cues.zh: 就像地球在夜晚那側一般 天空在日全食期間是黑暗的

cues.text: and filled with stars.
cues.en: and filled with stars.
cues.zh: 並可見滿天星斗

cues.text: But while the moon perfectly covers the surface of the Sun, it doesn't block out the Sun's outer atmosphere,
cues.en: But while the moon perfectly covers the surface of the Sun, it doesn't block out the Sun's outer atmosphere,
cues.zh: 並可見滿天星斗 但是就算月球完全遮蓋 太陽的表面 它也擋不住太陽的大氣層

cues.text: its corona, which appears as a fiery ring around the dark disc of the moon.
cues.en: its corona, which appears as a fiery ring around the dark disc of the moon.
cues.zh: 即日冕，看起來就像一圈火環 在月球暗影的外圍

cues.text: Solar eclipses occur several times a year, but most often they are partial eclipses
cues.en: Solar eclipses occur several times a year, but most often they are partial eclipses
cues.zh: 一年會發生好幾次日食 但多數情況是日偏食

cues.text: where the Moon doesn't quite line up with the Sun.
cues.en: where the Moon doesn't quite line up with the Sun.
cues.zh: 也就是月球與太陽並非完全對齊

cues.text: And, when the Moon and Sun are perfectly aligned, the Moon is usually too far from Earth in its orbit
cues.en: And, when the Moon and Sun are perfectly aligned, the Moon is usually too far from Earth in its orbit
cues.zh: 再者，有時月球與太陽排成一直線時 月球在公轉軌道上的位置 離地球太遠

cues.text: to completely cover the Sun, creating an annular eclipse.
cues.en: to completely cover the Sun, creating an annular eclipse.
cues.zh: 月球在公轉軌道上的位置 離地球太遠 無法完全遮蓋太陽 就會發生日環食

cues.text: During an annular or partial eclipse, the sky remains bright.
cues.en: During an annular or partial eclipse, the sky remains bright.
cues.zh: 就會發生日環食 在日環食或日偏食發生時 天空依然明亮

cues.text: Even on those rare occasions of a total eclipse, the Moon's shadow is most likely to fall
cues.en: Even on those rare occasions of a total eclipse, the Moon's shadow is most likely to fall
cues.zh: 天空依然明亮 即使是很罕見的日全食 月球的陰影最有可能落在 佔地球 70% 的海面上

cues.text: on the 70% of Earth that is covered by water, and few people, if any, will see it.
cues.en: on the 70% of Earth that is covered by water, and few people, if any, will see it.
cues.zh: 佔地球 70% 的海面上 所以只有極少數人有幸能見到此奇景

cues.text: The eclipse of 2017 will be remarkable on a larger scale because the Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.
cues.en: The eclipse of 2017 will be remarkable on a larger scale because the Moon is slowly moving away from Earth.
cues.zh: 所以只有極少數人有幸能見到此奇景 2017 年的日食很值得注意， 因為長久來看 月球正逐漸遠離地球

cues.text: If a furry ancestor of ours had bothered to look up during a solar eclipse a hundred million years ago,
cues.en: If a furry ancestor of ours had bothered to look up during a solar eclipse a hundred million years ago,
cues.zh: 月球正逐漸遠離地球 如果我們有著毛皮的祖先願意費神 在幾億年前的一場日食中抬頭仰望

cues.text: it wouldn't have seen the fiery corona of the Sun.
cues.en: it wouldn't have seen the fiery corona of the Sun.

cues.text: Caffeine evolved in plants where it serves a few purposes.
cues.en: Caffeine evolved in plants where it serves a few purposes.
cues.zh: 所以它如何使我們醒著呢 咖啡因在植物中演化 扮演著幾個角色

cues.text: In high doses, as it's found in the leaves and seeds of certain species,
cues.en: In high doses, as it's found in the leaves and seeds of certain species,
cues.zh: 咖啡因在植物中演化 扮演著幾個角色 高劑量咖啡因 如同在某些物種的 葉子及種子中能找到的

cues.text: it's toxic to insects.
cues.en: it's toxic to insects.
cues.zh: 如同在某些物種的 葉子及種子中能找到的 對昆蟲有毒性

cues.text: But when they consume it in lower doses, as it's found in nectar,
cues.en: But when they consume it in lower doses, as it's found in nectar,
cues.zh: 對昆蟲有毒性 但當牠們攝取低劑量時 如同花蜜中能找到的

cues.text: it can actually help them remember and revisit flowers.
cues.en: it can actually help them remember and revisit flowers.
cues.zh: 但當牠們攝取低劑量時 如同花蜜中能找到的 咖啡因實際上可以幫助牠們 記住並重返花朵

cues.text: In the human body, caffeine acts as a stimulant for the central nervous system.
cues.en: In the human body, caffeine acts as a stimulant for the central nervous system.
cues.zh: 在人體內，咖啡因作為一種 中樞神經興奮劑

cues.text: It keeps us awake by blocking one of the body's key sleep-inducing molecules,
cues.en: It keeps us awake by blocking one of the body's key sleep-inducing molecules,
cues.zh: 在人體內，咖啡因作為一種 中樞神經興奮劑 它藉由阻斷體內其中一種 誘發睡眠的關鍵分子而使我們醒著

cues.text: a substance called adenosine.
cues.en: a substance called adenosine.
cues.zh: 它藉由阻斷體內其中一種 誘發睡眠的關鍵分子而使我們醒著 一種叫做腺苷的物質

cues.text: Your body needs a constant supply of energy, which it gets by breaking down a high-energy molecule called ATP.
cues.en: Your body needs a constant supply of energy, which it gets by breaking down a high-energy molecule called ATP.
cues.zh: 一種叫做腺苷的物質 你的身體需要穩定的能量供應 藉由分解一種叫三磷酸腺核苷 的高能分子而得到

cues.text: In the process, it liberates adenosine, ATP's chemical backbone.
cues.en: In the process, it liberates adenosine, ATP's chemical backbone.
cues.zh: 藉由分解一種叫三磷酸腺核苷 的高能分子而得到 在過程中 它釋出腺苷 就是 ATP 的化學結構骨架

cues.text: Neurons in your brain have receptors perfectly tailored to this molecule.
cues.en: Neurons in your brain have receptors perfectly tailored to this molecule.
cues.zh: 它釋出腺苷 就是 ATP 的化學結構骨架 你腦中的神經元 有為這種分子量身打造的受體

cues.text: When adenosine docks to these receptors, it activates a cascade of biochemical reactions
cues.en: When adenosine docks to these receptors, it activates a cascade of biochemical reactions
cues.zh: 你腦中的神經元 有為這種分子量身打造的受體 當腺苷停泊於受體時 它會活化一連串的生化反應

cues.text: that cause neurons to fire more sluggishly and slow the release of important brain-signaling molecules.
cues.en: that cause neurons to fire more sluggishly and slow the release of important brain-signaling molecules.
cues.zh: 它會活化一連串的生化反應 使得神經元較慵懶地放電 並減緩重要大腦傳訊分子的釋放

cues.text: In other words, you get sleepy.
cues.en: In other words, you get sleepy.
cues.zh: 並減緩重要大腦傳訊分子的釋放 換句話說，你會感到想睡

cues.text: Caffeine is what's called an adenosine receptor antagonist.
cues.en: Caffeine is what's called an adenosine receptor antagonist.
cues.zh: 換句話說，你會感到想睡 咖啡因是所謂的腺苷受體拮抗劑

cues.text: That means it derails this process of slowing your neurons down
cues.en: That means it derails this process of slowing your neurons down
cues.zh: 咖啡因是所謂的腺苷受體拮抗劑 意思是咖啡因會藉由阻斷腺苷受體 來阻止使神經元變遲緩的過程

cues.text: by blocking adenosine receptors.
cues.en: by blocking adenosine receptors.
cues.zh: 來阻止使神經元變遲緩的過程

cues.text: Caffeine and adenosine have a similar molecular structure, close enough that caffeine can wedge into the adenosine receptors,
cues.en: Caffeine and adenosine have a similar molecular structure, close enough that caffeine can wedge into the adenosine receptors,
cues.zh: 咖啡因和腺苷有相似的分子結構 接近到咖啡因可以卡進腺苷受體中

cues.text: but not close enough to activate them.
cues.en: but not close enough to activate them.
cues.zh: 接近到咖啡因可以卡進腺苷受體中 但沒有接近到能夠活化受體

cues.text: To summarize, adenosine inhibits your neurons.
cues.en: To summarize, adenosine inhibits your neurons.
cues.zh: 總結來說，腺苷抑制你的神經元

cues.text: Caffeine inhibits the inhibitor, so it stimulates you.
cues.en: Caffeine inhibits the inhibitor, so it stimulates you.
cues.zh: 咖啡因抑制了抑制劑，所以它刺激你

cues.text: Caffeine can also boost positive feelings.
cues.en: Caffeine can also boost positive feelings.
cues.zh: 咖啡因抑制了抑制劑，所以它刺激你 咖啡因也能促進正向的感覺

cues.text: In some neurons, the adenosine receptors are linked to receptors for another molecule called dopamine.
cues.en: In some neurons, the adenosine receptors are linked to receptors for another molecule called dopamine.
cues.zh: 在某些神經元中 腺苷受體與另一種叫 多巴胺的分子之受體連線

cues.text: One of dopamine's roles in the brain is to promote feelings of pleasure.
cues.en: One of dopamine's roles in the brain is to promote feelings of pleasure.
cues.zh: 腺苷受體與另一種叫 多巴胺的分子之受體連線 多巴胺在腦中的其中一個角色 是提升愉悅感

cues.text: When adenosine docks in one of these paired receptors, that can make it harder for dopamine to fit in its own spot,
cues.en: When adenosine docks in one of these paired receptors, that can make it harder for dopamine to fit in its own spot,
cues.zh: 當腺苷停泊在這些 成對受體中的一個時 會使多巴胺較難結合到自己的位置上

cues.text: interrupting its mood-lifting work.
cues.en: interrupting its mood-lifting work.
cues.zh: 會使多巴胺較難結合到自己的位置上 便幹擾了它提升心情的作用

cues.text: But when caffeine takes adenosine's place, it doesn't have the same effect,
cues.en: But when caffeine takes adenosine's place, it doesn't have the same effect,
cues.zh: 便幹擾了它提升心情的作用 但當咖啡因取代腺苷的位置時 它不會有相同的作用

cues.text: and dopamine can slide in.
cues.en: and dopamine can slide in.
cues.zh: 但當咖啡因取代腺苷的位置時 它不會有相同的作用 並且多巴胺可以滑進來

cues.text: There's evidence that caffeine's effects on adenosine and dopamine receptors
cues.en: There's evidence that caffeine's effects on adenosine and dopamine receptors
cues.zh: 有證據顯示咖啡因 對腺苷和多巴胺受體的作用

cues.text: can have long-term benefits, too, reducing the risk of diseases
cues.en: can have long-term benefits, too, reducing the risk of diseases
cues.zh: 也可能對於減少某些疾病 有長期的益處

cues.text: like Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and some types of cancer.
cues.en: like Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and some types of cancer.
cues.zh: 像是帕金森氏症、阿茲海默症 和某些型別的癌症

cues.text: Caffeine can also ramp up the body's ability to burn fat.
cues.en: Caffeine can also ramp up the body's ability to burn fat.
cues.zh: 咖啡因也能提升身體燃燒脂肪的能力

cues.text: In fact, some sports organizations think that caffeine gives athletes an unfair advantage
cues.en: In fact, some sports organizations think that caffeine gives athletes an unfair advantage
cues.zh: 咖啡因也能提升身體燃燒脂肪的能力 事實上，有些運動協會認為 咖啡因給予運動員不公平的優勢

cues.text: and have placed limits on its consumption.
cues.en: and have placed limits on its consumption.
cues.zh: 咖啡因給予運動員不公平的優勢 並已對咖啡因的使用設下限制

cues.text: From 1972 until 2004, Olympic athletes had to stay below a certain blood-caffeine concentration
cues.en: From 1972 until 2004, Olympic athletes had to stay below a certain blood-caffeine concentration
cues.zh: 並已對咖啡因的使用設下限制 從 1972 年到 2004 年 奧運選手的血中咖啡因 必須保持在某特定濃度之下

cues.text: to compete.
cues.en: to compete.
cues.zh: 奧運選手的血中咖啡因 必須保持在某特定濃度之下 才能比賽

cues.text: Of course, not all of caffeine's effects are so helpful.
cues.en: Of course, not all of caffeine's effects are so helpful.
cues.zh: 才能比賽 當然咖啡因的作用不全是有幫助的

cues.text: It might make you feel better and more alert, but it can also raise your heart rate and blood pressure,
cues.en: It might make you feel better and more alert, but it can also raise your heart rate and blood pressure,
cues.zh: 當然咖啡因的作用不全是有幫助的 它可能會讓你感覺較好，並較警覺 但它也能升高你的心率和血壓

cues.text: cause increased urination or diarrhea, and contribute to insomnia and anxiety.
cues.en: cause increased urination or diarrhea, and contribute to insomnia and anxiety.
cues.zh: 造成多尿或腹瀉 並引起失眠和焦慮

cues.text: Plus, the foods and beverages caffeine is found in have their own impacts on your body that have to be taken into account.
cues.en: Plus, the foods and beverages caffeine is found in have their own impacts on your body that have to be taken into account.
cues.zh: 並引起失眠和焦慮 此外，含有咖啡因的食物和飲料 它們本身對你身體的影響 也必須列入考慮

cues.text: Your brain can adapt to regular consumption of caffeine.
cues.en: Your brain can adapt to regular consumption of caffeine.
cues.zh: 它們本身對你身體的影響 也必須列入考慮 你的大腦可以適應規律的咖啡因攝取

cues.text: If your adenosine receptors are perpetually clogged, your body will manufacture extra ones.
cues.en: If your adenosine receptors are perpetually clogged, your body will manufacture extra ones.
cues.zh: 你的大腦可以適應規律的咖啡因攝取 如果你的腺苷受體被長期堵塞 你的身體會額外製造

cues.text: That way, even with caffeine around, adenosine can still do its job of signaling the brain to power down.
cues.en: That way, even with caffeine around, adenosine can still do its job of signaling the brain to power down.
cues.zh: 你的身體會額外製造 這樣一來，即使有咖啡因存在 腺苷還是能做它傳訊 使大腦省電的工作

cues.text: That's why you may find you need to consume more and more caffeine
cues.en: That's why you may find you need to consume more and more caffeine
cues.zh: 腺苷還是能做它傳訊 使大腦省電的工作 這就是為什麼你可能會發覺 你需要消耗越來越多的咖啡因 以感受到相同的警覺

cues.text: to feel as alert.
cues.en: to feel as alert.
cues.zh: 以感受到相同的警覺

cues.text: There are more and more adenosine receptors to block.
cues.en: There are more and more adenosine receptors to block.
cues.zh: 以感受到相同的警覺 有越來越多的腺苷受體需要被阻斷

cues.text: It's also why if you suddenly quit caffeine, you may experience an unpleasant withdrawal.
cues.en: It's also why if you suddenly quit caffeine, you may experience an unpleasant withdrawal.
cues.zh: 有越來越多的腺苷受體需要被阻斷 這也是為什麼 如果你突然戒掉咖啡因 你可能會經歷一段不舒服的退癮

cues.text: With plenty of receptors and no competition, adenosine can work overtime,
cues.en: With plenty of receptors and no competition, adenosine can work overtime,
cues.zh: 你可能會經歷一段不舒服的退癮 有著許多受體，並且沒有競爭者 腺苷可能加班

cues.text: causing symptoms like headaches, tiredness, and depressed moods.
cues.en: causing symptoms like headaches, tiredness, and depressed moods.
cues.zh: 腺苷可能加班 造成症狀如頭痛 疲倦 和憂鬱的心情

cues.text: But in a few days, the extra adenosine receptors will disappear,
cues.en: But in a few days, the extra adenosine receptors will disappear,
cues.zh: 但幾天後，多餘的腺苷受體就會消失

cues.text: your body will readjust, and you'll feel just as alert as ever,
cues.en: your body will readjust, and you'll feel just as alert as ever,
cues.zh: 但幾天後，多餘的腺苷受體就會消失 你的身體會重新調整 然後你會感覺像從前一樣警覺

cues.text: even without an infusion of the world's most popular stimulant.
cues.en: even without an infusion of the world's most popular stimulant.
cues.zh: 然後你會感覺像從前一樣警覺 即使沒有注入全世界 最受歡迎的興奮劑

foVMwJtlR5s.title: What is déjà vu? What is déjà vu? - Michael Molina
foVMwJtlR5s.speaker: TED-Ed
foVMwJtlR5s.zh: 【TED-Ed】什麼是似曾相識？什麼是似曾相識？ ——麥可‧莫利納（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Have you experienced déjà vu?
cues.en: Have you experienced déjà vu?
cues.zh: 曾對生活中的場景產生既視感嗎？

cues.text: It's that shadowy feeling you get when a situation seems familiar.
cues.en: It's that shadowy feeling you get when a situation seems familiar.
cues.zh: 身邊出現的人事物隱約地 讓你感到似曾相識

cues.text: A scene in a restaurant plays out exactly as you remember.
cues.en: A scene in a restaurant plays out exactly as you remember.
cues.zh: 讓你感到似曾相識 例如餐廳內出現一個場景 和你記憶中某個片段不謀而合

cues.text: The world moves like a ballet you've choreographed, but the sequence can't be based on a past experience
cues.en: The world moves like a ballet you've choreographed, but the sequence can't be based on a past experience
cues.zh: 和你記憶中某個片段不謀而合 像整個世界跳起了芭蕾 而你就是編舞者 但你對這一切毫無經驗 因為你從未在這裡吃過飯

cues.text: because you've never eaten here before.
cues.en: because you've never eaten here before.
cues.zh: 因為你從未在這裡吃過飯

cues.text: This is the first time you've had clams, so what's going on?
cues.en: This is the first time you've had clams, so what's going on?
cues.zh: 在這之前你也沒嘗過蛤蜊 究竟是怎麼回事？

cues.text: Unfortunately, there isn't one single explanation for déjà vu.
cues.en: Unfortunately, there isn't one single explanation for déjà vu.
cues.zh: 究竟是怎麼回事？ 可惜目前無法完整解釋這個現象

cues.text: The experience is brief and occurs without notice, making it nearly impossible for scientists to record and study it.
cues.en: The experience is brief and occurs without notice, making it nearly impossible for scientists to record and study it.
cues.zh: 這感覺來得快 去得也快 使得科學家幾乎無法 記錄並研究它

cues.text: Scientists can't simply sit around and wait for it to happen to them -- this could take years.
cues.en: Scientists can't simply sit around and wait for it to happen to them -- this could take years.
cues.zh: 總不能讓科學家整天不事生產 靜待生活中出現似曾相識的場景 說不定得花上數年光陰

cues.text: It has no physical manifestations and in studies, it's described by the subject as a sensation or feeling.
cues.en: It has no physical manifestations and in studies, it's described by the subject as a sensation or feeling.
cues.zh: 說不定得花上數年光陰 沒有具體的證據 人們也總是把這現象歸類為 一種感官上的知覺

cues.text: Because of this lack of hard evidence, there's been a surplus of speculation over the years.
cues.en: Because of this lack of hard evidence, there's been a surplus of speculation over the years.
cues.zh: 正因為沒有鐵證 多年來充斥著各式臆測

cues.text: Since Emile Boirac introduced déjà vu as a French term meaning "already seen,"
cues.en: Since Emile Boirac introduced déjà vu as a French term meaning "already seen,"
cues.zh: 自從法國科學家艾米爾．布拉克 將既視感定義為似曾相識起

cues.text: more than 40 theories attempt to explain this phenomenon.
cues.en: more than 40 theories attempt to explain this phenomenon.
cues.zh: 將既視感定義為似曾相識起 超過 40 種理論希望能 解釋這個現象

cues.text: Still, recent advancements in neuroimaging and cognitive psychology
cues.en: Still, recent advancements in neuroimaging and cognitive psychology
cues.zh: 然而近來神經造影以及 認知心理學的發達限縮了

cues.text: narrow down the field of prospects.
cues.en: narrow down the field of prospects.
cues.zh: 認知心理學的發達限縮了 既視感成因的可能性

cues.text: Let's walk through three of today's more prevalent theories, using the same restaurant setting for each.
cues.en: Let's walk through three of today's more prevalent theories, using the same restaurant setting for each.
cues.zh: 讓我們來瞧瞧 三種目前最普遍的說法吧 皆套用前面餐廳的假設

cues.text: First up is dual processing.
cues.en: First up is dual processing.
cues.zh: 首先是雙歷程理論

cues.text: We'll need an action.
cues.en: We'll need an action.
cues.zh: 首先是雙歷程理論 用一個動作來解釋

cues.text: Let's go with a waiter dropping a tray of dishes.
cues.en: Let's go with a waiter dropping a tray of dishes.
cues.zh: 用一個動作來解釋 服務生打翻了一堆碗盤

cues.text: As the scene unfolds, your brain's hemispheres process a flurry of information:
cues.en: As the scene unfolds, your brain's hemispheres process a flurry of information:
cues.zh: 服務生打翻了一堆碗盤 隨著畫面出現 你的大腦開始處理 一連串的資訊

cues.text: the waiter's flailing arms, his cry for help, the smell of pasta.
cues.en: the waiter's flailing arms, his cry for help, the smell of pasta.
cues.zh: 服務生揮舞雙臂 他大聲求援 義大利麵的香味

cues.text: Within milliseconds, this information zips through pathways and is processed into a single moment.
cues.en: Within milliseconds, this information zips through pathways and is processed into a single moment.
cues.zh: 在千分之一秒內 這個訊息快速穿梭於大腦中 最後合為一個瞬間的動作

cues.text: Most of the time, everything is recorded in-sync.
cues.en: Most of the time, everything is recorded in-sync.
cues.zh: 最後合為一個瞬間的動作 大腦通常會同步記錄訊息

cues.text: However, this theory asserts that déjà vu occurs when there's a slight delay
cues.en: However, this theory asserts that déjà vu occurs when there's a slight delay
cues.zh: 然而這個理論主張 若有資訊在腦中出現了些微延誤

cues.text: in information from one of these pathways.
cues.en: in information from one of these pathways.
cues.zh: 既視感便油然而生

cues.text: The difference in arrival times causes the brain to interpret the late information
cues.en: The difference in arrival times causes the brain to interpret the late information
cues.zh: 既視感便油然而生 訊息抵達的時間差 使大腦將前後的資訊解讀成 不同的事件

cues.text: as a separate event.
cues.en: as a separate event.
cues.zh: 不同的事件

cues.text: When it plays over the already-recorded moment, it feels as if it's happened before
cues.en: When it plays over the already-recorded moment, it feels as if it's happened before
cues.zh: 當大腦播放已存在的記憶 感覺就像發生過了一樣

cues.text: because, in a sense, it has.
cues.en: because, in a sense, it has.
cues.zh: 感覺就像發生過了一樣 某種情況而言，的確如此

cues.text: Our next theory deals with a confusion of the past rather than a mistake in the present.
cues.en: Our next theory deals with a confusion of the past rather than a mistake in the present.
cues.zh: 下個理論與記憶的混淆有關 而非當下的錯誤

cues.text: This is the hologram theory, and we'll use that tablecloth to examine it.
cues.en: This is the hologram theory, and we'll use that tablecloth to examine it.
cues.zh: 這就是全息理論 我們用這張桌布來檢視它

cues.text: As you scan its squares, a distant memory swims up from deep within your brain.
cues.en: As you scan its squares, a distant memory swims up from deep within your brain.
cues.zh: 你細看上頭的格紋 一段模糊的回憶 從大腦深處浮現

cues.text: According to the theory, this is because memories are stored in the form of holograms,
cues.en: According to the theory, this is because memories are stored in the form of holograms,
cues.zh: 從大腦深處浮現 根據這個理論 記憶在腦中是以 全息圖的形式儲存

cues.text: and in holograms, you only need one fragment to see the whole picture.
cues.en: and in holograms, you only need one fragment to see the whole picture.
cues.zh: 在全息圖中 只需要一小部分 便能窺見全域性 你的大腦認出了這張桌布

cues.text: Your brain has identified the tablecloth with one from the past, maybe from your grandmother's house.

VqXnN_FQfrc.title: What Causes Lightning?
VqXnN_FQfrc.speaker: NOAA SciJinks
VqXnN_FQfrc.zh: 【NOAA SciJinks】閃電產生的原因是什麼？（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: What Causes Lightning?
cues.en: What Causes Lightning?
cues.zh: 閃電產生的原因是什麼？

cues.text: Lightning can be a beautiful—and scary—part of Earth’s weather.
cues.en: Lightning can be a beautiful—and scary—part of Earth’s weather.
cues.zh: 閃電是地球天氣中美麗又可怕的一部分。

cues.text: You probably have seen lightning in a thunderstorm, but do you know why lightning happens?
cues.en: You probably have seen lightning in a thunderstorm, but do you know why lightning happens?
cues.zh: 你可能在雷暴雨中見過閃電，但你知道為什麼會發生閃電嗎？

cues.text: Lightning comes from electrical charges that build up within a storm cloud.
cues.en: Lightning comes from electrical charges that build up within a storm cloud.
cues.zh: 閃電來自暴風雨雲中積聚的電荷。

cues.text: Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises high into the atmosphere.
cues.en: Thunderstorms form when warm, moist air rises high into the atmosphere.
cues.zh: 當溫暖潮濕的空氣上升到大氣中時，雷暴就會形成。

cues.text: This rising air is called an updraft.
cues.en: This rising air is called an updraft.
cues.zh: 這種上升的空氣稱為上升氣流。

cues.text: As air rises in the atmosphere, clouds form when water vapor in the air cools into water
cues.en: As air rises in the atmosphere, clouds form when water vapor in the air cools into water
cues.zh: 當空氣在大氣中上升時，空氣中的水蒸氣冷卻成水就會形成雲

cues.text: drops, called cloud droplets.
cues.en: drops, called cloud droplets.
cues.zh: 水滴，稱為雲滴。

cues.text: Some cloud droplets freeze into ice crystals.
cues.en: Some cloud droplets freeze into ice crystals.
cues.zh: 有些雲滴凍結成冰晶。

cues.text: These cloud droplets and ice crystals collide and form larger particles, called graupel.
cues.en: These cloud droplets and ice crystals collide and form larger particles, called graupel.
cues.zh: 這些雲滴和冰晶碰撞並形成更大的顆粒，稱為霰。

cues.text: As the ice crystals rise up, they collide with the larger and heavier graupel.
cues.en: As the ice crystals rise up, they collide with the larger and heavier graupel.
cues.zh: 當冰晶上升時，它們與更大、更重的霰粒碰撞。

cues.text: These collisions result in positively and negatively charged particles.
cues.en: These collisions result in positively and negatively charged particles.
cues.zh: 這些碰撞產生帶正電和帶負電的粒子。

cues.text: Ice crystals are small and light.
cues.en: Ice crystals are small and light.
cues.zh: 冰晶小而輕。

cues.text: The updraft carries the positively charged ice crystals higher and higher into the cloud.
cues.en: The updraft carries the positively charged ice crystals higher and higher into the cloud.
cues.zh: 上升氣流將帶正電的冰晶帶到雲中越來越高的位置。

cues.text: The thunderstorm cloud is mostly negatively charged, which causes a mostly positive charge
cues.en: The thunderstorm cloud is mostly negatively charged, which causes a mostly positive charge
cues.zh: 雷暴雲大部分帶負電，這會導致大部分帶正電

cues.text: to form on the ground.
cues.en: to form on the ground.
cues.zh: 在地面上形成。

cues.text: When these opposite charges become strong enough, there is an electrical discharge—an
cues.en: When these opposite charges become strong enough, there is an electrical discharge—an
cues.zh: 當這些相反的電荷變得足夠強時，就會發生放電——

cues.text: energy release—in the form of lightning.
cues.en: energy release—in the form of lightning.
cues.zh: 能量釋放－以閃電的形式。

cues.text: Lightning often connects the negative charges in the cloud to positive charges on the ground.
cues.en: Lightning often connects the negative charges in the cloud to positive charges on the ground.
cues.zh: 閃電經常將雲中的負電荷與地面上的正電荷連線起來。

cues.text: This is called cloud-to-ground lightning.
cues.en: This is called cloud-to-ground lightning.
cues.zh: 這稱為雲對地閃電。

cues.text: Why does lightning often hit trees, telephone poles, or other tall structures first?
cues.en: Why does lightning often hit trees, telephone poles, or other tall structures first?
cues.zh: 為什麼閃電經常先擊中樹木、電線桿或其他高層建築？

cues.text: Trees and telephone poles are often the tallest objects on the ground.
cues.en: Trees and telephone poles are often the tallest objects on the ground.
cues.zh: 樹木和電線桿通常是地面上最高的物體。

cues.text: So, they are closest to the storm cloud and the first thing in the path of lightning.
cues.en: So, they are closest to the storm cloud and the first thing in the path of lightning.
cues.zh: 因此，它們距離風暴雲最近，也是閃電路徑上的第一個東西。

cues.text: Lightning can also stay within a cloud or even travel between two clouds.
cues.en: Lightning can also stay within a cloud or even travel between two clouds.
cues.zh: 閃電也可以停留在雲層內，甚至可以在兩層雲層之間傳播。

cues.text: This happens when lightning travels from a negative charge in one cloud to a positive
cues.en: This happens when lightning travels from a negative charge in one cloud to a positive
cues.zh: 當閃電從一朵雲中的負電荷傳播到正電荷時，就會發生這種情況

cues.text: charge within another cloud.
cues.en: charge within another cloud.
cues.zh: 在另一個雲中充電。

cues.text: This is known as intra-cloud lightning.
cues.en: This is known as intra-cloud lightning.
cues.zh: 這被稱為雲內閃電。

cues.text: By the time you see lightning in the sky, a storm is probably already underway in your
cues.en: By the time you see lightning in the sky, a storm is probably already underway in your
cues.zh: 當你看到天空中的閃電時，風暴可能已經在你的身邊發生了。

cues.text: neighborhood.
cues.en: neighborhood.
cues.zh: 鄰裡。

cues.text: But tracking lightning from space can help meteorologists predict the intensity of a
cues.en: But tracking lightning from space can help meteorologists predict the intensity of a
cues.zh: 但是從太空追蹤閃電可以幫助氣象學家預測閃電的強度

cues.text: storm.
cues.en: storm.
cues.zh: 風暴。

cues.text: NOAA’s GOES-R series weather satellites captured this imagery of lightning during
cues.en: NOAA’s GOES-R series weather satellites captured this imagery of lightning during
cues.zh: NOAA 的 GOES-R 系列氣象衛星在

cues.text: a series of thunderstorms over the Midwestern United States.
cues.en: a series of thunderstorms over the Midwestern United States.
cues.zh: 美國中西部上空發生一系列雷暴。

cues.text: Imagery and information from these satellites help forecasters to predict the intensity
cues.en: Imagery and information from these satellites help forecasters to predict the intensity
cues.zh: 來自這些衛星的影象和資訊幫助預報員預測強度

cues.text: of a storm and whether or not the storm will produce high winds or tornadoes.
cues.en: of a storm and whether or not the storm will produce high winds or tornadoes.
cues.zh: 風暴的發生以及風暴是否會產生強風或龍捲風。

cues.text: Find out more about Earth’s weather at NOAA SciJinks!
cues.en: Find out more about Earth’s weather at NOAA SciJinks!
cues.zh: 在 NOAA SciJinks 中瞭解更多有關地球天氣的資訊！

cues.text: It's a bit contentious but we're going to be hearing a lot about it.
cues.en: It's a bit contentious but we're going to be hearing a lot about it.
cues.zh: 這有點有爭議，但我們會聽到很多關於它的訊息。

cues.text: It's called CDR.
cues.en: It's called CDR.
cues.zh: 這就是所謂的CDR。

cues.text: So carbon dioxide removal.
cues.en: So carbon dioxide removal.
cues.zh: 從而去除二氧化碳。

cues.text: What we want to do is put that carbon back where it belongs.
cues.en: What we want to do is put that carbon back where it belongs.
cues.zh: 我們想要做的就是將碳放回它所屬的地方。

cues.text: Giana Amador is a CDR advocate and she's going to help us explain this with the bathtub metaphor.
cues.en: Giana Amador is a CDR advocate and she's going to help us explain this with the bathtub metaphor.
cues.zh: Giana Amador 是 CDR 的倡導者，她將用浴缸的比喻來幫助我們解釋這一點。

cues.text: The bathtub in this situation is our atmosphere and the water in the bathtub is the CO2
cues.en: The bathtub in this situation is our atmosphere and the water in the bathtub is the CO2
cues.zh: 在這種情況下，浴缸就是我們的大氣，浴缸裡的水就是二氧化碳

cues.text: that's in our atmosphere.
cues.en: that's in our atmosphere.
cues.zh: 這就是我們的氣氛。

cues.text: Before the Industrial Revolution the land and ocean typically released as much CO2 into the air
cues.en: Before the Industrial Revolution the land and ocean typically released as much CO2 into the air
cues.zh: 在工業革命之前，陸地和海洋通常會向空氣中釋放同樣多的二氧化碳

cues.text: as they absorbed back down through this drain.
cues.en: as they absorbed back down through this drain.
cues.zh: 當它們透過這個排水溝吸收回來時。

cues.text: But when people started digging up coal and oil to power their machines, first in Europe and then in the US
cues.en: But when people started digging up coal and oil to power their machines, first in Europe and then in the US
cues.zh: 但當人們開始開採煤炭和石油來為他們的機器提供動力時，首先在歐洲，然後在美國

cues.text: it sent this new flow of CO2 into the air one that the plants and oceans couldn't keep up with.
cues.en: it sent this new flow of CO2 into the air one that the plants and oceans couldn't keep up with.
cues.zh: 它將新的二氧化碳流排放到空氣中，植物和海洋無法跟上。

cues.text: About 45% of those emissions stay in the atmosphere trapping heat and setting us up
cues.en: About 45% of those emissions stay in the atmosphere trapping heat and setting us up
cues.zh: 其中約 45% 的排放物留在大氣中，捕獲熱量並為我們提供環境

cues.text: for an escalating array of climate disasters.
cues.en: for an escalating array of climate disasters.
cues.zh: 應對一系列不斷升級的氣候災害。

cues.text: So in 2015, all of the countries send someone off to Paris
cues.en: So in 2015, all of the countries send someone off to Paris
cues.zh: 所以2015年所有國家都派人去巴黎

cues.text: to say, “Okay, everyone, we need to keep warming well below two degrees Celsius.”
cues.en: to say, “Okay, everyone, we need to keep warming well below two degrees Celsius.”
cues.zh: 說：“好吧，大家，我們需要將氣溫控制在遠低於攝氏兩度。”

cues.text: And really we're aiming for 1.5 degrees.
cues.en: And really we're aiming for 1.5 degrees.
cues.zh: 事實上，我們的目標是 1.5 度。

cues.text: That's above pre-industrial levels.
cues.en: That's above pre-industrial levels.
cues.zh: 這高於工業化前的水平。

cues.text: And the exact numbers matter less than the fact that every increment of warming increases risk.
cues.en: And the exact numbers matter less than the fact that every increment of warming increases risk.
cues.zh: 確切的數字並不重要，重要的是每一次變暖都會增加風險這一事實。

cues.text: So first and foremost, we need to turn off the tap.
cues.en: So first and foremost, we need to turn off the tap.
cues.zh: 因此，首先，我們需要關閉水龍頭。

cues.text: Everything else is futile if we don't stop the root of the problem today.
cues.en: Everything else is futile if we don't stop the root of the problem today.
cues.zh: 如果我們今天不解決問題的根源，其他一切都是徒勞的。

cues.text: Turn off that tap.
cues.en: Turn off that tap.
cues.zh: 關掉那個水龍頭。

cues.text: Stop emitting CO2.
cues.en: Stop emitting CO2.
cues.zh: 停止排放二氧化碳。

cues.text: Not only have we not turned off any taps.
cues.en: Not only have we not turned off any taps.
cues.zh: 我們不僅沒有關閉任何水龍頭。

cues.text: Global emissions are still rising, especially in Asia...
cues.en: Global emissions are still rising, especially in Asia...
cues.zh: 全球排放量仍在上升，尤其是在亞洲...

cues.text: where, you know, 60% of human beings live many of whom are just emerging out of poverty.
cues.en: where, you know, 60% of human beings live many of whom are just emerging out of poverty.
cues.zh: 你知道，60%的人口生活在那裡，其中許多人只是擺脫貧困。

cues.text: So now we're here at nearly 1.2 degrees of warming.
cues.en: So now we're here at nearly 1.2 degrees of warming.
cues.zh: 所以現在我們的氣溫已經升高了將近 1.2 度。

cues.text: Frankly, we have not done what it would take to meet that 1.5 degree goal.
cues.en: Frankly, we have not done what it would take to meet that 1.5 degree goal.
cues.zh: 坦白說，我們還沒有採取措施來實現 1.5 度的目標。

cues.text: But we may be able to keep warming under two degrees if all of those net zero promises
cues.en: But we may be able to keep warming under two degrees if all of those net zero promises
cues.zh: 但如果所有這些淨零承諾，我們也許能夠將氣溫升高控制在兩度以下

cues.text: become real net zero policies.
cues.en: become real net zero policies.
cues.zh: 成為真正的淨零政策。

cues.text: And that's where things get a little tricky.
cues.en: And that's where things get a little tricky.
cues.zh: 這就是事情變得有點棘手的地方。

cues.text: Turning these emissions all the way off could get really hard really expensive or even unfair.
cues.en: Turning these emissions all the way off could get really hard really expensive or even unfair.
cues.zh: 完全關閉這些排放可能會變得非常困難、昂貴，甚至不公平。

cues.text: So everyone's kind of hoping that we can work from the bottom of the tub to... kind of increase the size of the drain
cues.en: So everyone's kind of hoping that we can work from the bottom of the tub to... kind of increase the size of the drain
cues.zh: 所以每個人都希望我們可以從浴缸底部開始工作......增加排水管的尺寸

cues.text: increase the speed at which we can drain that water from the bathtub.
cues.en: increase the speed at which we can drain that water from the bathtub.
cues.zh: 提高我們從浴缸排出水的速度。

cues.text: Now, CDR is distinct from CCS which prevents emissions at the source. That works on the faucet.
cues.en: Now, CDR is distinct from CCS which prevents emissions at the source. That works on the faucet.
cues.zh: 現在，CDR 與 CCS 不同，後者從源頭防止排放。這在水龍頭上有效。

cues.text: CDR grabs CO2 from the air and people have come up with a lot of interesting ways of doing that.
cues.en: CDR grabs CO2 from the air and people have come up with a lot of interesting ways of doing that.
cues.zh: CDR 從空氣中捕獲二氧化碳，人們想出了很多有趣的方法來做到這一點。

cues.text: The most common one so far is planting and protecting forests.
cues.en: The most common one so far is planting and protecting forests.
cues.zh: 迄今為止最常見的是植樹造林和保護森林。

cues.text: It's one of the more affordable CDR approaches right now and it has a lot of benefits aside from capturing CO2.
cues.en: It's one of the more affordable CDR approaches right now and it has a lot of benefits aside from capturing CO2.
cues.zh: 它是目前更實惠的 CDR 方法之一，除了捕獲二氧化碳之外，它還有很多好處。

cues.text: But we've seen from problems with the carbon offsets market that it can be hard to verify.
cues.en: But we've seen from problems with the carbon offsets market that it can be hard to verify.
cues.zh: 但我們從碳補償市場的問題中看到，它可能很難驗證。

cues.text: And, you know, trees don't live forever.
cues.en: And, you know, trees don't live forever.
cues.zh: 而且，你知道，樹木不會永遠活著。

cues.text: So most of the modeling scenarios that limit warming assume we’ll also be able to build a new drain
cues.en: So most of the modeling scenarios that limit warming assume we’ll also be able to build a new drain
cues.zh: 因此，大多數限制變暖的建模場景都假設我們也能夠建造一個新的排水溝

cues.text: for more permanent carbon storage.
cues.en: for more permanent carbon storage.
cues.zh: 以獲得更永久的碳儲存。

cues.text: So through things like rock weathering, we can crush up a bunch of rocks
cues.en: So through things like rock weathering, we can crush up a bunch of rocks
cues.zh: 所以透過岩石風化之類的事情，我們可以粉碎一堆岩石

cues.text: that naturally react with CO2 and try to speed up that reaction.
cues.en: that naturally react with CO2 and try to speed up that reaction.
cues.zh: 自然地與二氧化碳發生反應並試圖加速該反應。

cues.text: Or we can use chemistry to mimic...
cues.en: Or we can use chemistry to mimic...
cues.zh: 或者我們可以用化學來模仿...

cues.text: natural processes through technologies like direct air capture which basically use a type of chemical that selectively binds
cues.en: natural processes through technologies like direct air capture which basically use a type of chemical that selectively binds
cues.zh: 透過直接空氣捕獲等技術進行自然過程，這些技術基本上使用一種選擇性結合的化學物質

cues.text: with CO2 to capture it from the air.
cues.en: with CO2 to capture it from the air.
cues.zh: 與二氧化碳一起從空氣中捕獲它。

cues.text: These techniques all come with different costs and they're in really early stages of development.
cues.en: These techniques all come with different costs and they're in really early stages of development.
cues.zh: 這些技術都有不同的成本，而且還處於開發的早期階段。

cues.text: So there's a concern that the people in charge of the faucets will see any movement down here as an excuse
cues.en: So there's a concern that the people in charge of the faucets will see any movement down here as an excuse
cues.zh: 因此有人擔心負責水龍頭的人會以這裡的任何動靜為藉口

cues.text: to avoid making cuts up there.
cues.en: to avoid making cuts up there.
cues.zh: 以避免在那裡進行切割。

cues.text: Should we be counting on large amounts of carbon removal for our climate plans?
cues.en: Should we be counting on large amounts of carbon removal for our climate plans?
cues.zh: 我們的氣候計畫是否應該指望大量碳去除？

cues.text: Well, it seems we already are.
cues.en: Well, it seems we already are.
cues.zh: 嗯，看來我們已經是了。

cues.text: The US government's net zero plan calls for 500 million metric tons of CO2 removal
cues.en: The US government's net zero plan calls for 500 million metric tons of CO2 removal
cues.zh: 美國政府的淨零計劃要求減排5億噸二氧化碳

cues.text: by 2050, up from zero today.
cues.en: by 2050, up from zero today.
cues.zh: 到 2050 年，這個數字將從現在的零上升。

cues.text: Model simulations that limit warming to 1.5 degrees envision around 3.8 billion tons of permanent
cues.en: Model simulations that limit warming to 1.5 degrees envision around 3.8 billion tons of permanent
cues.zh: 將升溫限制在 1.5 度的模型模擬預計約 38 億噸永久變暖

cues.text: carbon removal globally every year.
cues.en: carbon removal globally every year.
cues.zh: 每年全球碳排放量。

cues.text: And this...
cues.en: And this...
cues.zh: 還有這個...

cues.text: is the total amount of permanent carbon removal that has happened so far.
cues.en: is the total amount of permanent carbon removal that has happened so far.
cues.zh: 是迄今為止發生的永久碳去除總量。

cues.text: So would you call that wishful thinking?
cues.en: So would you call that wishful thinking?
cues.zh: 那麼你會稱之為一廂情願嗎？

cues.text: Or is it foresight about how much can happen in 30 years
cues.en: Or is it foresight about how much can happen in 30 years
cues.zh: 還是30年後會發生多少事情的預見

cues.text: if we start our way up the learning curve now?
cues.en: if we start our way up the learning curve now?
cues.zh: 如果我們現在開始學習曲線呢？

cues.text: We have actually a really strong playbook of developing technologies and driving down costs.
cues.en: We have actually a really strong playbook of developing technologies and driving down costs.
cues.zh: 實際上，我們在開發技術和降低成本方面擁有非常強大的劇本。

cues.text: If we go all the way back to the 1970s we see technologies like solar PV be around $70 per watt.
cues.en: If we go all the way back to the 1970s we see technologies like solar PV be around $70 per watt.
cues.zh: 如果我們追溯到 20 世紀 70 年代，我們會看到太陽能光電等技術的價格約為每瓦 70 美元。

cues.text: Fast forward to 2023.
cues.en: Fast forward to 2023.
cues.zh: 快進到 2023 年。

cues.text: We see those prices down at around $0.07 per watt
cues.en: We see those prices down at around $0.07 per watt
cues.zh: 我們看到這些價格下降到每瓦 0.07 美元左右

cues.text: or even lower and at price parity with fossil fuels.
cues.en: or even lower and at price parity with fossil fuels.
cues.zh: 甚至更低，且與化石燃料價格持平。

cues.text: The challenge with that is that renewable energy produces something that's quite useful, which is energy and CDR...
cues.en: The challenge with that is that renewable energy produces something that's quite useful, which is energy and CDR...
cues.zh: 面臨的挑戰是再生能源產生非常有用的東西，那就是能源和 CDR…

cues.text: What is the customer for CDR?
cues.en: What is the customer for CDR?
cues.zh: What is the customer for CDR?

cues.text: Where does the demand come from?
cues.en: Where does the demand come from?
cues.zh: Where does the demand come from?

cues.text: You've seen some major companies including Stripe, Meta, Alphabet, McKinsey, Microsoft...
cues.en: You've seen some major companies including Stripe, Meta, Alphabet, McKinsey, Microsoft...
cues.zh: 你看過一些大公司，包括 Stripe、Meta、Alphabet、麥肯錫、微軟…

cues.text: All of these companies have made commitments to purchase carbon dioxide removal as part of their
cues.en: All of these companies have made commitments to purchase carbon dioxide removal as part of their
cues.zh: 所有這些公司都承諾購買二氧化碳去除裝置，作為其策略的一部分。

cues.text: corporate social responsibility plans.
cues.en: corporate social responsibility plans.
cues.zh: 企業社會責任計畫。

cues.text: That being said, I think in the long term carbon removal could be provided as a public service
cues.en: That being said, I think in the long term carbon removal could be provided as a public service
cues.zh: 話雖如此，我認為從長遠來看，碳清除可以作為公共服務提供

cues.text: in the ways that we manage some of our other pollution.
cues.en: in the ways that we manage some of our other pollution.
cues.zh: 我們管理其他一些汙染的方式。

cues.text: We pay for someone to come around to collect our trash and to manage it in a way that it's safe for our communities.
cues.en: We pay for someone to come around to collect our trash and to manage it in a way that it's safe for our communities.
cues.zh: 我們花錢請人來收集我們的垃圾，並以對我們社群安全的方式進行管理。

cues.text: The US government is already offering billions of dollars to try to get a direct air capture industry off the ground.
cues.en: The US government is already offering billions of dollars to try to get a direct air capture industry off the ground.
cues.zh: 美國政府已經提供數十億美元，試圖推動直接空氣捕獲產業的發展。

cues.text: And I think it makes sense for the countries that have used the most fossil fuels to do the work of finding out
cues.en: And I think it makes sense for the countries that have used the most fossil fuels to do the work of finding out
cues.zh: 我認為對於使用最多化石燃料的國家來說，進行找出答案的工作是有意義的

cues.text: if CDR can scale.
cues.en: if CDR can scale.
cues.zh: 如果 CDR 可以擴充。

cues.text: But if it doesn't...
cues.en: But if it doesn't...
cues.zh: 但如果不...

cues.text: well, then net zero will have been just another way of kicking the can down the road.
cues.en: well, then net zero will have been just another way of kicking the can down the road.
cues.zh: 好吧，那麼淨零排放就只是另一種方式。

cues.text: Which, of course, is how we ended up here in the first place.
cues.en: Which, of course, is how we ended up here in the first place.
cues.zh: 當然，這就是我們最初來到這裡的原因。

cues.text: In this position where we may now have no choice...
cues.en: In this position where we may now have no choice...
cues.zh: 在這種情況下，我們現在可能別無選擇......

cues.text: but to try everything.
cues.en: but to try everything.
cues.zh: 但要嘗試一切。

cues.en: Typical spacing between electrodes runs between three and a half and five

cues.text: millimetres — call it four.

cues.zh: 毫米——稱之為四。

cues.text: or four coarse numbers.
cues.en: or four coarse numbers.
cues.zh: 或四個粗略數字。

cues.en: I call this the Blob.

cues.text: You have never put a point on a screen.
cues.en: You have never put a point on a screen.
cues.zh: 您從未在螢幕上放置過一個點。

cues.en: By now the obvious objection has arrived, and it is a good one.

0H_X461z3iI.title: Is There a Way to Sober Up Faster?
0H_X461z3iI.speaker: SciShow
0H_X461z3iI.zh: 【SciShow】有沒有辦法可以更快醒酒？（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: If you drink alcohol, you’ve probably heard some tips and tricks for getting sober faster.
cues.en: If you drink alcohol, you’ve probably heard some tips and tricks for getting sober faster.
cues.zh: 如果您喝酒，您可能聽說過一些更快清醒的提示和技巧。

cues.text: Unfortunately, there is nothing most of us can do other than wait it out.
cues.en: Unfortunately, there is nothing most of us can do other than wait it out.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，除了等待，我們大多數人無能為力。

cues.text: But scientists recently figured out something that might help, at least in a clinical setting:
cues.en: But scientists recently figured out something that might help, at least in a clinical setting:
cues.zh: 但科學家最近發現了一些可能有幫助的東西，至少在臨床環境中：

cues.text: They have found a way to breathe the booze out.
cues.en: They have found a way to breathe the booze out.
cues.zh: 他們找到了一個方法來撥出酒氣。

cues.text: And while it won’t help you after a night on the town, it does have the serious potential to save lives.
cues.en: And while it won’t help you after a night on the town, it does have the serious potential to save lives.
cues.zh: 雖然在鎮上度過一夜後它對你沒有幫助，但它確實具有拯救生命的巨大潛力。

cues.text: So when we drink, alcohol in the form of ethanol goes from our guts into our bloodstream.
cues.en: So when we drink, alcohol in the form of ethanol goes from our guts into our bloodstream.
cues.zh: 因此，當我們喝酒時，酒精以乙醇的形式從我們的腸道進入我們的血液。

cues.text: And from there, it affects our brains, circulation, and all sorts of other systems that make us, you know, feel drunk.
cues.en: And from there, it affects our brains, circulation, and all sorts of other systems that make us, you know, feel drunk.
cues.zh: 從那裡開始，它會影響我們的大腦、血液迴圈和各種其他系統，使我們，你知道，感到醉酒。

cues.text: Then, our livers sober us up by converting the alcohol into another compound.
cues.en: Then, our livers sober us up by converting the alcohol into another compound.
cues.zh: 然後，我們的肝臟透過將酒精轉化為另一種化合物來使我們清醒。

cues.text: 90 percent of the ethanol in our bodies is cleared through the liver, and to this day, we have not been able to speed that process up.
cues.en: 90 percent of the ethanol in our bodies is cleared through the liver, and to this day, we have not been able to speed that process up.
cues.zh: 我們體內 90% 的乙醇是經由肝臟清除的，直到今天，我們還無法加快這個過程。

cues.text: But there is another way to get alcohol out of your blood: exhaling it.
cues.en: But there is another way to get alcohol out of your blood: exhaling it.
cues.zh: 但還有另一種方法可以將酒精從血液中排出：呼氣。

cues.text: See, if there’s a greater concentration of some gas in your blood than in your lungs,
cues.en: See, if there’s a greater concentration of some gas in your blood than in your lungs,
cues.zh: 看，如果你的血液中某些氣體的濃度比你肺部的濃度高，

cues.text: you’ll start to breathe that gas out.
cues.en: you’ll start to breathe that gas out.
cues.zh: 你會開始撥出這些氣體。

cues.text: This is actually why we breathe out carbon dioxide.
cues.en: This is actually why we breathe out carbon dioxide.
cues.zh: 這其實就是我們撥出二氧化碳的原因。

cues.text: The tiny blood vessels around our lungs called capillaries have a higher concentration of
cues.en: The tiny blood vessels around our lungs called capillaries have a higher concentration of
cues.zh: 我們肺部周圍的微小血管（稱為毛細血管）含有較高濃度的

cues.text: carbon dioxide than in the air in our lungs.
cues.en: carbon dioxide than in the air in our lungs.
cues.zh: 我們肺部的二氧化碳比空氣中的二氧化碳還要多。

cues.text: That difference is enough to make the CO2 travel into the lungs and eventually, out of our mouths and noses.
cues.en: That difference is enough to make the CO2 travel into the lungs and eventually, out of our mouths and noses.

cues.text: If it’s at a higher concentration in someone’s blood than in the air, they will breathe it out.
cues.en: If it’s at a higher concentration in someone’s blood than in the air, they will breathe it out.

cues.en: In a 2020 paper from Scientific Reports, researchers came up with a simple, yet elegant way to make this work:

cues.text: Just have people breathe in more CO2.
cues.en: Just have people breathe in more CO2.
cues.zh: 只是讓人們吸入更多的二氧化碳。

QAa2O_8wBUQ.title: What is Dark Matter and Dark Energy?
QAa2O_8wBUQ.speaker: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
QAa2O_8wBUQ.zh: 【Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell】什麼是暗物質和暗能量？（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Matter, as we know it; Atoms, stars and galaxies, planets and trees, rocks and us.
cues.en: Matter, as we know it; Atoms, stars and galaxies, planets and trees, rocks and us.
cues.zh: 我們所熟知的物質： 原子、恆星、星系、行星、樹、岩石，以及我們。

cues.text: This matter accounts for less than 5% of the known universe.
cues.en: This matter accounts for less than 5% of the known universe.
cues.zh: 這些物質佔整個宇宙不到５%。

cues.text: About 25% is dark matter; and 70% is dark energy.
cues.en: About 25% is dark matter; and 70% is dark energy.
cues.zh: 這些物質佔整個宇宙不到５%。 在整個宇宙中， 大約２５%是暗物質，７０%是暗能量。

cues.text: Both of which are invisible.
cues.en: Both of which are invisible.
cues.zh: 暗物質與暗能量都無法被觀測到。

cues.text: This is kind of strange because it suggests that everything we experience is
cues.en: This is kind of strange because it suggests that everything we experience is
cues.zh: 這聽起來有點奇怪， 這表示我們所接觸到的世界只佔了極其微小的部分。

cues.text: really only a tiny fraction of reality.
cues.en: really only a tiny fraction of reality.
cues.zh: 這聽起來有點奇怪， 這表示我們所接觸到的世界只佔了極其微小的部分。

cues.text: But it gets worse.
cues.en: But it gets worse.
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是， 我們對暗物質與暗能量究竟是什麼、如何運作毫無頭緒

cues.text: We really have no clue what dark matter and energy are, or how they work.
cues.en: We really have no clue what dark matter and energy are, or how they work.
cues.zh: 更糟糕的是， 我們對暗物質與暗能量究竟是什麼、如何運作毫無頭緒

cues.text: We are pretty sure they exist though.
cues.en: We are pretty sure they exist though.
cues.zh: 我們非常確定它們是存在的。 至於，為什麼我們知道它們存在呢？

cues.text: So, what do we know?
cues.en: So, what do we know?
cues.zh: 我們非常確定它們是存在的。 至於，為什麼我們知道它們存在呢？

cues.text: Dark matter is the stuff that makes it possible for galaxies to exist.
cues.en: Dark matter is the stuff that makes it possible for galaxies to exist.
cues.zh: 暗物質使星系穩定存在

cues.text: When we calculated why the universe is structured the way it is, it quickly became clear that there's just not enough normal matter.
cues.en: When we calculated why the universe is structured the way it is, it quickly became clear that there's just not enough normal matter.
cues.zh: 我們開始分析宇宙的結構時，發現能被觀測的"普通物質"並不足以令宇宙維持穩定存在。

cues.text: The gravity of the visible matter is not strong enough to form galaxies and complex structures.
cues.en: The gravity of the visible matter is not strong enough to form galaxies and complex structures.
cues.zh: 來自"普通物質"的重力不足以形成星系這樣的複雜結構，恆星間會更為鬆散，並四處散佈，

cues.text: The stars would more likely be scattered all over the place and not form galaxies.
cues.en: The stars would more likely be scattered all over the place and not form galaxies.
cues.zh: 來自"普通物質"的重力不足以形成星系這樣的複雜結構，恆星間會更為鬆散，並四處散佈， 這將導致星系無法形成。 因此，我們確信一定有某種東西在維繫星系的結構。

cues.text: So, we know there is something else inside and around them.
cues.en: So, we know there is something else inside and around them.
cues.zh: 這將導致星系無法形成。 因此，我們確信一定有某種東西在維繫星系的結構。

cues.text: Something that doesn't emit or reflect light.
cues.en: Something that doesn't emit or reflect light.
cues.zh: 某種東西，它不發射光，也不反射光

cues.text: Something dark...
cues.en: Something dark...
cues.zh: 所以稱作「暗」。

cues.text: but besides being able to calculate the existence of dark matter,
cues.en: but besides being able to calculate the existence of dark matter,
cues.zh: 所以稱作「暗」。 除了能計算到暗物質的存在以外，

cues.text: we can see it... kind of.
cues.en: we can see it... kind of.
cues.zh: 我們還能看到它的微小跡象。 高濃度暗物質的地方會使經過它的光線扭曲。

cues.text: Places with a high concentration of dark matter bend light passing near by.
cues.en: Places with a high concentration of dark matter bend light passing near by.
cues.zh: 我們還能看到它的微小跡象。 高濃度暗物質的地方會使經過它的光線扭曲。

cues.text: So we know there's something there that interacts with gravity.
cues.en: So we know there's something there that interacts with gravity.
cues.zh: 我們還能看到它的微小跡象。 高濃度暗物質的地方會使經過它的光線扭曲。 因此我們確信有東西在那兒，並且會與重力作用。

cues.text: Right now, we have more ideas about what dark energy is not, than what it is!
cues.en: Right now, we have more ideas about what dark energy is not, than what it is!
cues.zh: 現在， 對於暗物質是什麼有進一步認識， 那麼它究竟是什麼？

cues.text: We know dark matter is not just clouds of normal matter without stars,
cues.en: We know dark matter is not just clouds of normal matter without stars,
cues.zh: 我們知道暗物質並非一團無光源的普通物質， 因為普通物質會放射出我們能觀測到的粒子。

cues.text: because it would emit particles we could detect.
cues.en: because it would emit particles we could detect.
cues.zh: 我們知道暗物質並非一團無光源的普通物質， 因為普通物質會放射出我們能觀測到的粒子。

cues.en: The obvious industrial method, melting the ore with carbon the way you smelt iron, fails outright.

cues.text: It has to be chemistry.

cues.text: Not fire, but chlorine.

cues.text: So, the electrons near the Earth’s surface are repelled away, and the ground underneath

cues.text: cloud.

cues.text: Basically, an electric field describes how much force, and in what direction a positive

cues.zh: 基本上，電場描述了法向力的大小和方向

cues.text: charge would go if it were in the field -- in this case, upward toward the cloud.
cues.en: charge would go if it were in the field -- in this case, upward toward the cloud.
cues.zh: 如果它在場中，電荷就會向上移動——在這種情況下，電荷會向上流向雲。

cues.text: And when the difference in charges builds up enough, the first stage of lightning begins.
cues.en: And when the difference in charges builds up enough, the first stage of lightning begins.
cues.zh: 當電荷差異夠大時，閃電的第一階段就開始了。

cues.text: Most of the time we see negative lightning.
cues.en: Most of the time we see negative lightning.
cues.zh: 大多數時候我們看到的是負面閃電。

cues.text: This is when the electric field grows strong enough that an invisible channel of negative charges, called a stepped leader, begins to branch toward the ground at about 50 meters
cues.en: This is when the electric field grows strong enough that an invisible channel of negative charges, called a stepped leader, begins to branch toward the ground at about 50 meters
cues.zh: 當電場變得足夠強時，一個看不見的負電荷通道（稱為階梯先導）開始在大約 50 公尺處向地面分支

cues.text: per microsecond.
cues.en: per microsecond.
cues.zh: 每微秒。

cues.text: Meanwhile, an upward-moving channel of positive charges called a streamer rises up.
cues.en: Meanwhile, an upward-moving channel of positive charges called a streamer rises up.
cues.zh: 同時，稱為流光的向上移動的正電荷通道上升。

cues.text: They meet with a huge, bright flash that travels up.
cues.en: They meet with a huge, bright flash that travels up.
cues.zh: 他們遇到了一道向上移動的巨大而明亮的閃光。

cues.text: Not to mention the heat -- over 25,000 degrees Celsius, which is about 5 times hotter than
cues.en: Not to mention the heat -- over 25,000 degrees Celsius, which is about 5 times hotter than
cues.zh: 更不用說溫度了——超過 25,000 攝氏度，大約是地球溫度的 5 倍。

cues.text: the surface of the Sun.
cues.en: the surface of the Sun.
cues.zh: 太陽表面。

cues.text: Because the negatively-charged electrons stream from the cloud down to the ground, it’s
cues.en: Because the negatively-charged electrons stream from the cloud down to the ground, it’s
cues.zh: 因為帶負電的電子從雲流到地面，

cues.text: called negative lightning.
cues.en: called negative lightning.
cues.zh: 稱為負閃電。

cues.text: There’s also the much-less-common positive lightning -- with a net transfer of positive
cues.en: There’s also the much-less-common positive lightning -- with a net transfer of positive
cues.zh: 還有不太常見的正閃電——具有正閃電的淨傳輸

cues.text: charge from the cloud to the ground instead.
cues.en: charge from the cloud to the ground instead.
cues.zh: 而是從雲端充電到地面。

cues.text: These strikes start at the top of a cloud, where positive charges hang out, so they need to travel through more air to reach the ground.
cues.en: These strikes start at the top of a cloud, where positive charges hang out, so they need to travel through more air to reach the ground.
cues.zh: 這些撞擊從雲層頂部開始，那裡有正電荷，因此它們需要穿過更多的空氣才能到達地面。

cues.text: So they need even more charge separation -- which means the strikes can be up to 10 times stronger
cues.en: So they need even more charge separation -- which means the strikes can be up to 10 times stronger

cues.text: than negative lightning.

cues.text: to be released.
cues.en: to be released.
cues.zh: 被釋放。

cues.text: If this happens, we call them red sprites.
cues.en: If this happens, we call them red sprites.
cues.zh: 如果發生這種情況，我們稱它們為紅色精靈。

cues.text: They usually only last milliseconds, and can kinda look like giant jellyfish in the sky.
cues.en: They usually only last milliseconds, and can kinda look like giant jellyfish in the sky.
cues.zh: 它們通常只持續幾毫秒，看起來有點像天空中的巨型水母。

cues.text: And if that sounds cool -- there’s another type of lightning called a blue jet.
cues.en: And if that sounds cool -- there’s another type of lightning called a blue jet.
cues.zh: 如果這聽起來很酷的話——還有另一種型別的閃電，稱為藍色噴射。

cues.text: This lightning occurs when large amounts of positive charge stream upward, in order to neutralize the charge in the cloud.
cues.en: This lightning occurs when large amounts of positive charge stream upward, in order to neutralize the charge in the cloud.
cues.zh: 當大量正電荷向上流動以中和雲中的電荷時，就會發生這種閃電。

cues.text: The blue jets can get up to 40 kilometers high, but only last for fractions of a second.
cues.en: The blue jets can get up to 40 kilometers high, but only last for fractions of a second.
cues.zh: 藍色噴射流的高度可達 40 公里，但只能持續不到一秒。

cues.text: And scientists believe that their blue color comes from ionized nitrogen molecules.
cues.en: And scientists believe that their blue color comes from ionized nitrogen molecules.
cues.zh: 科學家認為它們的藍色來自電離氮分子。

cues.text: Even weirder is ball lightning -- a glowing grapefruit-sized ball of gas that lasts up
cues.en: Even weirder is ball lightning -- a glowing grapefruit-sized ball of gas that lasts up
cues.zh: 更奇怪的是球狀閃電——一種發光的葡萄柚大小的氣體球，可持續存在

cues.text: to 20 seconds.
cues.en: to 20 seconds.
cues.zh: 至 20 秒。

cues.text: But scientists aren’t quite sure what causes it.
cues.en: But scientists aren’t quite sure what causes it.
cues.zh: 但科學家不太確定是什麼原因造成的。

cues.text: One theory suggests that ball lightning is caused by the ions made by a lightning strike
cues.en: One theory suggests that ball lightning is caused by the ions made by a lightning strike
cues.zh: 一種理論認為球狀閃電是由雷擊產生的離子引起的

cues.text: near glass, like a window.
cues.en: near glass, like a window.
cues.zh: 靠近玻璃，如窗戶。

cues.text: The ions could pile up on one side of the glass and create an electric field, exciting
cues.en: The ions could pile up on one side of the glass and create an electric field, exciting
cues.zh: 離子可以堆積在玻璃的一側並產生電場，令人興奮

cues.text: air molecules on the other side, which would release photons and create a glow.
cues.en: air molecules on the other side, which would release photons and create a glow.
cues.zh: 另一側的空氣分子會釋放光子並產生光芒。

cues.text: Another theory suggests that elements in soil are to blame.
cues.en: Another theory suggests that elements in soil are to blame.
cues.zh: 另一種理論認為，土壤中的元素是罪魁禍首。

cues.text: In 2012, scientists in China recorded the first video of ball lightning.
cues.en: In 2012, scientists in China recorded the first video of ball lightning.
cues.zh: 2012年，中國科學家錄製了首個球狀閃電影片。

cues.text: They monitored the light it emitted, and found that it contained silicon, iron, and calcium,
cues.en: They monitored the light it emitted, and found that it contained silicon, iron, and calcium,
cues.zh: 他們監測它發出的光，發現它含有矽、鐵和鈣，

cues.text: which are all elements found in soil.
cues.en: which are all elements found in soil.
cues.zh: 這些都是土壤中發現的元素。

cues.text: So, a cloud-to-ground lightning strike might vaporize the soil’s silicate compounds,
cues.en: So, a cloud-to-ground lightning strike might vaporize the soil’s silicate compounds,
cues.zh: 因此，雲對地的雷擊可能會蒸發土壤中的矽酸鹽化合物，

cues.text: which react with the surrounding atmosphere to produce a ball of light.
cues.en: which react with the surrounding atmosphere to produce a ball of light.
cues.zh: 它與周圍的大氣反應，產生光球。

cues.text: So, the next time you’re watching a thunderstorm from the warm, dry safety of your home, remember
cues.en: So, the next time you’re watching a thunderstorm from the warm, dry safety of your home, remember
cues.zh: 因此，下次當您在溫暖、乾燥、安全的家中觀看雷暴時，請記住

cues.en: that all this lightning has a lot of physics behind it.
cues.zh: 所有這些閃電背後都有許多物理原理。

cues.text: The Sun, smooth and round and peaceful.

cues.en: can hit Earth and have serious consequences for humanity.

cues.en: So hot that it rips atoms into electrons and nuclei, all flowing around each other in a plasma.

cues.text: This plasma is pushed around and shaped by the Sun's magnetic field.
cues.en: This plasma is pushed around and shaped by the Sun's magnetic field.
cues.zh: 這些電漿體被太陽的磁場推動並成形。

cues.text: Similar to how the Sun's gravitational field reaches out to the planets and shapes their orbits.
cues.en: Similar to how the Sun's gravitational field reaches out to the planets and shapes their orbits.

cues.text: But magnetism is very different from gravity.
cues.en: But magnetism is very different from gravity.
cues.zh: 但是磁力與重力有很大的不同。

cues.en: Magnetism is one part of a dual force: Electromagnetism.

cues.text: On the Sun, the plasma—made of electrically charged protons and electrons—

cues.text: They're stuck in a dynamic feedback loop called a dynamo,
cues.en: They're stuck in a dynamic feedback loop called a dynamo,
cues.zh: 它們被困在稱為發電機的動態回饋迴路中，

cues.text: which keeps the sun's magnetic field alive.
cues.en: which keeps the sun's magnetic field alive.
cues.zh: 該迴路使太陽的磁場保持活躍。

cues.text: This magnetic field stores enormous amounts of energy
cues.en: This magnetic field stores enormous amounts of energy
