cues.text: WALTER ISAACSON: The "Mona Lisa" has become some grand thing in our imagination.
cues.en: WALTER ISAACSON: The "Mona Lisa" has become some grand thing in our imagination.
cues.zh: 華特‧艾薩克森：《蒙娜麗莎》已經成為我們想像中的宏偉之物。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Each time you see the "Mona Lisa," you have a different feeling
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Each time you see the "Mona Lisa," you have a different feeling
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：每次看《蒙娜麗莎》都有不同的感受

cues.text: about what she has in mind.
cues.en: about what she has in mind.
cues.zh: 關於她的想法。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Every year, millions visit her, drawn by her beauty
cues.en: NARRATOR: Every year, millions visit her, drawn by her beauty
cues.zh: 旁白：每年都有數百萬人被她的美麗所吸引而拜訪她

cues.text: or, perhaps, her fame.
cues.en: or, perhaps, her fame.
cues.zh: 或者，也許是她的名氣。

cues.text: BORGO: They've clocked the average amount the visitors spend looking at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: BORGO: They've clocked the average amount the visitors spend looking at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 博爾戈：他們統計了遊客觀看《蒙娜麗莎》的平均花費，

cues.text: and that's roughly about 15 seconds.
cues.en: and that's roughly about 15 seconds.
cues.zh: 大約需要 15 秒。

cues.text: You're more focused on getting a good picture for your Instagram feed than actually looking at the painting.
cues.en: You're more focused on getting a good picture for your Instagram feed than actually looking at the painting.
cues.zh: 您更專注於為 Instagram 動態獲取一張好照片，而不是實際觀看這幅畫。

cues.text: NARRATOR: So is the "Mona Lisa" just famous for being famous?
cues.en: NARRATOR: So is the "Mona Lisa" just famous for being famous?
cues.zh: 旁白：那麼《蒙娜麗莎》只是因為出名而出名嗎？

cues.text: More icon than art?
cues.en: More icon than art?
cues.zh: 更多的是圖示而不是藝術？

cues.text: Or does she deserve her place on the Louvre's throne as the most celebrated painting in the world?
cues.en: Or does she deserve her place on the Louvre's throne as the most celebrated painting in the world?
cues.zh: 或者她配得上羅浮宮作為世界上最著名的畫作的寶座？

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: It's not just a portrait of a woman who was living 500 years ago.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: It's not just a portrait of a woman who was living 500 years ago.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：這不僅僅是一幅生活在 500 年前的女性的肖像。

cues.text: It's a demonstration of how painting could show life.
cues.en: It's a demonstration of how painting could show life.
cues.zh: 這是繪畫如何展現生活的示範。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Now researchers are using new techniques to investigate the most famous painting on Earth
cues.en: NARRATOR: Now researchers are using new techniques to investigate the most famous painting on Earth
cues.zh: 旁白：現在研究人員正在使用新技術來研究地球上最著名的畫作

cues.text: like never before.
cues.en: like never before.
cues.zh: 前所未有。

cues.text: ♪ MARTIN KEMP: The smile is crucial.
cues.en: ♪ MARTIN KEMP: The smile is crucial.
cues.zh: ♪ 馬丁坎普：微笑至關重要。

cues.text: It's teasing you, saying, "I know something you don't know."
cues.en: It's teasing you, saying, "I know something you don't know."
cues.zh: 它在戲弄你，說：“我知道一些你不知道的事情。”

cues.text: NARRATOR: Could the "Mona Lisa," with her enigmatic smile,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Could the "Mona Lisa," with her enigmatic smile,
cues.zh: 旁白：帶著神秘微笑的“蒙娜麗莎”，

cues.text: be the key to decoding the man who made her--
cues.en: be the key to decoding the man who made her--
cues.zh: 成為破解創造她的男人的鑰匙——

cues.text: Leonardo da Vinci?
cues.en: Leonardo da Vinci?
cues.zh: 列奧納多·達·芬奇？

cues.text: No doubt he was a brilliant artist, but he was also a groundbreaking scientist.
cues.en: No doubt he was a brilliant artist, but he was also a groundbreaking scientist.
cues.zh: 毫無疑問，他是一位傑出的藝術家，但他也是一位開創性的科學家。

cues.text: He anticipated theories by both Galileo and Newton
cues.en: He anticipated theories by both Galileo and Newton
cues.zh: 他預見了伽利略和牛頓的理論

cues.text: by at least a century.
cues.en: by at least a century.
cues.zh: 至少一個世紀。

cues.text: And dreamed up remarkable inventions that seem to predict our modern age:
cues.en: And dreamed up remarkable inventions that seem to predict our modern age:
cues.zh: 並夢想著一些非凡的發明，這些發明似乎預示著我們的現代時代：

cues.text: armored tanks, flying machines, even something like a self-driving car.
cues.en: armored tanks, flying machines, even something like a self-driving car.
cues.zh: 裝甲坦克、飛行器，甚至自動駕駛汽車之類的東西。

cues.text: But were his scientific explorations a distraction from his painting?
cues.en: But were his scientific explorations a distraction from his painting?
cues.zh: 但他的科學探索會分散他對繪畫的注意力嗎？

cues.text: Or was science the secret to his artistic genius?
cues.en: Or was science the secret to his artistic genius?
cues.zh: 或者科學是他藝術天才的秘密？

cues.text: Was the "Mona Lisa," in fact, Leonardo's greatest invention?
cues.en: Was the "Mona Lisa," in fact, Leonardo's greatest invention?
cues.zh: 《蒙娜麗莎》其實是李奧納多最偉大的發明嗎？

cues.text: ISAACSON: If you want to understand Leonardo da Vinci, you just have to look at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: ISAACSON: If you want to understand Leonardo da Vinci, you just have to look at the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：如果你想了解達文西，你只需要看看《蒙娜麗莎》

cues.text: because it's all there.
cues.en: because it's all there.
cues.zh: 因為一切都在那裡。

cues.text: It's the culmination of a lifetime spent loving science and art.
cues.en: It's the culmination of a lifetime spent loving science and art.
cues.zh: 這是一生熱愛科學和藝術的頂峰。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: In the back streets of Florence, Italy,
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: In the back streets of Florence, Italy,
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：在義大利佛羅倫斯的後街，

cues.text: Valter Conti and his daughter Elena prepare for their tribute to Leonardo
cues.en: Valter Conti and his daughter Elena prepare for their tribute to Leonardo
cues.zh: 瓦爾特·孔蒂和他的女兒埃琳娜準備向萊昂納多致敬

cues.text: and the "Mona Lisa"...
cues.en: and the "Mona Lisa"...
cues.zh: 還有《蒙娜麗莎》…

cues.text: Human statues handing out Leonardo quotes.
cues.en: Human statues handing out Leonardo quotes.
cues.zh: 人體雕像分發達芬奇名言。

cues.text: It's their way of marking the 500th anniversary
cues.en: It's their way of marking the 500th anniversary
cues.zh: 這是他們紀念 500 週年的方式

cues.text: of Leonardo's death, and just one of many celebrations
cues.en: of Leonardo's death, and just one of many celebrations
cues.zh: 萊昂納多去世，這只是眾多慶祝活動之一

cues.text: that are in the works around the world.
cues.en: that are in the works around the world.
cues.zh: 世界各地都在進行中。

cues.text: From a fine art museum in Beijing to a multimedia extravaganza in Peru...
cues.en: From a fine art museum in Beijing to a multimedia extravaganza in Peru...
cues.zh: 從北京的美術館到秘魯的多媒體盛宴…

cues.text: And a blockbuster exhibition at the Louvre.
cues.en: And a blockbuster exhibition at the Louvre.
cues.zh: 以及在羅浮宮舉辦的一場轟動一時的展覽。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: For the Louvre museum, it's a really important moment.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: For the Louvre museum, it's a really important moment.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：對羅浮宮來說，這是一個非常重要的時刻。

cues.text: Because Louvre is like Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.en: Because Louvre is like Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.zh: 因為羅浮宮就像達文西。

cues.text: We have the third of all his paintings.
cues.en: We have the third of all his paintings.
cues.zh: 我們擁有他所有畫作中的第三幅。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Vincent Delieuvin oversees the five Leonardo masterpieces
cues.en: NARRATOR: Vincent Delieuvin oversees the five Leonardo masterpieces
cues.zh: 旁白：文森特德利文 (Vincent Delieuvin) 監督達文西的五部傑作

cues.text: that hang at the Louvre.
cues.en: that hang at the Louvre.
cues.zh: 掛在羅浮宮。

cues.text: ♪ That's the largest collection in the world.
cues.en: ♪ That's the largest collection in the world.
cues.zh: ♪ 這是世界上最大的收藏。

cues.text: While Leonardo may be the most famous painter of all time,
cues.en: While Leonardo may be the most famous painter of all time,
cues.zh: 雖然萊昂納多可能是有史以來最著名的畫家，

cues.text: he completed surprisingly few paintings.
cues.en: he completed surprisingly few paintings.
cues.zh: 他完成的畫作少得驚人。

cues.text: Leonardo was really someone experimental.
cues.en: Leonardo was really someone experimental.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多確實是個實驗者。

cues.text: He didn't want to paint a lot.
cues.en: He didn't want to paint a lot.
cues.zh: 他不想畫太多。

cues.text: He wanted to paint a perfect painting.
cues.en: He wanted to paint a perfect painting.
cues.zh: 他想畫出一幅完美的畫。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: So what did it take for Leonardo to make a perfect painting?
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: So what did it take for Leonardo to make a perfect painting?
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：那麼李奧納多需要什麼才能創作出一幅完美的畫作呢？

cues.text: The answer may be lying right under Delieuvin's feet.
cues.en: The answer may be lying right under Delieuvin's feet.
cues.zh: 答案可能就在德利文的腳下。

cues.text: For the upcoming exhibition, he is working with a team of scientists
cues.en: For the upcoming exhibition, he is working with a team of scientists
cues.zh: 對於即將舉行的展覽，他正在與科學家團隊合作

cues.text: housed downstairs from the Louvre, at the Center for Research and Restoration
cues.en: housed downstairs from the Louvre, at the Center for Research and Restoration
cues.zh: 位於羅浮宮樓下的研究與修復中心

cues.text: of Museums in France.
cues.en: of Museums in France.
cues.zh: 法國的博物館。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Thanks to a new kind of scientific investigation, we are really able to get inside the painting
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：由於一種新的科學研究，我們真正能夠進入畫作內部

cues.text: and to understand how Leonardo was working to perfect the painting
cues.en: and to understand how Leonardo was working to perfect the painting
cues.zh: 並瞭解李奧納多如何努力完善這幅畫

cues.text: for a long, long time-- during five, ten, 20 years.
cues.en: for a long, long time-- during five, ten, 20 years.
cues.zh: 很長很長一段時間──五年、十年、二十年。

cues.text: It's really something really specific to Leonardo.
cues.en: It's really something really specific to Leonardo.
cues.zh: 這確實是萊昂納多特有的東西。

cues.text: NARRATOR: They are peering deep inside Leonardo's masterpieces,
cues.en: NARRATOR: They are peering deep inside Leonardo's masterpieces,
cues.zh: 旁白：他們正在深入探究列奧納多的傑作，

cues.text: hoping to reveal the secrets of his technique
cues.en: hoping to reveal the secrets of his technique
cues.zh: 希望揭示他技術的秘密

cues.text: that our eyes cannot see.
cues.en: that our eyes cannot see.
cues.zh: 我們的眼睛看不見。

cues.text: BRUNO MOTTIN: The eye sees something that it believes to be two-dimensional,
cues.en: BRUNO MOTTIN: The eye sees something that it believes to be two-dimensional,
cues.zh: BRUNO MOTTIN：眼睛看到它認為是二維的東西，

cues.text: but which is really three-dimensional, because there is depth in a painting.
cues.en: but which is really three-dimensional, because there is depth in a painting.
cues.zh: 但這確實是三維的，因為繪畫有深度。

cues.text: NARRATOR: For art historian Bruno Mottin, the first step is to understand
cues.en: NARRATOR: For art historian Bruno Mottin, the first step is to understand
cues.zh: 旁白：對藝術史學家布魯諾‧莫丁來說，第一步是理解

cues.text: the chemistry of Leonardo's paint, starting with the powdered minerals
cues.en: the chemistry of Leonardo's paint, starting with the powdered minerals
cues.zh: 萊昂納多顏料的化學成分，從礦物粉開始

cues.text: that were the source of his colors.
cues.en: that were the source of his colors.
cues.zh: 這就是他色彩的來源。

cues.text: MOTTIN: You have green, which is made with the scratching of copper plates,
cues.en: MOTTIN: You have green, which is made with the scratching of copper plates,
cues.zh: MOTTIN：你有綠色，它是用銅板刮痕製成的，

cues.text: you have vermillion, which is made with mercury, you have lead white, which is made with lead.
cues.en: you have vermillion, which is made with mercury, you have lead white, which is made with lead.
cues.zh: 你有朱紅色，它是由汞製成的，你有鉛白，它是由鉛製成的。

cues.text: But these can't be applied directly on a painting-- it has to be mixed with something else.
cues.en: But these can't be applied directly on a painting-- it has to be mixed with something else.
cues.zh: 但這些不能直接應用在繪畫上——它必須與其他東西混合。

cues.text: NARRATOR: These colored pigments are mixed with a liquid, like oil.
cues.en: NARRATOR: These colored pigments are mixed with a liquid, like oil.
cues.zh: 旁白：這些彩色顏料與液體（如油）混合。

cues.text: That gets painted on in layers.
cues.en: That gets painted on in layers.
cues.zh: 這是分層繪製的。

cues.text: ♪ In a cross-section of a painting,
cues.en: ♪ In a cross-section of a painting,
cues.zh: ♪ 在一幅畫的橫切面中，

cues.text: you have the base- which today is frequently canvas,
cues.en: you have the base- which today is frequently canvas,
cues.zh: 你有底座——今天通常是帆布，

cues.text: but in Leonardo's time, they used planks of wood.
cues.en: but in Leonardo's time, they used planks of wood.
cues.zh: 但在列奧納多時代，他們使用木板。

cues.text: On that is a coat of white that can reflect light.
cues.en: On that is a coat of white that can reflect light.
cues.zh: 上面有一層可以反射光線的白色塗層。

cues.text: As the artist works, semi-translucent paint is built up layer by layer
cues.en: As the artist works, semi-translucent paint is built up layer by layer
cues.zh: 隨著藝術家的創作，半透明的顏料一層一層堆積起來

cues.text: and then sealed with a coat of varnish.
cues.en: and then sealed with a coat of varnish.
cues.zh: 然後用一層清漆密封。

cues.text: In the end, our eyes see the interplay between the light reflected off different pigments
cues.en: In the end, our eyes see the interplay between the light reflected off different pigments
cues.zh: 最後，我們的眼睛看到不同顏料反射的光之間的相互作用

cues.text: suspended in the layers, creating depth and elusive subtleties.
cues.en: suspended in the layers, creating depth and elusive subtleties.
cues.zh: 懸浮在層層之中，創造出深度和難以捉摸的微妙之處。

cues.text: MOTTIN: Oil is a translucent medium, which gives to the mixture a deepness.
cues.en: MOTTIN: Oil is a translucent medium, which gives to the mixture a deepness.
cues.zh: MOTTIN：油是一種半透明介質，賦予混合物深度。

cues.text: You can see through all the layers.
cues.en: You can see through all the layers.
cues.zh: 你可以看透所有的層。

cues.text: You don't only see a flat surface.
cues.en: You don't only see a flat surface.
cues.zh: 您看到的不僅僅是平坦的表面。

cues.text: You have the feeling of what is beneath the painting.
cues.en: You have the feeling of what is beneath the painting.
cues.zh: 你可以感覺到畫作底下的東西。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo worked on the "Mona Lisa" for about 16 years.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo worked on the "Mona Lisa" for about 16 years.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多為《蒙娜麗莎》工作了大約 16 年。

cues.text: Can these investigative techniques help reveal, ultimately, what he was doing all that time?
cues.en: Can these investigative techniques help reveal, ultimately, what he was doing all that time?
cues.zh: 這些調查技術能否最終幫助揭示他一直在做什麼？

cues.text: ♪ The "Mona Lisa" began in Florence, Italy, in 1503
cues.en: ♪ The "Mona Lisa" began in Florence, Italy, in 1503
cues.zh: ♪ 《蒙娜麗莎》於 1503 年誕生於義大利佛羅倫斯

cues.text: as a commission from a wealthy cloth merchant to paint his wife, Lisa Gherardini.
cues.en: as a commission from a wealthy cloth merchant to paint his wife, Lisa Gherardini.
cues.zh: 受一位富有布商的委託，為他的妻子麗莎·蓋拉迪尼 (Lisa Gherardini) 作畫。

cues.text: The word "mona" was a polite form of address, much like "madam," hence "Mona Lisa."
cues.en: The word "mona" was a polite form of address, much like "madam," hence "Mona Lisa."
cues.zh: “蒙娜”一詞是一種禮貌的稱呼，很像“女士”，因此稱為“蒙娜麗莎”。

cues.text: Over time, she became something much more.
cues.en: Over time, she became something much more.
cues.zh: 隨著時間的推移，她變得更加重要。

cues.text: BORGO: The "Mona Lisa" started off as a portrait for a merchant's wife
cues.en: BORGO: The "Mona Lisa" started off as a portrait for a merchant's wife
cues.zh: 博爾戈：《蒙娜麗莎》最初是為一位商人的妻子繪製的肖像

cues.text: and ended up as a sort of manifesto, if you want,
cues.en: and ended up as a sort of manifesto, if you want,
cues.zh: 最後成為一種宣言，如果你願意的話，

cues.text: of his ability as a, as a painter, of his conception of the world, even.
cues.en: of his ability as a, as a painter, of his conception of the world, even.
cues.zh: 他作為畫家的能力，甚至他對世界的看法。

cues.text: NARRATOR: So is this what the real Lisa looked like?
cues.en: NARRATOR: So is this what the real Lisa looked like?
cues.zh: 旁白：這就是真正的麗莎的樣子嗎？

cues.text: And how different does she appear today from what Leonardo painted 500 years ago?
cues.en: And how different does she appear today from what Leonardo painted 500 years ago?
cues.zh: 她今天的樣子與 500 年前列奧納多的畫有何不同？

cues.text: To find out, scientists captured the "Mona Lisa" with an array of high-tech cameras.
cues.en: To find out, scientists captured the "Mona Lisa" with an array of high-tech cameras.
cues.zh: 為了找到答案，科學家們用一系列高科技相機拍攝了《蒙娜麗莎》。

cues.text: These detect light in the electromagnetic spectrum that is not visible to our eyes.
cues.en: These detect light in the electromagnetic spectrum that is not visible to our eyes.
cues.zh: 它們檢測我們肉眼不可見的電磁頻譜中的光。

cues.text: ♪ So just as some cameras can see wildlife in the dark,
cues.en: ♪ So just as some cameras can see wildlife in the dark,
cues.zh: ♪ 就像有些相機可以在黑暗中看到野生動物一樣，

cues.text: these cameras can help us see the "Mona Lisa" in a new light--
cues.en: these cameras can help us see the "Mona Lisa" in a new light--
cues.zh: 這些相機可以幫助我們以新的視角看待《蒙娜麗莎》——

cues.text: literally.
cues.en: literally.
cues.zh: 從字面上看。

cues.text: Each image provides clues about her past.
cues.en: Each image provides clues about her past.
cues.zh: 每張照片都提供了有關她過去的線索。

cues.text: MOTTIN: So we have a lot of different images, which can tell us
cues.en: MOTTIN: So we have a lot of different images, which can tell us
cues.zh: MOTTIN：所以我們有很多不同的影象，它們可以告訴我們

cues.text: about the structure of the painting and the, the way it has been made.
cues.en: about the structure of the painting and the, the way it has been made.
cues.zh: 關於這幅畫的結構及其製作方式。

cues.text: NARRATOR: In the ultraviolet image, blotches of dark blue appear.
cues.en: NARRATOR: In the ultraviolet image, blotches of dark blue appear.
cues.zh: 旁白：在紫外線影像中，出現深藍色斑點。

cues.text: These reveal areas of paint which are not by Leonardo's hand.
cues.en: These reveal areas of paint which are not by Leonardo's hand.
cues.zh: 這些揭示了並非由萊昂納多之手繪製的油漆區域。

cues.text: They are modern restorations to repair damage to the painting,
cues.en: They are modern restorations to repair damage to the painting,
cues.zh: 它們是現代修復品，用於修復畫作的損壞，

cues.text: like this dangerous crack in the wood base.
cues.en: like this dangerous crack in the wood base.
cues.zh: 就像木底座上這條危險的裂縫。

cues.text: And for Mottin, it reveals even more.
cues.en: And for Mottin, it reveals even more.
cues.zh: 對於莫廷來說，它揭示了更多。

cues.text: MOTTIN: It shows us that the painting is in fact colored by a greenish and yellowish varnish
cues.en: MOTTIN: It shows us that the painting is in fact colored by a greenish and yellowish varnish
cues.zh: 莫廷：它向我們表明，這幅畫實際上是用綠色和黃色清漆著色的

cues.text: which changes the colors of the true painting.
cues.en: which changes the colors of the true painting.
cues.zh: 這會改變真實繪畫的顏色。

cues.text: NARRATOR: This thick varnish has yellowed and darkened over time,
cues.en: NARRATOR: This thick varnish has yellowed and darkened over time,
cues.zh: 旁白：隨著時間的推移，這種厚厚的清漆已經變黃變暗，

cues.text: making it difficult to make out some of the details.
cues.en: making it difficult to make out some of the details.
cues.zh: 使得一些細節變得難以辨認。

cues.text: She looks rather like a plump lady, we should say, because we do not know where the arm stops.
cues.en: She looks rather like a plump lady, we should say, because we do not know where the arm stops.
cues.zh: 我們應該說，她看起來很像一位豐滿的女士，因為我們不知道手臂停在哪裡。

cues.text: NARRATOR: But this infrared image clearly shows this dark area was once translucent.
cues.en: NARRATOR: But this infrared image clearly shows this dark area was once translucent.
cues.zh: 旁白：但這張紅外線影像清楚地顯示這個黑暗區域曾經是半透明的。

cues.text: Lisa is wearing a veil that gracefully falls over her surprisingly slender shoulders.
cues.en: Lisa is wearing a veil that gracefully falls over her surprisingly slender shoulders.
cues.zh: 麗莎戴著面紗，優雅地垂在她出奇纖細的肩膀上。

cues.text: ♪ To penetrate the very deepest layers, the team turn to a tool more familiar to us
cues.en: ♪ To penetrate the very deepest layers, the team turn to a tool more familiar to us
cues.zh: ♪ 為了穿透最深層，團隊轉向了我們更熟悉的工具

cues.text: from a doctor's office: X-rays.
cues.en: from a doctor's office: X-rays.
cues.zh: 來自醫生辦公室：X 光檢查。

cues.text: These can reveal how the painting began.
cues.en: These can reveal how the painting began.
cues.zh: 這些可以揭示這幅畫是如何開始的。

cues.text: Most artists at the time began with a drawing and then filled it in with thick paint.
cues.en: Most artists at the time began with a drawing and then filled it in with thick paint.
cues.zh: 當時的大多數藝術家都是從一幅圖畫開始，然後用厚厚的顏料填滿它。

cues.text: So the X-ray looks like this, Raphael's "La Belle Jardinière."
cues.en: So the X-ray looks like this, Raphael's "La Belle Jardinière."
cues.zh: 所以 X 光看起來像這樣，拉斐爾的《美麗的花園》。

cues.text: The figures started out clearly defined-- and stayed that way.
cues.en: The figures started out clearly defined-- and stayed that way.
cues.zh: 這些數字一開始就明確定義，而且一直都是如此。

cues.text: ♪ But when Leonardo's paintings are X-rayed,
cues.en: ♪ But when Leonardo's paintings are X-rayed,
cues.zh: ♪ 但是當列奧納多的畫作經過 X 光檢查時，

cues.text: the figures often vanish.
cues.en: the figures often vanish.
cues.zh: 這些數字經常消失。

cues.text: ♪ ELISABETH RAVAUD: Leonardo image are like phantom.
cues.en: ♪ ELISABETH RAVAUD: Leonardo image are like phantom.
cues.zh: ♪ 伊莉莎白‧拉沃：李奧納多的形象就像幻影。

cues.text: We don't understand at first sight what really is on the picture.
cues.en: We don't understand at first sight what really is on the picture.
cues.zh: 我們乍看之下並不明白圖片上到底是什麼。

cues.text: NARRATOR: In the X-ray of the "Mona Lisa," there is no clear outline.
cues.en: NARRATOR: In the X-ray of the "Mona Lisa," there is no clear outline.
cues.zh: 旁白：在《蒙娜麗莎》的X光片中，沒有清晰的輪廓。

cues.text: Instead, the image evolved as Leonardo made continual adjustments.
cues.en: Instead, the image evolved as Leonardo made continual adjustments.
cues.zh: 相反，隨著列奧納多不斷調整，形像不斷演變。

cues.text: This also suggests Lisa may not have looked exactly like this.
cues.en: This also suggests Lisa may not have looked exactly like this.
cues.zh: 這也表明麗莎可能看起來並不完全像這樣。

cues.text: ISAACSON: He keeps it.
cues.en: ISAACSON: He keeps it.
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：他保留著它。

cues.text: He doesn't deliver it to the merchant who commissioned it.
cues.en: He doesn't deliver it to the merchant who commissioned it.
cues.zh: 他不會將其交付給委託它的商人。

cues.text: Because for him, it's no longer a portrait of Mona Lisa.
cues.en: Because for him, it's no longer a portrait of Mona Lisa.
cues.zh: 因為對他來說，這不再是蒙娜麗莎的肖像。

cues.text: It is a universal painting.
cues.en: It is a universal painting.
cues.zh: 這是一幅普遍的繪畫。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: In the upcoming exhibition, Delieuvin plans to hang
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: In the upcoming exhibition, Delieuvin plans to hang
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：在即將舉行的展覽中，德利尤文計劃懸掛

cues.text: some of these scientific masterpieces along with Leonardo's original paintings.
cues.en: some of these scientific masterpieces along with Leonardo's original paintings.
cues.zh: 其中一些科學傑作以及達·芬奇的原畫。

cues.text: The scans prove an essential point about Leonardo's artistry--
cues.en: The scans prove an essential point about Leonardo's artistry--
cues.zh: 這些掃描證明瞭列奧納多藝術天賦的一個重要觀點——

cues.text: he painted like no one else.
cues.en: he painted like no one else.
cues.zh: 他的畫法無人能及。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo is one of the first artists
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo is one of the first artists
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：李奧納多是最早的藝術家之一

cues.text: to be really free.
cues.en: to be really free.
cues.zh: 真正自由。

cues.text: He felt free to change his mind, not only during the drawing preparation,
cues.en: He felt free to change his mind, not only during the drawing preparation,
cues.zh: 他可以隨意改變主意，不僅是在繪圖準備期間，

cues.text: but also during the painting of his work.
cues.en: but also during the painting of his work.
cues.zh: 也是在他的作品繪畫過程中。

cues.text: This is incredibly not common.
cues.en: This is incredibly not common.
cues.zh: 這是非常不常見的。

cues.text: He is the only one to give such liberty, free manner, in his execution.
cues.en: He is the only one to give such liberty, free manner, in his execution.
cues.zh: 他是唯一一個在執行時給予如此自由、自由的方式的人。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: Artists then were considered craftsmen, and needed to churn out paintings for patrons.
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: Artists then were considered craftsmen, and needed to churn out paintings for patrons.
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：當時的藝術家被認為是工匠，需要為顧客製作畫作。

cues.text: So how did Leonardo become such a free spirit?
cues.en: So how did Leonardo become such a free spirit?
cues.zh: 那麼列奧納多是如何變得如此自由的呢？

cues.text: From the beginning, Leonardo was an outsider.
cues.en: From the beginning, Leonardo was an outsider.
cues.zh: 從一開始，李奧納多就是一個局外人。

cues.text: ♪ Born in 1452 to an unwed farm girl
cues.en: ♪ Born in 1452 to an unwed farm girl
cues.zh: ♪ 出生於 1452 年，父親是一位未婚的農家女孩

cues.text: in the small Italian town of Vinci, he was named "Leonardo from Vinci."
cues.en: in the small Italian town of Vinci, he was named "Leonardo from Vinci."
cues.zh: 在義大利小鎮芬奇，他被稱為「來自芬奇的李奧納多」。

cues.text: Therefore, Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.en: Therefore, Leonardo da Vinci.
cues.zh: 因此，列奧納多·達·芬奇。

cues.text: ISAACSON: Leonardo had the great good fortune to be born out of wedlock.
cues.en: ISAACSON: Leonardo had the great good fortune to be born out of wedlock.
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：李奧納多非常幸運，是非婚生的。

cues.text: It meant he didn't have crammed into him
cues.en: It meant he didn't have crammed into him
cues.zh: 這顯示他並沒有塞進他的身體裡

cues.text: the sort of old dusty scholastic wisdom of the Middle Ages.
cues.en: the sort of old dusty scholastic wisdom of the Middle Ages.
cues.zh: 那種古老的、塵封已久的中世紀經院智慧。

cues.text: Instead, he got to be self-taught.
cues.en: Instead, he got to be self-taught.
cues.zh: 相反，他必須自學。

cues.text: It also meant he didn't have to be a notary like his father.
cues.en: It also meant he didn't have to be a notary like his father.
cues.zh: 這也意味著他不必像他父親那樣成為公證人。

cues.text: And so he has a fresh life, where he can be anything he wants.
cues.en: And so he has a fresh life, where he can be anything he wants.
cues.zh: 這樣他就有了新鮮的生活，他可以成為任何他想要的人。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: At about 14, Leonardo's father sent him to learn a trade in Florence,
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: At about 14, Leonardo's father sent him to learn a trade in Florence,
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：大約 14 歲時，李奧納多的父親送他去佛羅倫斯學習一門手藝，

cues.text: the epicenter of commerce, learning, and beauty at the beginning of the Renaissance.
cues.en: the epicenter of commerce, learning, and beauty at the beginning of the Renaissance.
cues.zh: 文藝復興初期商業、學術和美容的中心。

cues.text: PAOLO GALLUZZI: Florence was one of the most advanced social organization of the planet.
cues.en: PAOLO GALLUZZI: Florence was one of the most advanced social organization of the planet.
cues.zh: 保羅‧加盧齊：佛羅倫斯是地球上最先進的社會組織之一。

cues.text: Very wealthy city.
cues.en: Very wealthy city.
cues.zh: 非常富有的城市。

cues.text: A city that was attracting the brightest guys around.
cues.en: A city that was attracting the brightest guys around.
cues.zh: 這座城市吸引了周圍最聰明的人。

cues.text: KEMP: Florence is just extraordinary at this time, to produce Donatello, Masaccio, Brunelleschi,
cues.en: KEMP: Florence is just extraordinary at this time, to produce Donatello, Masaccio, Brunelleschi,
cues.zh: 坎普：此時的佛羅倫斯非常出色，誕生了多納泰羅、馬薩喬、布魯內萊斯基、

cues.text: Michelangelo, Raphael.
cues.en: Michelangelo, Raphael.
cues.zh: 米開朗基羅、拉斐爾。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: With no formal education, Leonardo started as an apprentice
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: With no formal education, Leonardo started as an apprentice
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：李奧納多沒有受過正規教育，一開始就是學徒

cues.text: in one of the leading artist's studios of the day: the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio.
cues.en: in one of the leading artist's studios of the day: the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio.
cues.zh: 在當今頂尖藝術家的工作室之一：Andrea del Verrocchio 的工作室。

cues.text: was a sculptor above all, but also a painter, an architect.
cues.en: was a sculptor above all, but also a painter, an architect.
cues.zh: 首先是一位雕塑家，同時也是一位畫家、建築師。

cues.text: He could play music.
cues.en: He could play music.
cues.zh: 他可以演奏音樂。

cues.text: ♪ So the example of Verrocchio was very important
cues.en: ♪ So the example of Verrocchio was very important
cues.zh: ♪ 所以韋羅基奧的例子非常重要

cues.text: to Leonardo.
cues.en: to Leonardo.
cues.zh: 給萊昂納多。

cues.text: Leonardo's training with Verrocchio is a real model of how an artist should evolve.
cues.en: Leonardo's training with Verrocchio is a real model of how an artist should evolve.
cues.zh: 列奧納多與韋羅基奧的訓練是藝術家如何發展的真實典範。

cues.text: Technique is subordinate to the act of seeing.
cues.en: Technique is subordinate to the act of seeing.
cues.zh: 技術從屬於觀察行為。

cues.text: It's about the eye, and it's Leonardo who first described that.
cues.en: It's about the eye, and it's Leonardo who first described that.
cues.zh: 這是關於眼睛的，萊昂納多首先描述了這一點。

cues.text: NARRATOR: It is believed the handsome model for this Verrocchio statue of David
cues.en: NARRATOR: It is believed the handsome model for this Verrocchio statue of David
cues.zh: 旁白：人們相信這座韋羅基奧大衛雕像的英俊模特

cues.text: is his apprentice, a young Leonardo.
cues.en: is his apprentice, a young Leonardo.
cues.zh: 是他的學徒，年輕的李奧納多。

cues.text: So, they think that Leonardo posed for his master.
cues.en: So, they think that Leonardo posed for his master.
cues.zh: 所以，他們認為萊昂納多是為他的主人擺姿勢的。

cues.text: It's a very elegant boy face framed by these beautiful curls.
cues.en: It's a very elegant boy face framed by these beautiful curls.
cues.zh: 這是一張非常優雅的男孩臉，被美麗的捲髮所包圍。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Despite the circumstances of his illegitimate birth, the workshop gave Leonardo a way to get ahead in life.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Despite the circumstances of his illegitimate birth, the workshop gave Leonardo a way to get ahead in life.
cues.zh: 旁白：儘管李奧納多是非婚生，但研討會為他提供了一條在生活中取得成功的方法。

cues.text: ISAACSON: He's a misfit.
cues.en: ISAACSON: He's a misfit.
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：他不合群。

cues.text: He's illegitimate.
cues.en: He's illegitimate.
cues.zh: 他是非法的。

cues.text: He's gay, he's left-handed, he's a vegetarian, he's distracted,
cues.en: He's gay, he's left-handed, he's a vegetarian, he's distracted,
cues.zh: 他是同性戀，他是左撇子，他是素食主義者，他心不在焉，

cues.text: and yet he's embraced by the people of Florence because it was a very tolerant city.
cues.en: and yet he's embraced by the people of Florence because it was a very tolerant city.
cues.zh: 然而，他受到了佛羅倫薩人民的歡迎，因為這是一個非常寬容的城市。

cues.text: NARRATOR: One of the most challenging construction projects of the day
cues.en: NARRATOR: One of the most challenging construction projects of the day
cues.zh: 旁白：當今最具挑戰性的建設專案之一

cues.text: was capping the dome of the breathtaking cathedral with a golden sphere.
cues.en: was capping the dome of the breathtaking cathedral with a golden sphere.
cues.zh: 正在用金色的球體覆蓋令人驚嘆的大教堂的圓頂。

cues.text: The commission of the crowning of the cupola
cues.en: The commission of the crowning of the cupola
cues.zh: 圓頂加冕委託

cues.text: with a gilded sphere was a very important one.
cues.en: with a gilded sphere was a very important one.
cues.zh: 鍍金球體是一個非常重要的。

cues.text: And that's a commission that Verrocchio secured.
cues.en: And that's a commission that Verrocchio secured.
cues.zh: 這就是韋羅基奧獲得的佣金。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Verrocchio's team, which included a young Leonardo,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Verrocchio's team, which included a young Leonardo,
cues.zh: 旁白：韋羅基奧的團隊，其中包括年輕的李奧納多，

cues.text: had to figure out not only the design, but also how to secure the one-and-a-half-ton ball
cues.en: had to figure out not only the design, but also how to secure the one-and-a-half-ton ball
cues.zh: 不僅要弄清楚設計，還要弄清楚如何固定一噸半的球

cues.text: on top of the nearly 370-foot high cathedral.
cues.en: on top of the nearly 370-foot high cathedral.
cues.zh: 在近370英尺高的大教堂頂部。

cues.text: ISAACSON: Figuring out how to get the ball on top of the cathedral helps Leonardo become a great engineer.
cues.en: ISAACSON: Figuring out how to get the ball on top of the cathedral helps Leonardo become a great engineer.
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：弄清楚如何讓球到達大教堂頂部有助於萊昂納多成為一名偉大的工程師。

cues.text: It helps him become an artist, because he gets the perspective of the ball right.
cues.en: It helps him become an artist, because he gets the perspective of the ball right.
cues.zh: 這幫助他成為藝術家，因為他對球的看法是正確的。

cues.text: That combination of science, engineering, and art becomes part of who Leonardo da Vinci is.
cues.en: That combination of science, engineering, and art becomes part of who Leonardo da Vinci is.
cues.zh: 科學、工程和藝術的結合成為李奧納多·達文西的一部分。

cues.text: NARRATOR: In fact, in sheer quantity, Leonardo's scientific investigations
cues.en: NARRATOR: In fact, in sheer quantity, Leonardo's scientific investigations
cues.zh: 旁白：事實上，從數量上看，列奧納多的科學研究

cues.text: far outweigh his output of paintings.
cues.en: far outweigh his output of paintings.
cues.zh: 遠遠超過了他的繪畫作品。

cues.text: The proof of that lies in a remarkable collection
cues.en: The proof of that lies in a remarkable collection
cues.zh: 證明這一點的證據在於非凡的收藏

cues.text: of replicas of his notebooks.
cues.en: of replicas of his notebooks.
cues.zh: 他的筆記本的複製品。

cues.text: GALLUZZI: We have very few records, in the whole history of science,
cues.en: GALLUZZI: We have very few records, in the whole history of science,
cues.zh: 加盧齊：在整個科學史上，我們的記錄非常少，

cues.text: similar to Leonardo's manuscripts.
cues.en: similar to Leonardo's manuscripts.
cues.zh: 與列奧納多的手稿相似。

cues.text: These are not books.
cues.en: These are not books.
cues.zh: 這些不是書。

cues.text: You cannot compare that to a work of, by Galileo or by Newton,
cues.en: You cannot compare that to a work of, by Galileo or by Newton,
cues.zh: 你不能將其與伽利略或牛頓的著作進行比較，

cues.text: because they have solved the problems before writing their books.
cues.en: because they have solved the problems before writing their books.
cues.zh: 因為他們在寫書之前就已經解決了問題。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Paolo Galluzzi is the director of the Galileo Museum in Florence.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Paolo Galluzzi is the director of the Galileo Museum in Florence.
cues.zh: 旁白：保羅‧加魯齊 (Paolo Galluzzi) 是佛羅倫斯伽利略博物館的館長。

cues.text: GALLUZZI: What we have in Leonardo is the direct expression of his internal dialogue.
cues.en: GALLUZZI: What we have in Leonardo is the direct expression of his internal dialogue.
cues.zh: 加盧齊：李奧納多的特點是他內心對話的直接表達。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's notebooks span his lifetime.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's notebooks span his lifetime.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多的筆記本貫穿了他的一生。

cues.text: They even come pocket-sized.
cues.en: They even come pocket-sized.
cues.zh: 它們甚至是口袋大小的。

cues.text: BORGO: We're sure that those 6,000 pages that we have are by him.
cues.en: BORGO: We're sure that those 6,000 pages that we have are by him.
cues.zh: BORGO：我們確信我們擁有的那 6,000 頁是他寫的。

cues.text: And this is just one-fourth of what he actually penned.
cues.en: And this is just one-fourth of what he actually penned.
cues.zh: 這只是他實際寫下的四分之一。

cues.text: So we're talking about something he was obsessed by throughout his life.
cues.en: So we're talking about something he was obsessed by throughout his life.
cues.zh: 所以我們正在談論他一生都痴迷的事情。

cues.text: NARRATOR: The brilliance and breadth of Leonardo's notebooks is astonishing.
cues.en: NARRATOR: The brilliance and breadth of Leonardo's notebooks is astonishing.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多筆記本的才華和廣度令人驚嘆。

cues.text: His ideas seem to predict our modern age,
cues.en: His ideas seem to predict our modern age,
cues.zh: 他的思想似乎預示著我們的現代，

cues.text: making Leonardo much more than a Renaissance scientist for many.
cues.en: making Leonardo much more than a Renaissance scientist for many.
cues.zh: 對許多人來說，李奧納多不僅僅是一位文藝復興時期的科學家。

cues.text: His dreams of human flight include a helicopter-like machine
cues.en: His dreams of human flight include a helicopter-like machine
cues.zh: 他的人類飛行夢想包括一架像直升機一樣的機器

cues.text: and a parachute.
cues.en: and a parachute.
cues.zh: 和降落傘。

cues.text: A fascination with water led to ambitious civil engineering proposals.
cues.en: A fascination with water led to ambitious civil engineering proposals.
cues.zh: 對水的迷戀催生了雄心勃勃的土木工程提案。

cues.text: ♪ And he conceived an intriguing self-propelled machine
cues.en: ♪ And he conceived an intriguing self-propelled machine
cues.zh: ♪ 他構思了一種有趣的自走式機器

cues.text: that seems part-automobile, part-early robot.
cues.en: that seems part-automobile, part-early robot.
cues.zh: 這看起來一半是汽車，一半是早期機器人。

cues.text: But could any of these inventive designs have actually worked?
cues.en: But could any of these inventive designs have actually worked?
cues.zh: 但這些創意的設計真的能發揮作用嗎？

cues.text: JOHN OCHSENDORF: Leonardo is, of course, a great artist,
cues.en: JOHN OCHSENDORF: Leonardo is, of course, a great artist,
cues.zh: 約翰‧奧克森多夫：李奧納多當然是一位偉大的藝術家，

cues.text: but he's also a great scientist, and, I would argue, a great engineer.
cues.en: but he's also a great scientist, and, I would argue, a great engineer.
cues.zh: 但他也是一位偉大的科學家，而且，我認為，他也是一位偉大的工程師。

cues.text: The geometry is stunning...
cues.en: The geometry is stunning...
cues.zh: 幾何形狀令人驚嘆...

cues.text: NARRATOR: One small sketch in Leonardo's notebooks has so intrigued M.I.T. engineer John Ochsendorf
cues.en: NARRATOR: One small sketch in Leonardo's notebooks has so intrigued M.I.T. engineer John Ochsendorf
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多筆記本上的一幅小草圖引起了麻省理工學院的興趣。工程師約翰‧奧克森多夫

cues.text: that he asked his graduate student Karly Bast to bring 21st-century engineering rigor
cues.en: that he asked his graduate student Karly Bast to bring 21st-century engineering rigor
cues.zh: 他要求他的研究生 Karly Bast 帶來 21 世紀的工程嚴謹性

cues.text: to see if Leonardo's 16th-century idea would in fact stand.
cues.en: to see if Leonardo's 16th-century idea would in fact stand.
cues.zh: 看看列奧納多 16 世紀的想法是否真的成立。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: There is a historical reason for this, because you see it in the drawing, right?
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: There is a historical reason for this, because you see it in the drawing, right?
cues.zh: OCHSENDORF：這是有歷史原因的，因為你在圖中看到了，對吧？

cues.text: BAST: Yeah, these two aren't...
cues.en: BAST: Yeah, these two aren't...
cues.zh: BAST：是的，這兩個人不是…

cues.text: NARRATOR: In 1502, the year before starting the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: NARRATOR: In 1502, the year before starting the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 旁白：1502 年，也就是《蒙娜麗莎》創作的前一年，

cues.text: Leonardo proposed to the sultan of the Ottoman Empire
cues.en: Leonardo proposed to the sultan of the Ottoman Empire
cues.zh: 列奧納多向鄂圖曼帝國蘇丹求婚

cues.text: a bridge in Constantinople five times longer than any other span at the time.
cues.en: a bridge in Constantinople five times longer than any other span at the time.
cues.zh: 君士坦丁堡的一座橋比當時任何其他橋樑的長度都要長五倍。

cues.text: ♪ His plan for this ambitious project, sketched upside-down in a small notebook,
cues.en: ♪ His plan for this ambitious project, sketched upside-down in a small notebook,
cues.zh: ♪ 他對這個雄心勃勃的專案的計劃，倒掛在一個小筆記本上，

cues.text: offers few details-- yet just enough for Bast to bring it to life.
cues.en: offers few details-- yet just enough for Bast to bring it to life.
cues.zh: 提供的細節很少，但足以讓巴斯特將其變為現實。

cues.text: Leonardo provided four measurements, but he provided two sketches.
cues.en: Leonardo provided four measurements, but he provided two sketches.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多提供了四種測量結果，但他提供了兩張草圖。

cues.text: At first, it seems like a rough sketch, but as I dug into it,
cues.en: At first, it seems like a rough sketch, but as I dug into it,
cues.zh: 乍一看，這似乎是一個粗略的草圖，但當我深入研究它時，

cues.text: I realized there was a reason for every decision and every line.
cues.en: I realized there was a reason for every decision and every line.
cues.zh: 我意識到每一個決定和每一條路線都是有原因的。

cues.text: There was a lot of thought put into the force distribution, and it wasn't just aesthetic.
cues.en: There was a lot of thought put into the force distribution, and it wasn't just aesthetic.
cues.zh: 在力量分配上花了很多心思，而不僅僅是美觀。

cues.text: It was engineering.
cues.en: It was engineering.
cues.zh: 這是工程學。

cues.text: NARRATOR: And to test that engineering, Bast and her colleagues have built a scale model of the bridge
cues.en: NARRATOR: And to test that engineering, Bast and her colleagues have built a scale model of the bridge
cues.zh: 旁白：為了測試這項工程，巴斯特和她的同事們建造了一座橋樑的比例模型

cues.text: with a state-of-the-art 3-D printer.
cues.en: with a state-of-the-art 3-D printer.
cues.zh: 配備最先進的 3D 列印機。

cues.text: MOHAMED ISMAIL: Before 3-D printing came along, we'd have to try to build that bridge
cues.en: MOHAMED ISMAIL: Before 3-D printing came along, we'd have to try to build that bridge
cues.zh: MOHAMED ISMAIL：在 3D 列印出現之前，我們必須嘗試建造這座橋樑

cues.text: as close as we could to the full scale, because you couldn't reliably get the geometry quite right.
cues.en: as close as we could to the full scale, because you couldn't reliably get the geometry quite right.
cues.zh: 盡可能接近全尺寸，因為你無法可靠地獲得完全正確的幾何形狀。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's stone bridge would have been 500 times the size of this model,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's stone bridge would have been 500 times the size of this model,
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多的石橋尺寸是這個模型的 500 倍，

cues.text: but the physics are exactly the same.
cues.en: but the physics are exactly the same.
cues.zh: 但物理原理是完全相同的。

cues.text: BAST: We have the bridge, and we have the mold that's holding it up.
cues.en: BAST: We have the bridge, and we have the mold that's holding it up.
cues.zh: BAST：我們有這座橋，我們有支撐它的模具。

cues.text: The first piece should be easy to take off.
cues.en: The first piece should be easy to take off.
cues.zh: 第一件應該很容易脫下來。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Piece by piece, she removes the Styrofoam--
cues.en: NARRATOR: Piece by piece, she removes the Styrofoam--
cues.zh: 旁白：她一點一點地除去聚苯乙烯泡沫塑膠——

cues.text: a modern day stand-in for the wooden scaffolding used in Leonardo's day.
cues.en: a modern day stand-in for the wooden scaffolding used in Leonardo's day.
cues.zh: 達文西時代使用的木製鷹架的現代替代品。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: This is more like heart surgery than bridge construction.
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: This is more like heart surgery than bridge construction.
cues.zh: 奧克森多夫：這更像是心臟手術而不是橋樑建設。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Finally, the last support is removed.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Finally, the last support is removed.
cues.zh: 旁白：最後，最後一個支撐物被移除了。

cues.text: ♪ And Leonardo's stone bridge stands.
cues.en: ♪ And Leonardo's stone bridge stands.
cues.zh: ♪ 列奧納多的石橋矗立著。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: The geometry is aesthetically beautiful, and the fact that this is standing on its own
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: The geometry is aesthetically beautiful, and the fact that this is standing on its own
cues.zh: OCHSENDORF：幾何形狀非常美觀，而且它是獨立的

cues.text: tells us that it was feasible.
cues.en: tells us that it was feasible.
cues.zh: 告訴我們這是可行的。

cues.text: BAST: Absolutely.
cues.en: BAST: Absolutely.
cues.zh: 巴斯特：當然。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: Wow.
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: Wow.
cues.zh: 奧克森多夫：哇。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's bridge even stays up when they simulate an earthquake.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's bridge even stays up when they simulate an earthquake.
cues.zh: 旁白：當他們模擬地震時，李奧納多的橋甚至保持不動。

cues.text: Stop.
cues.en: Stop.
cues.zh: 停止。

cues.text: BAST: 1,500 pounds.
cues.en: BAST: 1,500 pounds.
cues.zh: BAST：1,500 磅。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: Oh, my God.
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: Oh, my God.
cues.zh: 奧森多夫：哦，天啊。

cues.text: It has moved by 30 feet, and the arch still stands.
cues.en: It has moved by 30 feet, and the arch still stands.
cues.zh: 它已經移動了 30 英尺，但拱門仍然矗立著。

cues.text: NARRATOR: The bridge does eventually collapse, but only after being moved the equivalent of 50 feet.
cues.en: NARRATOR: The bridge does eventually collapse, but only after being moved the equivalent of 50 feet.
cues.zh: 旁白：這座橋最終確實倒塌了，但只是在移動了 50 英尺之後。

cues.text: Leonardo has the artistic ability, and he also has that scientific knowledge
cues.en: Leonardo has the artistic ability, and he also has that scientific knowledge
cues.zh: 列奧納多有藝術才能，也有科學知識

cues.text: and that engineering capability where he can create things
cues.en: and that engineering capability where he can create things
cues.zh: 以及他可以創造事物的工程能力

cues.text: that are beautiful and structurally sound.
cues.en: that are beautiful and structurally sound.
cues.zh: 它們既美觀又結構合理。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Bast clearly had to fill in some details to get from this sketch
cues.en: NARRATOR: Bast clearly had to fill in some details to get from this sketch
cues.zh: 旁白：巴斯特顯然必須填寫一些細節才能從這個草圖中獲得

cues.text: to this model.
cues.en: to this model.
cues.zh: 到這個模型。

cues.text: And we don't know if the bridge could have been built with the wooden scaffold of the day.
cues.en: And we don't know if the bridge could have been built with the wooden scaffold of the day.
cues.zh: 我們不知道這座橋是否可以用當時的木鷹架建造。

cues.text: And he also shows...
cues.en: And he also shows...
cues.zh: 而且他還表明...

cues.text: NARRATOR: But she has shown Leonardo got the basic physics right.
cues.en: NARRATOR: But she has shown Leonardo got the basic physics right.
cues.zh: 旁白：但她已經向李奧納多證明瞭基本物理學的正確性。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: What's extraordinary is the ideas that he was coming up with more than 500 years ago.
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: What's extraordinary is the ideas that he was coming up with more than 500 years ago.
cues.zh: OCHSENDORF：非凡之處在於他 500 多年前提出的想法。

cues.text: Yep.
cues.en: Yep.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.text: OCHSENDORF: We're still trying to understand them.
cues.en: OCHSENDORF: We're still trying to understand them.
cues.zh: OCHSENDORF：我們仍在努力瞭解它們。

cues.text: ♪ NARRATOR: As with this ambitious proposal to the sultan,
cues.en: ♪ NARRATOR: As with this ambitious proposal to the sultan,
cues.zh: ♪ 旁白：正如向蘇丹提出的這項雄心勃勃的提議一樣，

cues.text: Leonardo sought out wealthy patrons throughout his life to support not only his art, but his scientific explorations.
cues.en: Leonardo sought out wealthy patrons throughout his life to support not only his art, but his scientific explorations.
cues.zh: 列奧納多一生都在尋找富有的贊助人，不僅支援他的藝術，也支援他的科學探索。

cues.text: At 30, he moved to Milan to work for its duke.
cues.en: At 30, he moved to Milan to work for its duke.
cues.zh: 30歲時，他搬到米蘭為公爵工作。

cues.text: 17 years later, when the duke was deposed, Leonardo had to move once again,
cues.en: 17 years later, when the duke was deposed, Leonardo had to move once again,
cues.zh: 17年後，公爵被廢黜，列奧納多不得不再次搬遷，

cues.text: back to Florence, and later, Rome.
cues.en: back to Florence, and later, Rome.
cues.zh: 回到佛羅倫斯，後來又回到羅馬。

cues.text: His accomplishments in science and art meant he had much to offer.
cues.en: His accomplishments in science and art meant he had much to offer.
cues.zh: 他在科學和藝術方面的成就意味著他可以做出很多貢獻。

cues.text: ISAACSON: Leonardo sells himself as an engineer, as well as an artist,
cues.en: ISAACSON: Leonardo sells himself as an engineer, as well as an artist,
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：李奧納多將自己推銷為工程師和藝術家，

cues.text: because he knows he can make a better living.
cues.en: because he knows he can make a better living.
cues.zh: 因為他知道他可以過更好的生活。

cues.text: But also, I think, Leonardo just loved the connection of the arts and sciences,
cues.en: But also, I think, Leonardo just loved the connection of the arts and sciences,
cues.zh: 但我認為，列奧納多隻是喜歡藝術與科學的聯絡，

cues.text: and he didn't want to have to be siloed as just a painter.
cues.en: and he didn't want to have to be siloed as just a painter.
cues.zh: 他不想被孤立為一名畫家。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's explorations in science can also be clearly seen in the details of his paintings.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's explorations in science can also be clearly seen in the details of his paintings.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多對科學的探索也可以從他的繪畫細節中清楚看出。

cues.text: He studied everything from botany to the physics of flowing water.
cues.en: He studied everything from botany to the physics of flowing water.
cues.zh: 他研究了從植物學到流水物理學的所有知識。

cues.text: Even the curls of human hair.
cues.en: Even the curls of human hair.
cues.zh: 甚至人類的捲髮。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: To paint something absolutely perfect, he had to understand how nature was done.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: To paint something absolutely perfect, he had to understand how nature was done.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：為了畫出絕對完美的東西，他必須瞭解大自然是如何完成的。

cues.text: To paint a mountain, to paint rocks, he had to understand why the rocks were of that kind.
cues.en: To paint a mountain, to paint rocks, he had to understand why the rocks were of that kind.
cues.zh: 要畫山、畫石頭，他必須明白為什麼石頭是這樣的。

cues.text: He was obsessed with that.
cues.en: He was obsessed with that.
cues.zh: 他對此很著迷。

cues.text: And that was what he called the science of painting.
cues.en: And that was what he called the science of painting.
cues.zh: 這就是他所說的繪畫科學。

cues.text: NARRATOR: The science of painting was all-encompassing for Leonardo.
cues.en: NARRATOR: The science of painting was all-encompassing for Leonardo.
cues.zh: 旁白：對李奧納多來說，繪畫科學是包羅永珍的。

cues.text: But how could he capture the beauty he observed in nature with paint?
cues.en: But how could he capture the beauty he observed in nature with paint?
cues.zh: 但他怎麼能用顏料捕捉到他在大自然中觀察到的美麗呢？

cues.text: ♪ Back at the Louvre, art restorers and researchers
cues.en: ♪ Back at the Louvre, art restorers and researchers
cues.zh: ♪ 回到羅浮宮，藝術修復者和研究人員

cues.text: are uncovering new clues in an elegant intensive care unit
cues.en: are uncovering new clues in an elegant intensive care unit
cues.zh: 在優雅的重症監護室中發現新的線索

cues.text: for priceless works of art.
cues.en: for priceless works of art.
cues.zh: 為無價的藝術作品。

cues.text: ♪ To prepare for the upcoming exhibit, Delieuvin and the team of scientists
cues.en: ♪ To prepare for the upcoming exhibit, Delieuvin and the team of scientists
cues.zh: ♪ 為了準備即將到來的展覽，Delieuvin 和科學家團隊

cues.text: are restoring a painting long shrouded by controversy.
cues.en: are restoring a painting long shrouded by controversy.
cues.zh: 正在修復一幅長期飽受爭議的畫作。

cues.text: For centuries, this portrait of Bacchus was considered one of the few paintings by Leonardo's hand.
cues.en: For centuries, this portrait of Bacchus was considered one of the few paintings by Leonardo's hand.
cues.zh: 幾個世紀以來，這幅巴克斯肖像被認為是列奧納多親手繪製的為數不多的畫作之一。

cues.text: But now, experts aren't so sure.
cues.en: But now, experts aren't so sure.
cues.zh: 但現在，專家們不太確定。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: For centuries, that painting was attributed to Leonardo.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: For centuries, that painting was attributed to Leonardo.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：幾個世紀以來，這幅畫被認為是李奧納多的作品。

cues.text: But during the 20th century, some historians said, "Well, it looks like difference
cues.en: But during the 20th century, some historians said, "Well, it looks like difference
cues.zh: 但在 20 世紀，一些歷史學家說：「嗯，這看起來像是差異

cues.text: compared to the other paintings." NARRATOR: Cinzia Pasquali has been brought in
cues.en: compared to the other paintings." NARRATOR: Cinzia Pasquali has been brought in
cues.zh: 與其他畫作相比。 」旁白：Cinzia Pasquali 已被帶入

cues.text: to restore the painting.
cues.en: to restore the painting.
cues.zh: 來恢復這幅畫。

cues.text: Can Leonardo's unique scientific techniques provide the clue she needs to finally solve the mystery:
cues.en: Can Leonardo's unique scientific techniques provide the clue she needs to finally solve the mystery:
cues.zh: 萊昂納多獨特的科學技術能否提供她最終解開謎團所需的線索：

cues.text: did Leonardo in fact paint this?
cues.en: did Leonardo in fact paint this?
cues.zh: 這真的是李奧納多畫的嗎？

cues.text: PASQUALI: NARRATOR: Restoration work is not for the faint of heart.
cues.en: PASQUALI: NARRATOR: Restoration work is not for the faint of heart.
cues.zh: 帕斯誇裡：旁白：修復工作不適合膽小的人。

cues.text: This painting may be in bad shape, but Pasquali is still taking her scalpel
cues.en: This painting may be in bad shape, but Pasquali is still taking her scalpel
cues.zh: 這幅畫的形狀可能很糟糕，但帕斯卡利仍然拿著她的手術刀

cues.text: to an irreplaceable masterpiece.
cues.en: to an irreplaceable masterpiece.
cues.zh: 成為無可取代的傑作。

cues.text: She scrapes away the yellow darkened varnish, revealing a vibrant color beneath.
cues.en: She scrapes away the yellow darkened varnish, revealing a vibrant color beneath.
cues.zh: 她刮掉黃色深色清漆，露出底下鮮豔的顏色。

cues.text: NARRATOR: But other parts of the painting appear more damaged.
cues.en: NARRATOR: But other parts of the painting appear more damaged.
cues.zh: 旁白：但是畫作的其他部分似乎受到了更多損壞。

cues.text: So Pasquali must rely on her training not only in art history,
cues.en: So Pasquali must rely on her training not only in art history,
cues.zh: 所以帕斯誇裡不僅要依靠她在藝術史的訓練，

cues.text: but also chemistry.
cues.en: but also chemistry.
cues.zh: 還有化學。

cues.text: ♪ The colors of pigment in paint can change or fade over time.
cues.en: ♪ The colors of pigment in paint can change or fade over time.
cues.zh: ♪ 油漆中顏料的顏色會隨著時間的推移而改變或褪色。

cues.text: But the chemistry of the pigments themselves can still be detected.
cues.en: But the chemistry of the pigments themselves can still be detected.
cues.zh: 但顏料本身的化學性質仍然可以被檢測到。

cues.text: Pasquali orders a special scan for the element copper,
cues.en: Pasquali orders a special scan for the element copper,
cues.zh: 帕斯誇利下令對銅元素進行特殊掃描，

cues.text: often used in green paint.
cues.en: often used in green paint.
cues.zh: 常用於綠色塗料。

cues.text: The scan reveals this dark area of the painting
cues.en: The scan reveals this dark area of the painting
cues.zh: 掃描顯示了畫作的這個黑暗區域

cues.text: was once a lush garden, until the copper in the paint darkened.
cues.en: was once a lush garden, until the copper in the paint darkened.
cues.zh: 曾經是一座鬱鬱蔥蔥的花園，直到油漆中的銅色變暗。

cues.text: PASQUALI: So we can see a lot of vegetable and leaves and plants and flower,
cues.en: PASQUALI: So we can see a lot of vegetable and leaves and plants and flower,
cues.zh: 帕斯誇裡：所以我們可以看到很多蔬菜、葉子、植物和花朵，

cues.text: and when you look on the surface of the work, they are not.
cues.en: and when you look on the surface of the work, they are not.
cues.zh: 當你看作品的表面時，你會發現它們並非如此。

cues.text: NARRATOR: While the beauty of these plants may suggest Leonardo's meticulous attention to detail,
cues.en: NARRATOR: While the beauty of these plants may suggest Leonardo's meticulous attention to detail,
cues.zh: 旁白：雖然這些植物的美麗可能顯示了李奧納多對細節的一絲不苟，

cues.text: that's not enough to say for sure he painted it himself.
cues.en: that's not enough to say for sure he painted it himself.
cues.zh: 這還不足以肯定地說這是他自己畫的。

cues.text: So the investigation turns to his brushwork.
cues.en: So the investigation turns to his brushwork.
cues.zh: 於是調查轉向他的筆觸。

cues.text: One of the most characteristic fingerprints of a Leonardo are remarkably thin layers of paint,
cues.en: One of the most characteristic fingerprints of a Leonardo are remarkably thin layers of paint,
cues.zh: 達文西最具特色的指紋之一是非常薄的油漆層，

cues.text: which can only be seen with a powerful microscope.
cues.en: which can only be seen with a powerful microscope.
cues.zh: 使用高倍顯微鏡才能看到。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Some Leonardos have been found to have as many as 30 layers of paint--
cues.en: NARRATOR: Some Leonardos have been found to have as many as 30 layers of paint--
cues.zh: 旁白：一些列奧納多被發現有多達 30 層油漆——

cues.text: many more than most painters.
cues.en: many more than most painters.
cues.zh: 比大多數畫家多得多。

cues.text: As she continues her restoration, Pasquali is looking for evidence of this unusual technique.
cues.en: As she continues her restoration, Pasquali is looking for evidence of this unusual technique.
cues.zh: 在繼續修復過程中，帕斯誇裡正在尋找這種不尋常技術的證據。

cues.text: But what was Leonardo trying to achieve with all those thin layers?
cues.en: But what was Leonardo trying to achieve with all those thin layers?
cues.zh: 但李奧納多試圖用這些薄層來實現什麼目的呢？

cues.text: Just ask a living painter.
cues.en: Just ask a living painter.
cues.zh: 只要問問活著的畫家就知道了。

cues.text: FLORENT FARGES: Da Vinci was always looking for beauty.
cues.en: FLORENT FARGES: Da Vinci was always looking for beauty.
cues.zh: FLORENT FARGES：達文西一直在尋找美。

cues.text: He's not just painting or drawing a tree.
cues.en: He's not just painting or drawing a tree.
cues.zh: 他不只是在畫畫或畫一棵樹。

cues.text: He wants to paint the perfect expression of what a tree is.
cues.en: He wants to paint the perfect expression of what a tree is.
cues.zh: 他想完美地表達一棵樹的本質。

cues.text: This aspiration to beauty is, to me, very inspiring as an artist.
cues.en: This aspiration to beauty is, to me, very inspiring as an artist.
cues.zh: 對我來說，身為藝術家，這種對美的渴望非常鼓舞人心。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Florent Farges is a painter in Dijon, France.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Florent Farges is a painter in Dijon, France.
cues.zh: 旁白：弗洛倫特·法格斯是法國第戎的畫家。

cues.text: In the tradition of the Renaissance, Farges runs an artist's workshop,
cues.en: In the tradition of the Renaissance, Farges runs an artist's workshop,
cues.zh: 秉承文藝復興的傳統，法吉斯經營藝術家工作室，

cues.text: but with a twist.
cues.en: but with a twist.
cues.zh: 但有一個轉折。

cues.text: FARGES: Hello, everyone, and welcome to a new video.
cues.en: FARGES: Hello, everyone, and welcome to a new video.
cues.zh: FARGES：大家好，歡迎觀看新影片。

cues.text: NARRATOR: His is a virtual one.
cues.en: NARRATOR: His is a virtual one.
cues.zh: 旁白：他是虛擬的。

cues.text: FARGES: This one is going to guide you through the entire process of classical figure painting.
cues.en: FARGES: This one is going to guide you through the entire process of classical figure painting.
cues.zh: FARGES：這篇將引導你完成古典人物畫的整個過程。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Most Italian painters at the time mixed their pigments into an egg base,
cues.en: NARRATOR: Most Italian painters at the time mixed their pigments into an egg base,
cues.zh: 旁白：當時大多數義大利畫家都會將顏料混合到蛋底中，

cues.text: using real egg.
cues.en: using real egg.
cues.zh: 使用真正的雞蛋。

cues.text: But egg tempera doesn't allow as much light to pass through it,
cues.en: But egg tempera doesn't allow as much light to pass through it,
cues.zh: 但蛋彩畫不允許那麼多光線穿過，

cues.text: so there is less depth in the painting.
cues.en: so there is less depth in the painting.
cues.zh: 所以這幅畫的深度較少。

cues.text: Instead, Leonardo decided to use an oil, like linseed or walnut.
cues.en: Instead, Leonardo decided to use an oil, like linseed or walnut.
cues.zh: 相反，李奧納多決定使用亞麻仁油或核桃油。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo was using oil.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Leonardo was using oil.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：李奧納多使用的是石油。

cues.text: Because oil helps to reproduce in the best way
cues.en: Because oil helps to reproduce in the best way
cues.zh: 因為油有助於以最佳方式繁殖

cues.text: the transition between light and shadow.
cues.en: the transition between light and shadow.
cues.zh: 光與影之間的過渡。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Gradually, Farges' portrait comes to life.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Gradually, Farges' portrait comes to life.
cues.zh: 旁白：漸漸地，法吉斯的肖像變得栩栩如生。

cues.text: For the finishing touches, Farges demonstrates how oil paint
cues.en: For the finishing touches, Farges demonstrates how oil paint
cues.zh: 對於最後的潤色，法格斯示範如何使用油畫顏料

cues.text: can be applied very thinly to create a subtle shading of light
cues.en: can be applied very thinly to create a subtle shading of light
cues.zh: 可以非常薄地塗抹以產生微妙的光影效果

cues.text: falling across the human body.
cues.en: falling across the human body.
cues.zh: 落在人體。

cues.text: FARGES: If I want, I can come back later and put another layer on top of that,
cues.en: FARGES: If I want, I can come back later and put another layer on top of that,
cues.zh: FARGES：如果我願意，我可以稍後再回來，在上面再放一層，

cues.text: to make this transition very soft.
cues.en: to make this transition very soft.
cues.zh: 讓這種過渡非常柔和。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's techniques are still being taught today
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's techniques are still being taught today
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多的技術至今仍在教授

cues.text: in his hometown of Florence.
cues.en: in his hometown of Florence.
cues.zh: 在他的家鄉佛羅倫薩。

cues.text: To make their paintings come alive, artists strive to capture human flesh
cues.en: To make their paintings come alive, artists strive to capture human flesh
cues.zh: 為了讓畫作栩栩如生，藝術家們努力捕捉人肉

cues.text: and the way light reveals its shape.
cues.en: and the way light reveals its shape.
cues.zh: 以及光揭示其形狀的方式。

cues.text: CECIL: Leonardo speaks about the smoky transition of light to shade.
cues.en: CECIL: Leonardo speaks about the smoky transition of light to shade.
cues.zh: 塞西爾：李奧納多談到了光與影的煙霧過渡。

cues.text: That's how we perceive in nature.
cues.en: That's how we perceive in nature.
cues.zh: 這就是我們感知自然的方式。

cues.text: The problem often with photographic images we see is that there's so much detail,
cues.en: The problem often with photographic images we see is that there's so much detail,
cues.zh: 我們看到的攝影影像經常出現的問題是細節太多，

cues.text: we don't get the broader effect.
cues.en: we don't get the broader effect.
cues.zh: 我們沒有得到更廣泛的影響。

cues.text: We see life very much out of focus-- we glance.
cues.en: We see life very much out of focus-- we glance.
cues.zh: 我們對生活的看法非常模糊——我們只是掃一眼。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Other artists of the day, like Sandro Botticelli, painted figures with hard outlines.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Other artists of the day, like Sandro Botticelli, painted figures with hard outlines.
cues.zh: 旁白：當時其他的藝術家，如桑德羅·波提切利，都用硬朗的輪廓描繪人物。

cues.text: But Leonardo used his fine layers to create soft transitions, obscuring the lines.
cues.en: But Leonardo used his fine layers to create soft transitions, obscuring the lines.
cues.zh: 但萊昂納多利用他精細的圖層來創造柔和的過渡，模糊了線條。

cues.text: This is his signature look, called "sfumato," from the Italian "fumo," or smoke.
cues.en: This is his signature look, called "sfumato," from the Italian "fumo," or smoke.
cues.zh: 這是他的標誌性造型，稱為“sfumato”，源自義大利語“fumo”，即煙霧。

cues.text: Unquestionably, the most famous example of Leonardo's sfumato
cues.en: Unquestionably, the most famous example of Leonardo's sfumato
cues.zh: 毫無疑問，最著名的達文西暈染法例子

cues.text: is that enigmatic smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.en: is that enigmatic smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.zh: 就是「蒙娜麗莎」那神秘的微笑。

cues.text: DELIEUVIN: Just look at the mouth.
cues.en: DELIEUVIN: Just look at the mouth.
cues.zh: DELIEUVIN：只要看看嘴巴就知道了。

cues.text: Look at the eyes.
cues.en: Look at the eyes.
cues.zh: 看看眼睛。

cues.text: You can't see lines.
cues.en: You can't see lines.
cues.zh: 你看不到線條。

cues.text: You just see the movement of the light.
cues.en: You just see the movement of the light.
cues.zh: 你只看到光的移動。

cues.text: That's incredible, and there is no comparison with other artists at that time.
cues.en: That's incredible, and there is no comparison with other artists at that time.
cues.zh: 這太不可思議了，與當時的其他藝術家無法相比。

cues.text: KEMP: There's no edge there at all.
cues.en: KEMP: There's no edge there at all.
cues.zh: KEMP：根本沒有優勢。

cues.text: It's all very uncertain.
cues.en: It's all very uncertain.
cues.zh: 這一切都非常不確定。

cues.text: This plays a psychological role, of course, because she is present but somehow not tangible.
cues.en: This plays a psychological role, of course, because she is present but somehow not tangible.
cues.zh: 當然，這起到了心理作用，因為她雖然在場，但不知怎麼的卻是無形的。

cues.text: She is idealized.
cues.en: She is idealized.
cues.zh: 她是理想化的。

cues.text: NARRATOR: For Leonardo, sfumato captured in two dimensions
cues.en: NARRATOR: For Leonardo, sfumato captured in two dimensions
cues.zh: 旁白：對李奧納多來說，在二維中捕捉暈染法

cues.text: what he observed in the three-dimensional world.
cues.en: what he observed in the three-dimensional world.
cues.zh: 他在三維世界中觀察到的東西。

cues.text: But in order to get the skin just right, he had to go deeper--
cues.en: But in order to get the skin just right, he had to go deeper--
cues.zh: 但為了讓肌膚恰到好處，他必須深入──

cues.text: to the muscles and tendons below.
cues.en: to the muscles and tendons below.
cues.zh: 到下面的肌肉和肌腱。

cues.text: Hold it like that.
cues.en: Hold it like that.
cues.zh: 就這樣握著吧。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Trudy Van Houten has taught anatomy for 30 years.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Trudy Van Houten has taught anatomy for 30 years.
cues.zh: 旁白：Trudy Van Houten 教授解剖學已有 30 年。

cues.text: Perfect.
cues.en: Perfect.
cues.zh: 完美的。

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Leonardo da Vinci constantly inspires me.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Leonardo da Vinci constantly inspires me.
cues.zh: VAN HOUTEN：達文西不斷地激勵我。

cues.text: NARRATOR: She says the science of anatomy is beautiful.
cues.en: NARRATOR: She says the science of anatomy is beautiful.
cues.zh: 旁白：她說解剖學是美麗的。

cues.text: SYLVAIN: Would you like me to cut that?
cues.en: SYLVAIN: Would you like me to cut that?
cues.zh: 西爾文：你想讓我把它剪掉嗎？

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Yes, please.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Yes, please.
cues.zh: 範·豪頓： 好的，請講。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Though the process often is not.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Though the process often is not.
cues.zh: 旁白：雖然這個過程常常不是這樣。

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: Nice.
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: Nice.
cues.zh: 範豪頓： 很好。

cues.text: You've beautifully preserved that tiny little vessel.
cues.en: You've beautifully preserved that tiny little vessel.
cues.zh: 你把那個小小的容器儲存得很好。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo dissected 30 bodies.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo dissected 30 bodies.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多解剖了 30 具屍體。

cues.text: And with no refrigeration, it would have been especially unpleasant.
cues.en: And with no refrigeration, it would have been especially unpleasant.
cues.zh: 如果沒有冰箱，那就特別不愉快。

cues.text: The intestines would've been a particular problem because they contain a lot of bacteria.
cues.en: The intestines would've been a particular problem because they contain a lot of bacteria.
cues.zh: 腸道可能是一個特別的問題，因為它們含有大量細菌。

cues.text: And even after death, the intestines become inflated, and larger and larger.
cues.en: And even after death, the intestines become inflated, and larger and larger.
cues.zh: 即使在死後，腸子也會變得膨脹，而且越來越大。

cues.text: That's where things were going to go bad quickest, and smell the worst.
cues.en: That's where things were going to go bad quickest, and smell the worst.
cues.zh: 那是事情變壞最快、氣味最難聞的地方。

cues.text: It's a very messy business.
cues.en: It's a very messy business.
cues.zh: 這是一件非常混亂的事情。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Many of the drawings from Leonardo's messy dissections
cues.en: NARRATOR: Many of the drawings from Leonardo's messy dissections
cues.zh: 旁白：許多圖畫來自李奧納多凌亂的解剖

cues.text: today live on in the most refined of places: Windsor Castle,
cues.en: today live on in the most refined of places: Windsor Castle,
cues.zh: 今天生活在最精緻的地方：溫莎城堡，

cues.text: just outside of London.
cues.en: just outside of London.
cues.zh: 就在倫敦郊區。

cues.text: Steps away from where Prince Harry and Meghan Markle posed for their wedding photos,
cues.en: Steps away from where Prince Harry and Meghan Markle posed for their wedding photos,
cues.zh: 距離哈利王子和梅根馬克爾拍婚紗照的地方僅幾步之遙，

cues.text: more than 200 Leonardo drawings are secured in the Print Room.
cues.en: more than 200 Leonardo drawings are secured in the Print Room.
cues.zh: 印刷室儲存著 200 多幅列奧納多的畫作。

cues.text: Martin Clayton is the curator of those drawings.
cues.en: Martin Clayton is the curator of those drawings.
cues.zh: 馬丁·克萊頓是這些畫作的策展人。

cues.text: CLAYTON: He couldn't help himself making a beautiful drawing.
cues.en: CLAYTON: He couldn't help himself making a beautiful drawing.
cues.zh: 克萊頓：他情不自禁地畫出了一幅美麗的圖畫。

cues.text: But what most interested Leonardo was the structure, the machinery of the body.
cues.en: But what most interested Leonardo was the structure, the machinery of the body.
cues.zh: 但李奧納多最感興趣的是身體的結構和機械。

cues.text: And this particular drawing is one of the finest examples
cues.en: And this particular drawing is one of the finest examples
cues.zh: 這幅特別的圖畫是最好的例子之一

cues.text: of Leonardo trying to understand how the shoulder works purely in mechanical terms.
cues.en: of Leonardo trying to understand how the shoulder works purely in mechanical terms.
cues.zh: 列奧納多試圖純粹從機械角度理解肩膀是如何運作的。

cues.text: There's no mystery of the body.
cues.en: There's no mystery of the body.
cues.zh: 身體並沒有什麼神秘之處。

cues.text: The body is a machine that can be looked at and analyzed in purely objective terms.
cues.en: The body is a machine that can be looked at and analyzed in purely objective terms.
cues.zh: 身體是一臺可以純粹客觀地觀察和分析的機器。

cues.text: NARRATOR: The beauty of Leonardo's drawings is undeniable.
cues.en: NARRATOR: The beauty of Leonardo's drawings is undeniable.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多繪畫的美麗是不可否認的。

cues.text: But in light of all that we've learned with the help of tools like the MRI,
cues.en: But in light of all that we've learned with the help of tools like the MRI,
cues.zh: 但鑑於我們在 MRI 等工具的幫助下所瞭解的一切，

cues.text: did he get it right?
cues.en: did he get it right?
cues.zh: 他做對了嗎？

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: If I were asked to grade his anatomical drawings,
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: If I were asked to grade his anatomical drawings,
cues.zh: VAN HOUTEN：如果我被要求對他的解剖圖進行評分，

cues.text: they would go from A to F.
cues.en: they would go from A to F.
cues.zh: 他們會從A到F。

cues.text: His drawing of the muscles, of things that he was directly observing
cues.en: His drawing of the muscles, of things that he was directly observing
cues.zh: 他畫的肌肉和他直接觀察到的事物

cues.text: and giving functional sense to, those I would give an A-plus.
cues.en: and giving functional sense to, those I would give an A-plus.
cues.zh: 並賦予功能意義，我會給這些人A+。

cues.text: In terms of some of the organs, I could not do so.
cues.en: In terms of some of the organs, I could not do so.
cues.zh: 有的器官我做不到。

cues.text: NARRATOR: One of Leonardo's most ambitious anatomical drawings is called the "Great Lady."
cues.en: NARRATOR: One of Leonardo's most ambitious anatomical drawings is called the "Great Lady."
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多最雄心勃勃的解剖圖之一被稱為「偉大的女士」。

cues.text: It is considered a masterpiece, but for Van Houten, it's a bit of a mess.
cues.en: It is considered a masterpiece, but for Van Houten, it's a bit of a mess.
cues.zh: 它被認為是一部傑作，但對於 Van Houten 來說，它有點混亂。

cues.text: VAN HOUTEN: The feature I went to right away are strange structures
cues.en: VAN HOUTEN: The feature I went to right away are strange structures
cues.zh: VAN HOUTEN：我立即訪問的功能是奇怪的結構

cues.text: flying out from the sides of the uterus.
cues.en: flying out from the sides of the uterus.
cues.zh: 從子宮兩側飛出。

cues.text: They reminded me of carrots with tops.
cues.en: They reminded me of carrots with tops.
cues.zh: 它們讓我想起了有頂的胡蘿蔔。

cues.text: CLAYTON: These strange sort of horn-like structures are ligaments observed by Leonardo in a cow.
cues.en: CLAYTON: These strange sort of horn-like structures are ligaments observed by Leonardo in a cow.
cues.zh: 克萊頓：這些奇怪的角狀結構是達文西在牛身上觀察到的韌帶。

cues.text: Leonardo assumed that all mammals have the same structures.
cues.en: Leonardo assumed that all mammals have the same structures.
cues.zh: 列奧納多假設所有哺乳動物都具有相同的結構。

cues.text: He's sort of feeling his way into a field that had never been illustrated before.
cues.en: He's sort of feeling his way into a field that had never been illustrated before.
cues.zh: 他正在摸索著進入一個從未被描​​繪過的領域。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo's ground-breaking dissections certainly informed his art.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo's ground-breaking dissections certainly informed his art.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多開創性的解剖無疑為他的藝術帶來了啟發。

cues.text: ♪ He returned to this painting, "Saint Jerome," after 20 years,
cues.en: ♪ He returned to this painting, "Saint Jerome," after 20 years,
cues.zh: ♪ 20年後他又回到了這幅畫《聖傑羅姆》，

cues.text: revising the neck to accurately portray the muscle beneath.
cues.en: revising the neck to accurately portray the muscle beneath.
cues.zh: 修改頸部以準確描繪下方的肌肉。

cues.text: He did not revisit one of his earliest paintings, "Ginevra de' Benci,"
cues.en: He did not revisit one of his earliest paintings, "Ginevra de' Benci,"
cues.zh: 他沒有重溫他最早的畫作之一“Ginevra de' Benci”

cues.text: and it shows in what has been called the flatness of her face.
cues.en: and it shows in what has been called the flatness of her face.
cues.zh: 這體現在她所謂的扁平臉上。

cues.text: But by the time of the "Mona Lisa," Leonardo's knowledge of anatomy is beautifully convincing.
cues.en: But by the time of the "Mona Lisa," Leonardo's knowledge of anatomy is beautifully convincing.
cues.zh: 但到了《蒙娜麗莎》的時代，李奧納多的解剖學知識已經非常令人信服了。

cues.text: One intriguing page of Leonardo's notebooks shows several illustrations of human lips
cues.en: One intriguing page of Leonardo's notebooks shows several illustrations of human lips
cues.zh: 列奧納多筆記本中有趣的一頁展示了幾張人類嘴唇的插圖

cues.text: in exaggerated expressions, done from dissections.
cues.en: in exaggerated expressions, done from dissections.
cues.zh: 以誇張的表達方式，透過解剖完成。

cues.text: ISAACSON: And it shows how each muscle and each nerve affects the lips,
cues.en: ISAACSON: And it shows how each muscle and each nerve affects the lips,
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：它顯示了每塊肌肉和每條神經如何影響嘴唇，

cues.text: and at the very top is this tiny faint sketch,
cues.en: and at the very top is this tiny faint sketch,
cues.zh: 最上面是這個微弱的小草圖，

cues.text: and you see the first sketch of what will be the smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.en: and you see the first sketch of what will be the smile of the "Mona Lisa."
cues.zh: 你會看到「蒙娜麗莎」微笑的第一幅草圖。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Anatomy and his painting technique explain in part how Leonardo infused the "Mona Lisa"
cues.en: NARRATOR: Anatomy and his painting technique explain in part how Leonardo infused the "Mona Lisa"
cues.zh: 旁白：解剖學和他的繪畫技巧部分解釋了列奧納多如何注入“蒙娜麗莎”

cues.text: with a lifelike quality.
cues.en: with a lifelike quality.
cues.zh: 具有栩栩如生的品質。

cues.text: But to complete the illusion, he needed to explore another area of science:
cues.en: But to complete the illusion, he needed to explore another area of science:
cues.zh: 但為了完成這個幻想，他需要探索另一個科學領域：

cues.text: how humans see.
cues.en: how humans see.
cues.zh: 人類如何看待。

cues.text: GALLUZZI: Among the many aspects in which Leonardo
cues.en: GALLUZZI: Among the many aspects in which Leonardo
cues.zh: 加魯齊：在萊昂納多的許多方面

cues.text: was using his knowledge as a scientist to become a better painter
cues.en: was using his knowledge as a scientist to become a better painter
cues.zh: 正在利用他作為科學家的知識成為更好的畫家

cues.text: is optics.
cues.en: is optics.
cues.zh: 是光學。

cues.text: And optics is called by Leonardo "perspectiva"-- perspective.
cues.en: And optics is called by Leonardo "perspectiva"-- perspective.
cues.zh: 列奧納多將光學稱為“perspectiva”——透視。

cues.text: FARGES: It's basic geometry, because when you have an object with parallel lines,
cues.en: FARGES: It's basic geometry, because when you have an object with parallel lines,
cues.zh: FARGES：這是基本幾何學，因為當你有一個具有平行線的物體時，

cues.text: they will seem to vanish into a point,
cues.en: they will seem to vanish into a point,
cues.zh: 它們似乎會消失成一個點，

cues.text: which is called the vanishing point.
cues.en: which is called the vanishing point.
cues.zh: 這就是所謂的消失點。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Leonardo was fascinated by many aspects of how we perceive our world.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Leonardo was fascinated by many aspects of how we perceive our world.
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多對我們如何看待世界的許多面向著迷。

cues.text: He even studied the composition of air to determine how atmosphere affects
cues.en: He even studied the composition of air to determine how atmosphere affects
cues.zh: 他甚至研究了空氣的成分，以確定大氣如何影響

cues.text: the appearance of objects in the distance.
cues.en: the appearance of objects in the distance.
cues.zh: 遠處物體的出現。

cues.text: Leonardo is trying to capture the complexity of the world.
cues.en: Leonardo is trying to capture the complexity of the world.
cues.zh: 萊昂納多試圖捕捉世界的複雜性。

cues.text: But how can you paint something that you cannot see,
cues.en: But how can you paint something that you cannot see,
cues.zh: 但你怎麼能畫出你看不到的東西，

cues.text: like the transparency of air?
cues.en: like the transparency of air?
cues.zh: 就像空氣的透明度一樣？

cues.text: ISAACSON: Leonardo not only looked at mathematical perspective, but he looked at how colors change as you get further away,
cues.en: ISAACSON: Leonardo not only looked at mathematical perspective, but he looked at how colors change as you get further away,
cues.zh: 艾薩克森：李奧納多不僅著眼於數學角度，而且還著眼於隨著距離越來越遠顏色如何變化，

cues.text: how the sharpness of something changes as you get further away from it.
cues.en: how the sharpness of something changes as you get further away from it.
cues.zh: 當你遠離某物時，它的清晰度如何變化。

cues.text: NARRATOR: And did Leonardo also discover tricks of perception
cues.en: NARRATOR: And did Leonardo also discover tricks of perception
cues.zh: 旁白：李奧納多是否也發現了感知的技巧？

cues.text: to pull off the greatest illusion of all: that elusive smile?
cues.en: to pull off the greatest illusion of all: that elusive smile?
cues.zh: 實現最大的幻想：那難以捉摸的微笑？

cues.text: She's looking out, and her smile is a reaction
cues.en: She's looking out, and her smile is a reaction
cues.zh: 她向外看，她的微笑是一種反應

cues.text: triggered by the arrival of somebody.
cues.en: triggered by the arrival of somebody.
cues.zh: 由某人的到來觸發。

cues.text: This is the fiction that the painting tries to establish.
cues.en: This is the fiction that the painting tries to establish.
cues.zh: 這就是這幅畫試圖建立的虛構。

cues.text: The great artists know how to draw you in,
cues.en: The great artists know how to draw you in,
cues.zh: 偉大的藝術家知道如何吸引你，

cues.text: but not to tell you what to think.
cues.en: but not to tell you what to think.
cues.zh: 但不是告訴你該怎麼想。

cues.text: They offer the tease.
cues.en: They offer the tease.
cues.zh: 他們提供戲弄。

cues.text: NARRATOR: The ambiguity of Mona Lisa's smile is indeed part of her allure.
cues.en: NARRATOR: The ambiguity of Mona Lisa's smile is indeed part of her allure.
cues.zh: 旁白：蒙娜麗莎微笑中的曖昧確實是她魅力的一部分。

cues.text: How did Leonardo pull that effect off?
cues.en: How did Leonardo pull that effect off?
cues.zh: 萊昂納多是如何實現這種效果的呢？

cues.text: That is a question that intrigued neurophysiologist Margaret Livingstone.
cues.en: That is a question that intrigued neurophysiologist Margaret Livingstone.
cues.zh: 這是神經生理學家瑪格麗特·利文斯頓感興趣的問題。

cues.text: She studies the human visual system: how our eyes and brain operate together
cues.en: She studies the human visual system: how our eyes and brain operate together
cues.zh: 她研究人類視覺系統：我們的眼睛和大腦如何協同運作

cues.text: to make sense of the world.
cues.en: to make sense of the world.
cues.zh: 去理解世界。

cues.text: LIVINGSTONE: As a neurophysiologist, I actually learn a lot from artists,
cues.en: LIVINGSTONE: As a neurophysiologist, I actually learn a lot from artists,
cues.zh: LIVINGSTONE：作為一名神經生理學家，我實際上從藝術家那裡學到了很多東西，

cues.text: because they study how we see.
cues.en: because they study how we see.
cues.zh: 因為他們研究我們如何看待。

cues.text: I study how we see.
cues.en: I study how we see.
cues.zh: 我研究我們如何看待。

cues.text: A lot of good art takes advantage of the computations your brain makes
cues.en: A lot of good art takes advantage of the computations your brain makes
cues.zh: 許多優秀的藝術作品都運用了你大腦的運算能力

cues.text: by exaggerating things that your visual system finds important.
cues.en: by exaggerating things that your visual system finds important.
cues.zh: 透過誇大你的視覺系統認為重要的事情。

cues.text: NARRATOR: Human vision is among the best in the animal kingdom.
cues.en: NARRATOR: Human vision is among the best in the animal kingdom.
cues.zh: 旁白：人類的視力是動物界中最好的。

cues.text: The center of our retina is packed with special photoreceptors
cues.en: The center of our retina is packed with special photoreceptors
cues.zh: 我們視網膜的中心充滿了特殊的感光器

cues.text: that enable us to see details, or sharpness.
cues.en: that enable us to see details, or sharpness.
cues.zh: 使我們能夠看到細節或清晰度。

cues.text: But away from the center-- toward the periphery-- there are fewer of those types of receptors.
cues.en: But away from the center-- toward the periphery-- there are fewer of those types of receptors.
cues.zh: 但遠離中心——朝向外圍——這類受體的數量較少。

cues.text: We can see movement, but not detail.
cues.en: We can see movement, but not detail.
cues.zh: 我們可以看到運動，但看不到細節。

cues.text: LIVINGSTONE: Okay, now I want you to close your eyes.
cues.en: LIVINGSTONE: Okay, now I want you to close your eyes.
cues.zh: 利文斯頓：好的，現在我要你閉上眼睛。

cues.text: I'm going to put up two version of the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.en: I'm going to put up two version of the "Mona Lisa,"
cues.zh: 我要放兩個版本的《蒙娜麗莎》

cues.text: one accurate and one distorted.
cues.en: one accurate and one distorted.
cues.zh: 一種是準確的，一種是扭曲的。

cues.text: NARRATOR: To illustrate, Livingstone enlists her colleague Peter
cues.en: NARRATOR: To illustrate, Livingstone enlists her colleague Peter
cues.zh: 旁白：為了說明這一點，利文斯頓邀請了她的同事彼得

cues.text: to see if he can spot a fake "Mona Lisa"
cues.en: to see if he can spot a fake "Mona Lisa"
cues.zh: 看看他是否能認出一幅贗品《蒙娜麗莎》

cues.text: using just his peripheral vision.
cues.en: using just his peripheral vision.
cues.zh: 僅使用他的餘光。

cues.text: Okay, briefly open your eyes and look at the yellow spot, then close them right away.
cues.en: Okay, briefly open your eyes and look at the yellow spot, then close them right away.
cues.zh: 好的，短暫地睜開眼睛，看看黃色的點，然後立即閉上眼睛。

cues.text: And point to which is the accurate reproduction.
cues.en: And point to which is the accurate reproduction.
cues.zh: 並指出哪一個是準確的再現。

cues.text: Open your eyes and see whether you chose the correct one.
cues.en: Open your eyes and see whether you chose the correct one.
cues.zh: 睜大眼睛看看你是否選擇了正確的。

cues.text: LIVINGSTONE: Point at the real version.
cues.en: LIVINGSTONE: Point at the real version.
